$description: Every AntFabric UI component as data, for an agent that has to use one or build one. Written by `pnpm tokens:build` (apps/catalogue/scripts/agent-surface.ts) from the docs in packages/docs/src/components/<category>/<id>.ts and the recipes in packages/core/src/recipes/<category>/<id>.ts; `pnpm check agent` fails when it is stale. Served at /components.json. Per component: `props` (as the docs declare them, the contract both kits implement: `type`, `default` (the kit's own), `sample` (the catalogue's example value, AntFabric's showcase, where it has one), `options`, `required`, `platforms` when not all, and for an event its `args` and the prop it `changes`), `parts` and `recipe` (each part's `$token` references by variant, state and platform, in the order they apply; later wins: base, then variants in the order listed, then states, then the platform; `tokens` lists every one), `a11y`, `examples` (prop objects; `slots` names a prop that held a drawing, left out), `platforms` (what each kit builds on, import line, notes, keyboard, gestures), `related`, and `files`: the paths in the repository (`null` where that kit has no file because the component is not on that platform). Tokens are in packages/core/tokens.json. Props, the recipe and its keys are in AUTHORING.md.

agent-steps.name: Agent steps
agent-steps.description: The tools an agent has run this turn, newest last: a pulsing dot while one runs, a tick when it is done, a cross when it failed, each with where it ran. Past the cap the oldest are counted, never dropped silently.

steps.description: Every step this turn has taken, oldest first: a key, the label a person reads ("Recent messages", not recent_messages), where it ran when there is somewhere worth naming (an MCP server, a plugin), and running, done or failed.

max.description: How many of the newest steps to draw; the rest become "+N earlier". 0 is the platform's own: 5 on web and desktop, 3 on the phone.

notes: A list named Steps; "+N earlier" is its first item. Web: a step's marker is an image named running, done or failed. Phone: each step is one stop, "running: Draft email via Gmail", and its marker is hidden.
A long label or source is cut to one line with its full text as the tooltip (web).
Labels and sources are printed as text, never Markdown.

examples.name: More than fit
examples.description: Thirteen steps: the newest are drawn, the rest counted.

edgeCases.title: A long label
edgeCases.handling: The label truncates to one line; the source keeps its place after it.

edgeCases.title: No source
edgeCases.handling: A tool with no source worth naming (an agent's own) has none; the row ends at the label. Nothing says "via" with nothing after it.

edgeCases.title: No steps yet
edgeCases.handling: Draws nothing. While an agent is only thinking, the thinking indicator stands alone.

web.base: A role=list of rows drawn from its recipe; the running dot on the kit's af-step-pulse, rows rise in

desktop.base: The same list, inside the thinking indicator's fold
notes: Today it is drawn only inside the thinking indicator, not on its own.

mobile.base: Views and Texts drawn from the same recipe; the dot pulses with Animated on the native driver and holds still under Reduce Motion; rows fade in
notes: The phone keeps three rows, the desktop five: a phone has less height to give a turn in flight.
Rows sit 4pt apart against the desktop's 6.

app-badge.name: App badge
app-badge.description: The unread count outside the app: the macOS Dock badge, the Windows taskbar overlay, the Linux launcher count, the browser tab title and favicon dot, and the iPhone and Android home-screen badge. One server-owned total, drawn the way each OS draws it.

appName.description: The app's name: the tab's title and what the OS reads the icon as. Its first letter is the icon's mark when there is no `mark`.

mark.description: The app icon's vector mark (`{ viewBox, paths }`), drawn at the icon's size in the colour the OS draws it in. Left out, the first letter of `appName`.

otherTab.description: The neighbouring browser tab in the web picture. "" draws none.

count.description: Unread mentions and DMs — the person's whole total, never one window's. 0 clears the badge.

dot.description: Activity without a mention (new messages in channels you follow). Drawn where the OS has a dot; ignored where it only has numbers.

mutedAll.description: Notifications are paused. Counts still show — they are facts, not interruptions — but the activity dot is dropped and, where we draw the badge ourselves, it turns grey.

a11y.label: 3 unread mentions and direct messages
notes: The OS announces its own badge (VoiceOver reads "AntFabric, 3 notifications"). The tab title count is what a screen reader hears when it lists tabs.

edgeCases.title: Zero
edgeCases.handling: Zero removes the badge everywhere: setBadgeCount(undefined) on desktop, setBadgeCountAsync(0) on the phone, the bare title "AntFabric" and the plain favicon on the web. Never an empty red dot, never "(0)".

edgeCases.title: Huge counts
edgeCases.handling: macOS and the tab title read "99+" (setBadgeLabel, since setBadgeCount takes only a number); the Windows overlay reads "9+" because it is 16 px; iOS and Android are given the real number and draw what they draw.

edgeCases.title: Read on another device, or signed out
edgeCases.handling: One read-state event clears the Dock, the taskbar, every tab's title and the phone's icon; a killed phone is corrected by the next push's aps.badge, or by a silent push when nothing new arrived. Signing out clears the badge first, so the next person never inherits a count.

edgeCases.title: Windows hides it
edgeCases.handling: Small taskbar buttons (Windows 10) and "Show badges on taskbar apps" off (Windows 11) both hide overlay icons, and a pinned-but-closed app has no overlay at all. The toast and Action Center count carry the signal; nothing may rely on the overlay being seen.

edgeCases.title: Linux without a launcher API
edgeCases.handling: Ubuntu Dock, Dash to Dock and KDE's task manager read the Unity LauncherEntry count; stock GNOME without a dock extension, and most tiling setups, show nothing. The tray icon and notifications are the signal there.

edgeCases.title: Paused notifications
edgeCases.handling: The count of mentions and DMs keeps showing — pausing stops interruptions, it does not hide what is waiting. The activity dot is dropped, and where we draw the badge (Windows overlay, favicon dot, Linux count) it goes grey. The OS-drawn red badges on macOS and iOS cannot change colour, so they stay red.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode and the favicon
edgeCases.handling: The generated Windows overlay and the canvas favicon are drawn per theme, with a ring in the taskbar or tab-strip colour so the dot reads on light and dark. The favicon listens to prefers-color-scheme, not the app theme, because the browser chrome follows the OS.

web.base: A drawing of the browser's tab strip: `<div role="img">`, inline styles over `t`, the favicon dot pops in with enter("pop"). What the app sets is document.title ("(3) AntFabric") and a canvas-drawn favicon on <link rel="icon">, plus navigator.setAppBadge(n) when installed as an app (Chrome, Edge, Safari web apps).
notes: The title count is mentions and DMs; the favicon dot is drawn for any unread. Both update in a background tab — that is when they matter.
Every open tab shows the same number: the count is server-owned and each tab applies the same read-state event.
A pinned tab shows no title at all, so in a pinned tab the favicon dot is the only signal.

desktop.base: A drawing of the macOS Dock, the Windows taskbar or a Linux launcher, picked by usePlatform().os: `<div role="img">`, inline styles over `t`, the badge pops in with enter("pop"). What the app calls is Tauri getCurrentWindow().setBadgeCount() (macOS Dock, Linux launcher), setBadgeLabel() on macOS for "99+" and "•", setOverlayIcon() on Windows.
notes: 0 clears the badge with setBadgeCount(undefined) — never setBadgeCount(0), which can leave an empty red dot on macOS (ADR-0354: a badge nobody can clear is never raised).
The count is clamped and NaN-proofed, and written only when it changes, to save an IPC round trip per event.
Needs core:window:allow-set-badge-count in src-tauri/capabilities/default.json; without it the call is refused silently and no badge ever appears.
Gap: Windows is unsupported by setBadgeCount. The overlay is a 16 px icon generated per count (1–9, then 9+) and per theme, passed to setOverlayIcon; until that lands Windows shows no badge.
macOS: the Dock bounce (requestUserAttention) is for a DM or mention only, once, and never while notifications are paused.

mobile.base: A drawing of the home-screen icon: a View with accessibilityRole "image", StyleSheet over useTheme() tokens, the wallpaper gradient through experimental_backgroundImage, the badge or dot popping in with <Enter motion="pop">. What the app calls is expo-notifications setBadgeCountAsync; APNs aps.badge set by notification-service keeps the number right while the app is killed.
notes: iOS draws a number only (no dot); Android launchers draw a dot from the notifications in the tray (Samsung One UI draws the number), and long-press shows "3 notifications".
In the catalogue the badge (not the icon) pops in when it first appears and on Replay, as the system badge does when a count arrives.
After a Reply or Mark as read from the notification, the count is re-read (unreadCount → setBadgeCount) so the icon matches what is left.

flows.title: A mention puts a number on the icon, and reading it takes it off

app-menu-bar.name: Application menu
app-menu-bar.description: Where the app's own commands live. On macOS it is the system menu bar at the top of the screen; on Windows and Linux it hangs off the ☰ button in the title bar; in a browser tab it is a small ⋯ menu holding only what makes sense in a tab — never Reload, Zoom or Quit, which the browser owns.

menus.description: { key, label, items? } for each menu, left to right. The first is the app menu on macOS and names the bar; Windows and Linux skip it and carry About and Quit under Help and File instead. Each menu's `items` are MenuItem rows (`shortcut`, `type: "separator"`, `checked`, `disabled`, a `submenu` drawn only as its chevron) plus `os`.

openMenu.description: The key of the menu drawn open. Empty closes it on macOS and Windows; on Linux it shows the popover's main list of menus.

highlight.description: The key (else the label) of the entry under the pointer or keyboard focus, for a static snapshot.

workspace.description: Names the web menu and its ⋯ trigger. Empty draws no header row.

host.description: Under the workspace name in the header.

workspaceIdentity.description: The workspace tile's colour in the header.

webItems.description: The web menu: MenuItem rows ({ icon, label, shortcut?, webShortcut?, disabled? }) with `trailingIcon?`, { type: "scheme" } for the Light / Dark / System row, or { type: "separator" }.

clock.description: The macOS picture's clock, at the right of the bar. Empty draws none.

onSelect.description: A desktop entry (which also closes the menu) or a web ⋯ entry was chosen. Disabled entries never fire it.

onOpenMenuChange.description: A menu title (macOS bar, Windows ☰ row, Linux main list) or the Linux back row was pressed, or an entry was chosen: the menu now open, or empty.

onColorSchemeChange.description: Light, Dark or System was pressed in the Theme row. The menu stays open.

notes: The macOS bar in the catalogue is a picture of the system's own menu bar; the real one is native and VoiceOver reads it as such.

The macOS bar is a role=menubar with one tab stop: Left and Right move along its titles (and open the neighbour while a menu is open), Down or Up opens a menu and focuses its first or last entry, Escape closes it and returns focus to its title.

Inside a menu Up, Down, Home, End and typing a letter move between entries, Left and Right go to the neighbouring menu, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the entry that opened it. The Windows ☰ panel and GNOME popover use the same keys; Right opens an entry's flyout, Left or Escape closes it.

The web ⋯ menu is a picture of an open menu (the app owns opening it), so it has no Escape of its own. Its entries take Up, Down, Home, End and typing; the Theme row is a radiogroup that is one stop in that order: Left, Right, Up and Down inside it move between Light, Dark and System and check the option they reach, and Tab leaves it.
Disabled items stay in the menu and are announced as dimmed — a command that vanishes is harder to find again than one that is greyed.
Every entry draws a focus ring. A long menu scrolls inside the window (80% of its height) instead of running off it.

edgeCases.title: The browser owns Reload, Zoom and Quit
edgeCases.handling: The web menu never lists them. ⌘R in a tab reloads the page: drafts are already in IndexedDB (saved as you type), and only a send still in flight raises the browser's 'Leave site?' prompt. ⌘+ / ⌘- are the browser's zoom and the layout reflows; the app never intercepts them.

edgeCases.title: Zoom at its limits
edgeCases.handling: At 200% Zoom In is greyed, at 50% Zoom Out is greyed, and Actual Size is greyed at 100%. Today the items stay enabled and the step pins at the end stop, which reads as a broken shortcut; the spec greys them so the menu says why nothing happened.

edgeCases.title: Clicked and pressed: still once
edgeCases.handling: WebKit hands ⌘R to the page first; the shortcut registry prevents it, so the keyboard path is the registry's and the menu accelerator is only a label. Clicking the item runs the menu handler. Each path fires exactly once — never a refresh and a reload together.

edgeCases.title: A page too broken to listen
edgeCases.handling: Force Reload is native on every OS. On macOS that is the system menu bar. On Windows and Linux the ☰ is drawn by the page, so the hidden native menu keeps Ctrl+Shift+R alive and the tray menu offers 'Reload window' as a mouse path that never touches the webview.

edgeCases.title: Window closed to the tray
edgeCases.handling: macOS keeps the app active with no window: View and History items are greyed (there is nothing to reload or zoom), Window › AntFabric and a Dock click bring the window back (ADR-0811). On Windows and Linux there is no menu while the window is hidden; the tray menu is the way back.

edgeCases.title: Report a Problem in a build without a report service
edgeCases.handling: The item is always there — hiding a command that every runbook screenshots is worse. Choosing it opens a dialog that says reporting is not available in this build and offers to copy diagnostics instead.

edgeCases.title: Desktop app may not be installed
edgeCases.handling: Chrome and Edge drop an unknown antfabric:// link silently: if the page still has focus 1.5 s later, the menu's next open puts 'Download the desktop app' first. Safari shows its own 'cannot open the page' sheet, so on Safari 'Open in desktop app' appears only after one open has succeeded on this browser (remembered locally).

edgeCases.title: Signed out or SSO expired
edgeCases.handling: The menu leads with 'Sign in again'; Preferences is disabled because it needs the account. Theme and Help still work signed out.

edgeCases.title: A long workspace name
edgeCases.handling: The header truncates to one line with an ellipsis; the full name is the menu's accessible name and the trigger's tooltip.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard-only and right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: Every menu opens and walks from the keyboard (Alt / F10 on Windows and Linux, Ctrl+F2 on macOS, Enter on ⋯ in a browser). In right-to-left languages the Windows cascade opens to the left and shortcuts sit at the start of the row.

edgeCases.title: Liquid Glass and earlier macOS
edgeCases.handling: macOS draws the menu bar, so its look follows the Mac's version: transparent bar and glass menus on 26+, vibrancy before. Our items, order and shortcuts are the same on both.

edgeCases.title: The Mac's Liquid Glass settings
edgeCases.handling: macOS draws the menu bar and its menus, so Clear or Tinted, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast apply by themselves. Our items and shortcuts don't change.

web.base: The ⋯ IconButton over a <div role="menu"> that pops in (enter("pop")): an Avatar header, <button role="menuitem"> rows with Kbd hints, and a role="radiogroup" Theme row of <button role="radio"> segments; inline styles over `t`, hover / press / focus from useInteraction, `colorScheme` through useControllable. The kit draws the menu open; opening it from the top bar, Esc and arrow-key movement belong to the menu primitive the app wraps it in.
notes: Deliberately NOT here: Reload, Force Reload, Zoom, Full Screen, Close Window, Quit. The browser owns every one of them and its own shortcuts (⌘R, ⌘+, ⌘W, ⌘Q) reach the browser before the page. Offering them twice teaches people a command that sometimes does something different.
No History menu either: the top bar's Back / Forward are the browser's own history, so a second copy here would be a third place for one command.

'Open in desktop app' fires the antfabric:// deep link for the current location; 'Download the desktop app' opens the download page. Both show whether or not the app is installed — the browser cannot tell — see the edge case.
Help opens the help centre in a new tab (target=_blank, the external-link glyph says so).
The menu pops in from the ⋯; pressing Light, Dark or System sets `colorScheme` and the selected segment moves without closing the menu.

keyboard.action: On the ⋯ button: opens the menu with the first item focused
Moves between items; Home / End jump to the ends; typing a letter jumps to the next item starting with it
Inside the Theme row: moves between Light, Dark and System
Closes the menu and returns focus to ⋯
Preferences, without opening the menu
Keyboard shortcuts, without opening the menu

desktop.base: macOS: a picture of the system menu bar over the wallpaper (role="menubar", <button role="menuitem"> titles, a dropdown that fades in; glass() on macOS 26) — in the app the real bar is Tauri's native Menu. Windows: the ☰ IconButton over a panel that pops in, each menu a row whose cascade fades in beside it. Linux: the same panel as a GNOME popover, the submenu sliding in place (enter("slide-left")) with a ‹ back row. Rows are <button role="menuitem"> with Kbd hints; inline styles over `t`, hover / press / focus from useInteraction, `openMenu` through useControllable.
notes: Today: Tauri's Menu::default (AntFabric, File, Edit, View, Window, Help) with five items prepended into View (view_menu.rs) and Report a Problem… appended to Help (help_menu.rs). On Windows and Linux that default renders as a native menu strip under the native title bar.
New in this spec: a History menu (Back ⌘[, Forward ⌘]) and AntFabric › Settings… ⌘, on macOS; the ☰ menu on Windows and Linux, which needs decorations: false (see title-bar).

⌘R is Reload = the data refresh (refreshWorkspace, ADR-0759) and keeps drafts and scroll; ⌘⇧R is Force Reload = WebviewWindow::reload(). Force Reload is handled in Rust, never in the page, because a page that needs it may not be listening.
Zoom steps through Chromium's eleven stops (50%–200%), is applied to every webview and remembered in settings.json under viewZoom.

Windows/Linux: the native menu stays attached and hidden (window.hide_menu()) so its accelerators — Ctrl+Shift+R above all — still fire when the page is dead. Verify muda keeps the accelerator table after hide_menu on Windows; if it does not, register Force Reload natively.
Linux draws GNOME's popover-menu convention: a submenu slides in place with a ‹ back row instead of cascading sideways.

Pressing a menu title (macOS bar, Windows ☰ cascade) sets `openMenu` and its dropdown fades in; pressing the open title closes it. The ☰ panel pops in. On Linux a menu in the popover's main list slides its submenu in and the ‹ row goes back to the list. Choosing an entry fires onSelect and closes the menu.
Shortcut glyphs come from the menu model, so macOS orders modifiers its own way (⇧⌘R) in the real menu even though the spec writes Mod+Shift+R once.

macOS 26+ (Tahoe): the system menu bar is transparent over the wallpaper and its menus are Liquid Glass — macOS draws both; the app only supplies the items. macOS 15 and earlier: the translucent bar and vibrancy menus. The Windows ☰ menu and the web ⋯ menu are ours and unchanged.

keyboard.action: View › Reload — re-reads the workspace; drafts and scroll positions stay
View › Force Reload — reloads the webview itself
Actual Size / Zoom In / Zoom Out
History › Back / Forward
Help › Report a Problem…
Windows and Linux: opens ☰ with File highlighted; Alt+F, Alt+E, Alt+V, Alt+S (History), Alt+W and Alt+H open a menu by its underlined letter
macOS: moves focus to the system menu bar (when keyboard navigation is on)

mobile.alternative: There is no app menu on a phone. The header photo opens /profile, which holds Preferences, Theme, Help, Report a problem and Sign out. Reload is pull-to-refresh, zoom is the system text size, and quitting is the app switcher.

approval-item.name: Approval item
approval-item.description: One decision routed to a person, from an agent, a plugin or an external ticket (AntFabric's: a Fabric agent, a Zoho Desk ticket, a Jira issue): what is asked, what is at stake, who asked, and Reject or Approve, or Answer when an agent asked a question instead. Decided, it says who decided and whether they confirmed it was them.

source.description: The tag's words: where the decision came from ("Agent", "Purchase orders", "Jira"). A plugin passes its own display name. Empty draws no tag.

agent.description: An agent proposed it: the tag takes the brand tone. The kit never decides who counts as an agent; the product sets it.

reference.description: The source's own id, drawn beside the tag whenever it is given: PO-4821, DESK-4821, PROJ-217.

subject.description: What is being asked, in a line. It names the card.
subject.sample: Send renewal proposal to Acme Corp

context.description: Why it is asked. Two lines at most here; the rest is on the approval itself.
context.sample: The sales agent drafted a renewal at this year's seat count with a 6% uplift.

amount.description: What is at stake, written as the source writes it.

requestedBy.description: Who asked: the agent's name, or the person who raised the ticket.

time.description: When it was asked, already formatted for the person.

status.description: pending and question need the person (the coral dot). approved and rejected are settled and lose their actions. expired is a request nobody decided in time; failed is a decision that could not be committed, and offers Retry.

decidedBy.description: Who decided, once it is decided: "You" for the person reading.

verify.description: Pending: approving asks the person to confirm it is them first (a passkey, a second factor, a fingerprint). Decided: the decision was confirmed that way.

deciding.description: A decision is on its way (the identity check, then the write-back): Approve spins and Reject waits.

expanded.description: The context is shown in full instead of clamped to two lines. A button under a long context (over about two lines) flips it.

onRetry.description: Retry was pressed on a failed decision: the app commits it again.

onApprove.description: The app runs the identity check when verify is on, commits the decision and writes it back to the source (a ticket, a plugin) as the person.

onAnswer.description: An agent's question: the app opens it to be answered.

notes: Each card is an article named by its subject (web); on the phone the buttons are the stops.
The buttons are named with the subject, starting with the visible word: "Approve: Send renewal proposal". `deciding` sets aria-busy on the card and on Approve.

Deciding removes the buttons: focus moves to the outcome line (a card that arrives decided does not take focus) and the outcome is announced ("Send renewal proposal: Approved by You"; assertive when the decision failed).
A long context can be expanded (a button with aria-expanded). The coral dot is an image named "Needs you".
Reject is a full button beside Approve, never a quiet link: refusing is as easy as agreeing.

edgeCases.handling: The decision is committed either way. The app shows the failure where the card sits (an inline banner) and retries the write-back; the card does not go back to pending.

edgeCases.title: The identity check is cancelled

notes: There is no approvals screen on any platform yet; this is a proposal from the phone's data model.

notes: The desktop has no approvals list today; its only approval is the question panel's gated tool call.

attachment-card.name: Attachment card
attachment-card.description: What a message carries besides words: a file with its type and size, an image thumbnail, a link preview, or a voice note. Uploading, paused and failed states live on the card itself, and compact is the staged chip inside the composer.

name.description: File name as uploaded. Also the accessible name's subject.

fileType.description: The family, from content type then extension. Picks the badge colours (desktop/web letters) and the glyph (mobile).

badge.description: Up to five letters on the desktop/web badge: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, KEY, ZIP, TS.

typeLabel.description: Human type name for the meta line.

size.description: Formatted size. Empty while the metadata is still loading.

status.description: uploading shows progress; paused is a stalled upload (offline or backgrounded) that resumes on its own; failed offers Retry.

src.description: Image thumbnail, or the link preview's image. A server-rendered thumbnail, never the full file.

description.description: Link preview description (og:description), two lines at most.
description.sample: Freeze on 12 November, staging soak for 48 hours, then the mobile and desktop builds ship together.

waveform.description: Bar heights in px (4–28), sampled to fit the width. Drawn, never announced.

played.description: How many waveform bars have played; those are coral.

compact.description: The staged chip in the composer tray: thumbnail or badge, name, size or progress, and Remove.

removable.description: Link preview only: the sender can remove the preview and keep the link.

onOpen.description: Desktop/web: preview (lightbox or file viewer). Mobile: MediaViewer for images, video and previewable files; Share (iOS) or Save to device (Android) for the rest.

onStatusChange.description: Called with `status` as Retry leaves it (uploading). Given `status` too, the card is controlled; otherwise Retry turns it back to uploading itself.

onRetry.description: Retry was pressed on a failed upload: the app starts it again.

onCancel.description: Cancel an upload in progress, remove a staged file, or remove a link's preview (Remove preview, web and desktop).

notes: File: "Preview Q4-release-checklist.pdf" (desktop/web) or "Q4-release-checklist.pdf, 2.4 MB · PDF. Open" (mobile): the action is part of the name.

While it is not ready the file card's name carries the state, since a button's children are not read: "Q4-release-checklist.pdf, uploading, 64%", "…upload paused at 64%", "…. Upload failed. Check your connection and try again." A progressbar sibling (web) or the stop's value (phone) exposes the percent.
A stall or a failure is announced when it happens (assertive for a failure); the percent is not read on every change.
Image: "Photo, <name>, <size>. Open". Thumbnails are decorative because the label already names them. A waveform is hidden and the play button carries the duration.

props.title: PLAT-2291 Composer drops the draft when the socket reconnects

edgeCases.title: A very long file name
edgeCases.handling: One line. The kit truncates in the middle so the extension survives ("platform-eng-incident-…-final-v12.pdf"). The full name is the title tooltip and part of the accessible name.

edgeCases.title: Offline mid-upload
edgeCases.handling: The upload pauses rather than fails: the bar turns amber, the line says it will resume on its own, and it does when the socket returns (resumable chunks). Send stays disabled until it finishes, and the draft is kept.

edgeCases.title: Slow upload
edgeCases.handling: The percentage keeps moving. After 8 s without progress the line reads "Still uploading… 64% of 184 MB" and Cancel stays available. A large file goes up on pick, not on send, so Enter never feels broken.

edgeCases.title: Retry after a failure
edgeCases.handling: Retry resumes from the last confirmed chunk and turns the card back to uploading in the same place; it cannot create a second copy because the upload id is reused. Pressing Retry twice is ignored while the first attempt is starting.

edgeCases.title: File refused before it starts
edgeCases.handling: Over the workspace's size limit, or a blocked type: the file is refused at pick time with a toast that names the limit, and no card is created. Nothing is half-uploaded.

edgeCases.title: Image will not load
edgeCases.handling: A thumbnail that 404s or fails to decode falls back to the file card with the image badge, so the file can still be downloaded. A deleted or no-longer-shared file shows "This file is no longer available" with no actions.

edgeCases.title: Link preview from an untrusted page
edgeCases.handling: The domain is printed first and is the real destination (after redirects), not the page's claimed site. Previews are fetched server-side, images are proxied, and nothing autoplays. If the fetch fails there is no card, only the link in the text.

edgeCases.title: Voice note while the phone is locked
edgeCases.handling: Playback continues with the screen locked and shows on the lock screen's now-playing controls; it pauses when headphones are unplugged. Recording needs the microphone permission — see composer.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: Badge colours switch to their dark soft pairs; a pale screenshot on a dark card keeps its hairline edge so it does not read as a hole in the surface.

web.base: Inline styles over `t`: the open target is a <button> (an <a href target=_blank> for a link), hover and focus from useInteraction; Download / Cancel / Retry are the kit's IconButton and Button. The lightbox is the app's, from onOpen.
notes: Download is a real link to a short-lived signed URL with Content-Disposition: attachment, so the browser's own download UI and ⌘-click both work.
Images lazy-load with explicit width and height so the timeline never reflows when a thumbnail arrives.
Upload progress belongs to the tab: closing the tab mid-upload asks "Leave site? Changes you made may not be saved." via beforeunload.

keyboard.action: Opens the preview
Moves from the card to Download / Cancel / Retry
Closes the lightbox and returns focus to the card

desktop.base: The same file as web (one component, desktop density tokens): the 40px letter badge, the middle-truncated name and the kit's IconButton / Button; the preview is the app's, from onOpen.
notes: The FileRow shape: 40px letter badge in the family colour, name in 13 SemiBold, "PDF document · 2.4 MB", a 26px Download. 320 wide, 100% on narrow panes.
Downloads go to the OS Downloads folder through Tauri's dialog/fs plugins and announce themselves with a native notification when the window is not focused.
Files already opened are kept in the app data cache, so they reopen offline; uncached files show "You're offline. This file will download when you're back."
In the catalogue, Retry on a failed upload sets `status` to uploading (the error line gives way to the progress track), and the voice note's play button toggles `playing`.

keyboard.action: Opens the preview
In the preview: saves the file (Download)
Closes the preview

mobile.base: Pressable + View, StyleSheet over useTheme() tokens; React Native <Image> for thumbnails, Linking for a link, the name truncated in the middle with ellipsizeMode; MediaViewer is the app's, from onOpen.
notes: Files: a 40pt recessed squircle with the family glyph tinted (PDF red, sheet green), "2.4 MB · PDF" faint.
Images: a 220 × 165 tile. Tap opens MediaViewer with swipe between this message's images and videos, pinch to zoom, swipe down to close.
A file the phone can preview opens in MediaViewer; anything else is Share on iOS and Save to device on Android, and the label says which.
The composer tray chip shows the picture during the upload, not after, so you can still change your mind about the right file.

gestures.action: Opens MediaViewer (images, video, previewable files) or Share / Save to device
Message actions sheet (with Save image for photos)
Closes it back to the message

avatar.name: Avatar
avatar.description: A person or an agent, as a photo or initials, with an optional presence dot. The fallback colour is chosen from the name so the same person is the same colour on every device.

src.description: Photo URL. A broken or slow image falls back to initials — never an empty circle.

shape.description: square is for channels, projects and bots; people are circles.

agent.description: Marks an AI agent: a sparkle badge, so a person never mistakes an agent's message for a colleague's.

decorative.description: Beside the person's name drawn as text (a message, a list row, a hover card): the face is hidden from assistive tech, so the name is not read twice.

a11y.label: {name}, {presence}
notes: Initials are hidden from screen readers — the name is the label.
`decorative` removes the role and the name and hides the face from assistive tech (aria-hidden on web; hidden from VoiceOver and TalkBack on the phone): use it beside a visible name.
Presence is announced in words, never by colour alone; dnd and away also differ in shape on the presence picker.

edgeCases.title: Single-word or emoji-only names
edgeCases.handling: Initials take the first letter of up to two words; one word gives one letter. A name with no letters (an emoji, a phone number) shows the person glyph instead of an empty disc.

edgeCases.title: Photo fails or loads slowly
edgeCases.handling: Initials render first and the photo fades in over them when it decodes. A 404 keeps the initials and is not retried in the same session.

edgeCases.title: Deactivated or external user
edgeCases.handling: A deactivated account is drawn in the neutral ink colour with no presence; an external (guest) user gets a square-corner badge in the hover card, not on the avatar.

edgeCases.title: Presence while offline
edgeCases.handling: When this device is offline, other people's presence is unknown, so dots are hidden rather than shown stale.

web.base: named by the person (and presence, in words), inline styles over `t`; initials always drawn, a lazy fading in over them and dropped on error
notes: Images are lazy-loaded with an explicit width and height so the row never reflows when the photo arrives.

desktop.base: The same as web, at desktop density; initials under a lazy that fades in and is dropped on error
notes: Photos are cached in the Tauri app data folder so the sidebar draws offline.
Hovering an avatar opens the person's hover card after 380 ms (existing desktop timing).

mobile.base: View (accessibilityRole image), StyleSheet over useTheme(); initials always drawn, React Native <Image> fading in over them with <Enter motion="fade"> and dropped on error
notes: The kit draws React Native's <Image>; the app's expo-image memory+disk cache stays in the app. The Notionist face from the current app is a src, not a separate component.
Presence dot grows to 10pt minimum so it survives Dynamic Type and small sizes.

gestures.action: Opens the person's profile sheet

flows.title: A face loads: initials at once, the photo when it arrives

avatar-stack.name: Avatar stack
avatar-stack.description: Overlapping faces for the people in a channel, a thread or a meeting, with a +N chip for the ones that do not fit. Each face wears a ring in the colour of the ground it sits on, so a stack of photos still reads as separate people.

people.description: Resolved people, in order: [{ name, identity, src? }]. The first is the lead (the thread's author, the meeting's host) and is drawn on top.

max.description: Faces drawn before the rest collapse into +N. The desktop facepile draws 3, the mobile AvatarStack 4.

total.description: Everyone in the group when `people` is only a preview — a channel of 240 sends its first faces and a count. 0 means `people` is everyone.

size.description: Avatar sizes: sm is 22px on desktop (the facepile's 24 at web density) and 28pt on mobile.

ground.description: The surface the stack sits on. The ring is cut in that colour — always a surface, never an accent.

a11y.label: 5 people
notes: A group named by the count ("5 people"); on both kits each drawn face is its own image named by the person ("Priya Raman"), so the names are reachable.
The +N digits are hidden; the chip is an image named "and 2 more" in words.

edgeCases.title: Photos side by side
edgeCases.handling: Without the ring, three photos read as one smeared image. Every face — the lead's too — wears a 2px ring in the ground's colour; a stack on a selected or sidebar row passes that ground so the ring cuts rather than outlines.

edgeCases.title: Huge member count
edgeCases.handling: The chip grows into a pill rather than shrinking the digits; +237 stays legible. Past 9,999 the kit writes +10k. The count comes from the server's member total, never from the length of the preview list.

edgeCases.title: Nobody, or only you
edgeCases.handling: An empty list renders nothing — no ghost discs. A DM with only yourself (notes to self) shows your one face and no chip.

edgeCases.title: An AI agent in the stack
edgeCases.handling: Fabric keeps its coral identity disc, so it is never mistaken for a colleague, but the sparkle badge is dropped at stack sizes — at 22px it would cover the next face. The agent is named in the group label.

edgeCases.title: Presence in a stack
edgeCases.handling: No presence dots: four dots in 70px is noise and the overlap hides half of them. Presence lives in the member list the stack opens.

edgeCases.title: Member joins or leaves while it is on screen
edgeCases.handling: The stack re-renders from the live roster without animating faces in or out; the count updates in place. Someone who left drops off the preview immediately — a stale face implies they can still read the channel.

edgeCases.title: Broken photo URL
edgeCases.handling: Each face falls back to its initials on its own. The stack never shrinks because one image failed.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: The stack starts at the right; the lead stays on top and the +N chip sits at the trailing (left) end. The overlap is margin-inline-start, not margin-left.

web.base: A role="group" <div> of the kit's Avatars, each ringed in the ground's surface colour and overlapping by a third (margin-inline-start), and a +N chip named in words; inline styles over `t`
notes: Hovering a face opens that person's hover card; hovering +N lists the hidden names (up to 12, then "and 40 more").
When the stack is a link (a channel's members), the whole stack is one <a> with the group label — not one tab stop per face.

keyboard.action: Opens the member list when the stack is interactive

desktop.base: The same <div> as web, at desktop density (22px faces)
notes: Today's Facepile: 24px faces at −7px overlap with a 2px surface ring; every ring is the surface colour, including the lead's (ADR-0389 — a coral ring on the first face read as a badge on one person).
+N counts what is HIDDEN, never the total. ChannelPane's header shows the roster TOTAL beside three faces and is deliberately a different statement; it stays a separate count, not this chip.
Photos come from the Tauri app-data cache, so the stack draws offline.

mobile.base: One accessible View (role group) of the kit's Avatars with ground-coloured rings and a marginStart overlap, and the +N chip; StyleSheet over useTheme()
notes: Today's AvatarStack: 28pt faces overlapping by a third, default max 4. The +N is the face discs' own grey with muted SemiBold (owner, 2026-10-05, ADR-8910) — it was a beige disc with white Bold and read as a person.
Faces render with expo-image's memory+disk cache; a stack inside a FlatList row never re-fetches on scroll.

gestures.action: Opens the member sheet (on surfaces where the stack is interactive)

A processed recording shows who was there

badge.name: Badge
badge.description: An unread count or a dot. Coral means it needs you (a mention, a DM); neutral means there is something new but nobody asked for you.

max.description: Above this the badge reads max+. The desktop rail uses 9 to keep its 64px column.

dot.description: A dot instead of a number — activity without a mention.

label.description: What the number counts, for the accessible name.

unread.description: The count is of unread things: with no `label`, the name says "3 unread". Off, a bare count is named by its number alone.

live.description: A change of the count is announced politely. Off by default: a sidebar of badges should not each speak.

notes: The number is hidden; the label says what it counts, e.g. "3 unread mentions". With no label the name is the count alone ("3"), or "3 unread" with `unread`.
Not a live region by default: `live` makes it role status (web) or a polite live region (phone). Never announce every increment — the parent row's label carries the count.

edgeCases.title: Count is zero or unknown
edgeCases.handling: Zero renders nothing — no empty pill. While counts are still loading the badge is absent, not 0; a skeleton is never used for a badge.

edgeCases.title: Read on another device
edgeCases.handling: Counts are server-owned. Reading a channel on the phone clears the desktop badge, the Dock badge, the tab title and the phone's icon badge through one read-state event.

edgeCases.title: Muted channel with a mention
edgeCases.handling: A muted channel shows no badge for ordinary messages, but a direct @mention still shows the coral count — muting is never allowed to hide someone asking for you.

web.base: <span role="img"> (role status when `live`) named by the count and what it counts, inline styles over `t`; pops in with enter("pop")
notes: The same total also drives the tab title, "(3) AntFabric", and the favicon dot — see Tab badge.
A badge pops in (fade and a 0.94 → 1 scale, 220ms) when its first unread arrives; a changing count does not re-pop.

desktop.base: The same <span role="img"> as web, inline styles over `t`; pops in with enter("pop")
notes: The app-wide total also goes to the Dock (macOS) or taskbar overlay (Windows) — see App icon badge.
A badge pops in when its first unread arrives; a changing count does not re-pop.

mobile.base: <Enter motion="pop"> (an Animated.View; a polite live region only when `live`), StyleSheet over useTheme()
notes: The same total is the home-screen icon badge, set with expo-notifications setBadgeCountAsync and kept in step by the server's push payload.
A badge pops in (Animated, the same 0.94 → 1 scale and fade) when its first unread arrives; a changing count does not re-pop.

bar-chart.name: BarChart
bar-chart.description: Bars for comparing categories, in a card with a title, an optional headline number and a legend that turns series off. Series sit side by side, are stacked on one bar, or run left to right for long labels and ranked lists. Bars always start at zero: a bar's length is its value. A single series with a loss is coloured by sign, so a bar below zero reads as one.

headingLevel.description: The heading level of the card's title, 1 to 6, so the chart keeps the page's heading order: a card under an h2 is an h3, one under an h1 is an h2. The phone has one kind of header and reads it for nothing. The card is not a landmark: the figure inside is named by the summary.

data.description: Rows, one per category: [{ team: "Support", fabric: 182, people: 141 }, …]. The same rows can feed a table, a stat and a line chart.

x.description: The field of each row that is the category: a word or a date.

y.description: The field, or fields, that are the values: "minutes" or ["fabric", "people"]. More than one are grouped side by side, or stacked. A value that is not a number draws no bar.

title.description: The card's title. It names the figure on the page, and is the first words of what a screen reader hears.

subtitle.description: One line under the title: what it covers. Empty draws none.

headline.description: A number to lead with, under the title: { value, format, delta, deltaFormat, inverse, period }. It is a MetricValue (in the chart's format unless it names one), a Delta badge and what the change is against ("resolved in October"). Left out, the card has none.

format.description: A format name, its options or a function: what core's `fmt` takes. The axis, the labels at the ends of bars, the tooltip, the summary and "View as table" all print through it, so they agree.

xFormat.description: The category's format, for a date: "month", "day", or options such as { type: "month", timeZone: "UTC" }. A timestamp under a date format is read as a point in time, so the summary reads as a trend. Left out, the category prints as it is.

labels.description: A field's name for people, for the legend, the tooltip and the table's headers: { opened: "Opened" }. A field with no entry prints its own name.

height.description: The plot's height, in px (points on the phone). The card is as wide as the space it is given.

empty.description: The title of the empty state when there are no rows. Say why: nothing yet and nothing matching a filter are different sentences.

emptyLine.description: One sentence under it: what to do about it.

loading.description: Grey bars of uneven heights in place of the plot, from the kit's Skeleton, and no "View as table". The header stays, so the card does not jump when the data arrives. Screen readers hear "Loading chart" once.

hidden.description: The series the legend has turned off, by field: ["resolved"]. Left out, the chart keeps its own, starting with every series on. Controlled when the app passes it with `onHiddenChange`.

onHiddenChange.description: A legend entry was pressed. Called with every series that is off now. The last series showing cannot be turned off, so pressing it calls nothing.

stacked.description: Stack the series on one bar, in order, the last one carrying the rounded end. The tooltip adds a total. A stack's scale is its sums, positives and negatives apart.

horizontal.description: Bars run left to right with the categories down the side. A single series gets its value at each bar's end and no value axis. Long category labels are cut with an ellipsis and the tooltip has the full one. On the phone a single horizontal series is a ranked list of rows, not a rotated chart.

a11y.label: The summary: "Resolved this month by team: Fabric: highest Support (182), lowest Sales ops (42); People: highest Support (141), lowest Onboarding (39)."
notes: The figure is named by the sentence core's `summarize` writes from the rows: categories read as highest and lowest, dates as a trend. It is heard, not printed: in the light theme most series colours sit under 3:1 against the card, so the tooltip and "View as table" give the numbers without colour.
"View as table" shows the same rows in Table, with real headers, and a Button names it by what it will do ("View as table", then "View as chart").
The legend says what it toggles: each entry is a button that is pressed while its series is on, and one that is off is struck through, not only dimmer. The last series showing cannot be turned off.
A bar coloured by sign is never only coloured: the tooltip and the table print the value with its minus, and a bar below zero hangs under a zero rule.
On the web the plot is a stop for the arrow keys (recharts' accessibility layer): the tooltip moves category to category, and the plot draws a focus edge while the keyboard is in it.

examples.name: Stacked, by month
examples.description: Fabric and people on one bar, the total in the tooltip. The headline's change is in points: a share moves in points, not in percent of a percent.

examples.name: Grouped, by team
examples.description: Side by side: Fabric's and people's resolved tickets for each team in October.

examples.name: First reply by channel
examples.description: Horizontal, one series: the value at the end of each bar and no value axis. On the phone it is a ranked list.

examples.name: Net seats added
examples.description: One series with a loss: gains and losses take the data palette's positive and negative, and the zero rule is drawn.

examples.name: A series turned off
examples.description: `hidden` is the legend's state: People is off, so the bars regroup and the scale re-fits to Fabric.

edgeCases.title: No rows
edgeCases.handling: An empty `data` draws the kit's EmptyState in the plot's place and says why; the card keeps its header and has no "View as table" and no legend.

edgeCases.title: One bar
edgeCases.handling: One category draws one bar, never wider than the bar maximum (so a lone bar is not a slab), centred in the plot.

edgeCases.title: All zero
edgeCases.handling: A series that is zero everywhere has no range to fit, so the axis reads 0 to 1 and there are no bars to draw: the baseline stays, the labels stay, and the summary says what each is.

edgeCases.title: Negative values
edgeCases.handling: Bars keep zero, so a negative bar hangs below the rule. One series with a loss is coloured by sign. Several series, or a stack, keep their own colours: the tooltip says the minus. The phone moves a negative bar's label under the bar.

edgeCases.title: Very long labels
edgeCases.handling: A horizontal chart cuts a label to the room its axis has and ends it with an ellipsis; the tooltip has the whole name. Under vertical bars a long label is thinned like a crowded one (the web drops the ones that collide, the phone keeps one in a few).

edgeCases.title: Many series
edgeCases.handling: Nine stacked series is one more than the palette has colours: the ninth reuses the first. The legend names every one and the tooltip lists them, so a repeated colour is never the only way to tell them apart. Past about six series, a table reads better; "View as table" is there.

edgeCases.title: A long daily series
edgeCases.handling: Fourteen daily bars have more labels than a phone has room for. The web drops the labels that would collide; the phone draws one in every few, centred on its bar, and every bar is still in the tooltip and the table.

edgeCases.title: Loading
edgeCases.handling: Grey bars of uneven heights fill the plot and the card keeps its header. There is no legend, no table button and no summary yet.

web.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a <section>: the title, an optional headline, "View as table" (Button); a ChartFrame holding recharts' BarChart (`layout="vertical"` for horizontal) with a Bar per series, Cells for the hover dim and the sign colours, and a LabelList for a horizontal bar's value; the Legend (toggle buttons) in the header beside the Button, as the reference dashboard has it
notes: Shipped from the data subpath: recharts is reached only from there. The chart is handed an explicit width and height.

Everything the chart reads from the tokens goes through `rechartsTheme(useChartTokens(), useReducedMotion())`, exported beside the chart: `<CartesianGrid {...theme.grid} /> <XAxis dataKey="team" {...theme.axis} /> <Bar fill={theme.series[0]} radius={theme.bar.radius} maxBarSize={theme.bar.maxBarSize} {...theme.motion.draw} />`. A chart the kit does not ship, written with recharts and the same call, matches.

The hovered category keeps its colour and the rest step back to 38% over 150ms; a bar's fill eases to a new colour over 250ms. The bars draw in once over 600ms on the kit's ease-out and tween to new values; reduced motion turns the movement off and keeps the fades.

A horizontal chart gives its categories up to 40% of the width, cuts a longer label with an ellipsis (the tooltip shows the whole one) and draws each bar's value after it, with no value axis and no rules.

keyboard.action: Moves into the plot, then on to the legend's entries and "View as table"
In the plot: moves the tooltip to the next category
In the plot: moves the tooltip to the previous category
On a legend entry: turns the series off or back on

desktop.base: The same Card, recharts' BarChart and Legend as web, at desktop density

keyboard.action: Moves into the plot, then on to the legend's entries and "View as table"
In the plot: moves the tooltip to the next category
In the plot: moves the tooltip to the previous category
On a legend entry: turns the series off or back on

mobile.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a View: the same header and Button, a ChartFrame holding react-native-gifted-charts' BarChart (`data` for grouped bars, `stackData` for stacked, `renderTooltip` for the card); a horizontal single series is a ranked list of Views instead;; the Legend's toggles above the plot
notes: `giftedTheme(useChartTokens())` is the chart tokens as gifted-charts' own props, exported beside the chart: `<BarChart {...theme.axis} barWidth={theme.bar.width} frontColor={theme.series[0]} />`.

Horizontal bars are a ranked list of rows (label and value over a track and its fill), not a rotated gifted-charts chart, whose labels turn sideways on a 390pt screen. More than one horizontal series draws the vertical chart.

gifted-charts' `height` is the part above zero: sections below zero are added to it, so the kit shrinks the plot by their share to keep the card's height, and moves a negative bar's label under the bar (`autoShiftLabels`).

gifted-charts opens its own tooltip on a grouped bar, but not on a stack (it compares the stack's selection with `===` against an array), so the kit draws the card itself over the pressed stack, centred on it and kept inside the plot. A press also lights the category's bars and steps the rest back, as the web's hover does.
A long series (fourteen days) has more labels than room: the kit draws one in every few, centred on its bar, and the tooltip names the day.
The bars draw in unless the person reduces motion. Under react-native-web (the catalogue, `pnpm check`) gifted-charts' animation is off.

gestures.action: Focuses its category: the others step back and the tooltip card shows each series at it
Turns the series off or back on
