bottom-sheet.name: Bottom sheet
bottom-sheet.description: The phone's one modal surface: a panel that slides up from the bottom with 20pt top corners, a grab handle, a title row with a close button, and whatever the screen needs to ask. It answers the keyboard, stops under the screen's header row, and — new in this spec — can be dragged down to dismiss.

title.description: Empty draws no title row — the handle and the content only.

largeTitle.description: The 28pt title for a sheet that is a destination of its own (New message), not a question about the screen under it.

tall.description: Full height, up to the header row behind it, so a list can grow and a footer action sits at the foot however short the list is.

children.description: What the sheet holds. Rows inside bleed to the gutter themselves.

primaryLabel.description: A full-width action pinned at the foot (Add 2 people). Empty draws none.

onPrimary.description: The primary button was pressed. The sheet does not close itself: close it from here, or leave it open while the action runs.

keyboard.description: Draws the on-screen keyboard, to show the sheet sitting on it.

dragging.description: Mid-drag: the panel follows the finger and the scrim lightens with it.

closed.description: Dismissed: the panel has slid back down off the screen and the scrim has cleared. What the close button does in the catalogue; in the app the sheet then unmounts and onClose fires.

onClose.description: The person asked to close: ×, backdrop, drag, back, the escape gesture.

onDismiss.description: The sheet has finished leaving. A screen that opens another sheet next waits for this — iOS drops a modal presented while another is still going.

a11y.label: {title}
notes: Phone: accessibilityViewIsModal keeps VoiceOver inside the sheet; the screen behind is the host's to hide on Android (importantForAccessibility), which the kit cannot reach from inside the sheet.

Phone: screen-reader focus moves to the title (a header), or to the handle when there is none, when the sheet opens; Android's back button closes it, and so does the escape gesture. The handle's touch area is the profile's 44pt target without drawing more, and the sheet sits above the keyboard on iOS (a KeyboardAvoidingView). The home-indicator inset is a token, not the device's safe area: the host's insets are not read.

Web: focus moves into the panel when it mounts, Tab stays inside, Esc closes, and focus returns to the opener when it unmounts; the 36 × 5 handle has a transparent box centred on it that reaches the profile's target size. The handle is the labelled "Dismiss" button — dragging is never the only way out.
A sheet without a title still takes an accessible name from its caller (`aria-label`, `accessibilityLabel`).

examples.name: Picker
examples.description: Add people: a search field and a checklist.

edgeCases.title: The keyboard comes up
edgeCases.handling: The panel lifts to sit on the keyboard and caps its height to the space above it; the list inside shrinks and scrolls rather than drawing under the keys. Nothing is estimated — no per-screen chrome constants — the sheet measures the inset. Closing dismisses the keyboard.

edgeCases.title: Dragged halfway, then let go
edgeCases.handling: Below the 25% threshold and slower than a fling, it springs back to rest; past it, it continues down and calls onClose. The scrim's opacity tracks the drag so the screen behind brightens as the sheet leaves. A drag that starts in the list while the list is scrolled only scrolls.

edgeCases.title: Dismissed with something typed in it
edgeCases.handling: A sheet holding an unsent draft or picked people snaps back on drag, backdrop tap or back, and asks "Discard your changes?" in a ConfirmSheet. Because iOS silently drops a modal presented while another is still dismissing, the confirm is presented from the first sheet's onDismiss (useSheetHandoff), never straight after onClose.

edgeCases.title: More content than the screen
edgeCases.handling: The panel stops under the header row and the body scrolls; a footer action stays pinned at the foot with the home-indicator space under it, so the CTA is always reachable without scrolling.

edgeCases.title: A sheet opened from a menu or another sheet
edgeCases.handling: One modal at a time. A menu row that opens a sheet closes the menu and presents the sheet from the menu's onDismiss; a sheet that leads to another replaces itself the same way. Stacked sheets are never drawn.

edgeCases.title: Text at 130%
edgeCases.handling: The 20pt title wraps; the 28pt large title stays on one line and truncates. Rows grow with their text. Font scale is capped at 1.3× as everywhere in the app, and the panel scrolls before it ever pushes the footer off screen.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: The sheet fades in and out instead of sliding. Dragging still moves it — direct manipulation follows the finger — but the release settles without a spring overshoot.

edgeCases.title: Backgrounded or killed
edgeCases.handling: Backgrounded, the sheet is exactly where it was on return. Killed, a transient sheet (a picker, a confirm) is not restored; the New message draft is saved as a draft and reappears in the composer, not as a sheet.

edgeCases.title: iPad and large phones in landscape
edgeCases.handling: At regular width the sheet becomes a centred form sheet at the app's 540pt modal width with all four corners rounded, the same content and the same drag. Landscape on a phone keeps the bottom sheet but caps it at 90% of the height.

edgeCases.title: Liquid Glass and earlier iOS
edgeCases.handling: The glass follows the iPhone's own settings with no work from us, because the kit draws it with the system material (GlassView): Clear or Tinted (Settings → Display & Brightness → Liquid Glass) changes how much shows through, Reduce Transparency makes it frosted and nearly opaque while keeping its shape, and Increase Contrast adds a contrasting edge. The app subscribes to AccessibilityInfo 'reduceTransparencyChanged' only to adjust what it draws around the glass. iOS before 26 keeps the blur look. This happens live in the app as the person changes the setting.

web.base: A <div role="dialog"> aria-modal on a scrim, inline styles over `t`; slides up with enter("slide-up"), then a drag or a close moves it with a transform transition. The handle is a Dismiss <button>; ×, the handle and Esc set `closed` (useControllable) and call onClose; onDismiss fires when the slide down ends
notes: Decision: a bottom sheet exists on the web only in a phone-width browser. At 640px and wider the same caller content opens as what it is on desktop: a Dialog for pickers and forms, a Menu for action lists, a HoverCard or side panel for details.
The kit does not lift the sheet over the on-screen keyboard or read the safe-area inset: the host that mounts it owns both (visualViewport, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)).
Drag-to-dismiss and the browser's pull-to-refresh are the host's: the kit's sheet follows `dragging` and `closed` and calls onClose from the handle, the × and Esc.

keyboard.action: Closes (a hardware keyboard on a tablet)
Trapped inside the sheet

gestures.action: Dismisses past 25% of the height, otherwise springs back

desktop.alternative: A window with a pointer has no bottom sheet. Each use maps to the desktop's own surface: a picker or form (Add people, New message) is a centred Dialog at the one modal width; a list of actions (message actions) is a Menu or Context menu; a person or channel card is a HoverCard; a detail pane (a task) is the right-hand side drawer — the Scrim's side alignment, as TaskDrawer uses. The window's minimum width keeps it out of phone territory, so there is no narrow breakpoint to fall back to.

mobile.base: <Enter motion="slide-up"> (role dialog, accessibilityViewIsModal) around an Animated.View that the handle and title row drag through PanResponder (past 120pt or a fling dismisses), on GlassSurface (Liquid Glass on iOS 26+); ScrollView body; `closed` through useControllable, onDismiss when the slide down ends
notes: The surface panel with 20pt top corners, the 36 × 5 handle 12pt from the top, then one 16pt rhythm: handle → title row → first child. The title row is the title on the left and the × in a 40pt box whose box (not glyph) sits on the 12pt gutter.
Title is 20pt semibold on a 24pt line; largeTitle is 28pt on the 40pt box line, one line.

At rest the panel stops under the screen's header row (status bar + 12 + 40 + 8 — y 119 on an 852pt iPhone) so the dimmed title behind is never cut through. With the keyboard up the cap is the space above the keys instead.

Keyboard: on iOS the sheet is inside a KeyboardAvoidingView and lifts above the keys; on Android the window's own adjustResize is relied on (an edge-to-edge Modal window that is not resized needs the host to measure the IME).
Closing always puts the keyboard away too.
Today's Sheet is a plain Modal with animationType slide and no drag. The kit's sheet adds drag-to-dismiss: a PanResponder on the handle and title row.

iOS 26+: Liquid Glass — the surface is drawn through expo-glass-effect's GlassView (gated on its availability check; the material itself follows the device's Clear / Tinted, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast settings). iOS 18 and earlier keep today's blur/opaque look. At a partial height the sheet floats 8pt in from the screen edges with fully rounded corners, as iOS 26 sheets do; at full height it meets the edges again.
In the catalogue the panel slides up on arrival and the × sets `closed`: the panel slides back down and the scrim clears. Replay brings it back.

gestures.gesture: Drag the handle or title row down
gestures.action: The panel follows the finger 1:1 and the scrim lightens with it; released past 25% of its height or flung faster than 1000 pt/s it dismisses, otherwise it springs back
Rubber-bands at 0.2× and springs back — a sheet has no taller detent

gestures.gesture: Drag down inside a scrolled list
gestures.action: Scrolls the list; only once the list is at its top does the same drag start moving the sheet
Closes
Dismisses the keyboard first if it is up, then closes
Closes

flows.title: Add people to a channel from a sheet
Swipe the sheet away

breadcrumbs.name: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.description: One 44px line across the top of the content, naming where you are and offering the way back up: Projects \ Release Train \ #release-train. It holds text and nothing else, except a small red pill with the elapsed time while a recording is running. On the Mac it is also the window's title bar.

items.description: [{ key, label, icon?, to? }], root first. key names the crumb. to is where the crumb goes; a crumb without one is plain text, because a crumb that looks clickable and goes nowhere is worse than one that never looked clickable. The last item is the current page and is never a link. icon is a pictogram before the label (lock for a private channel); a public channel's # is part of its label.

expanded.description: Every crumb is shown. Left (false) is the trail when it does not fit: the first crumb and the current page stay, and everything between folds into … , a button that unfolds the hidden crumbs in place. The product decides when the trail folds; this prop draws the folded state. Needs three crumbs or more.

lights.description: Today's Mac build: this row is the title bar, so the traffic lights float over its left end and the first crumb starts 96px in. Off in full screen (the lights hide) and off once the Title bar is drawn above this row.

status.description: What the status pill at the end of the bar says is happening. Empty draws nothing, so the strip is text and nothing else. live is a red fill, paused amber, busy a red fill with a grey dot (finishing up). AntFabric draws its meeting recorder here: live is Recording, busy is Saving….

statusDetail.description: The pill's second figure, in tabular figures so the pill does not shuffle sideways: a clock, a count. AntFabric passes the recorder's own snapshot (a 250 ms tick from Rust), formatted HH:MM:SS; this component never counts.

statusAction.description: What pressing the pill does: its title ("Open Recordings"), and the end of its accessible name with the first letter lowered ("Recording: 00:00:12, open Recordings").

label.description: The navigation landmark's name. Default: the `label` string ("Breadcrumb").

a11y.label: {label}
notes: An ordered list of list items, so a screen reader announces the structure; the backslashes are hidden, because a spoken "backslash" between every crumb is noise.
The current page is aria-current="page" and is not a link: it names where you already are.
The recording pill is a button, never a live region: a clock announced every 250 ms is worse than silence. Its name carries the destination: "Recording: 00:00:12, open Recordings".
… is a button named "Show the rest of the path" with aria-expanded=false; pressing it unfolds the hidden crumbs in place and moves focus to the first one.

edgeCases.title: A trail longer than the strip
edgeCases.handling: First the crumbs between the root and the current page fold into … , which unfolds them in order; the root never folds, so the way back to the top is always one click. Then the current page truncates with an ellipsis and its full name is the tooltip and the accessible name. A mid-trail crumb is never wider than 200px. Unfolding happens as soon as the window is wide enough again.

edgeCases.title: A very long channel name
edgeCases.handling: The current page is the only crumb that shrinks, so it takes the ellipsis while the root stays whole. The leaf's line height is the body-sm leading, never 1, so descenders are not clipped.

edgeCases.title: Nothing open
edgeCases.handling: An organisation with no channels, or the moment before the first list read answers, shows the root alone (ADR-4538), never Channels \ # with a bare hash naming a channel that is not there. With no conversation open, the destination is where you are.

edgeCases.title: Paused, then saving
edgeCases.handling: Paused turns the pill amber and says Paused with the time held; after Stop it reads Saving… with a grey dot until the file is written, then disappears. The time always comes from the recorder's own snapshot, so a stopped microphone can never keep counting. Tabular figures stop the pill shuffling sideways every second.

edgeCases.title: macOS traffic lights and full screen
edgeCases.handling: In today's Mac app the lights float over the row's left end, so the first crumb starts 96px in (16px start, three 12px lights, a 26px gap); move them in tauri.conf.json and this inset moves with them. In full screen macOS hides the lights and the inset drops back to 16px, read on mount and on every resize. Windows and Linux reserve nothing.

edgeCases.title: Renamed, moved or deleted elsewhere
edgeCases.handling: The trail is worked out from live state, so a channel renamed on someone's phone changes here in the same moment as the sidebar. A channel deleted or archived while open drops the trail to its root and the pane shows its own empty state. Offline, the desktop draws the trail from its SQLite cache, and crumbs to screens that need the network still go there and say so.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard only and screen readers
edgeCases.handling: Tab reaches only crumbs that go somewhere, then … , then the recording pill. A plain-text crumb such as Direct messages is not a stop, because there is no screen behind it. The focus ring is drawn on the crumb's own 3px by 6px padding, so it does not touch the separators.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left languages
edgeCases.handling: The trail runs right to left with the root at the right edge and the recording pill at the left. The backslash is mirrored so it still leans toward the next crumb. On a Mac set to Arabic or Hebrew the traffic lights move to the right, and the inset follows them.

web.base: A <nav> holding an <ol>: <a href> crumbs (a plain click calls onNavigate, ⌘-click and middle-click stay the browser's), plain-text steps and an aria-current leaf; inline styles over `t`, hover and focus from useInteraction; the … <button> unfolds a folded trail (`expanded` through useControllable, reported by onExpandedChange)
notes: The same 44px strip, directly under the Web top bar and spanning the content column. No traffic lights and no drag region: the browser owns the frame.
The trail comes from the route (each matched route's crumb, read with useMatches), so Back and Forward redraw it and a shared link lands with the right trail.
Crumbs are real links (<a href>), so middle-click and ⌘-click open that level in a new browser tab.
The current page names the browser tab: document.title is "#release-train · Release Train — AntFabric", after any unread count.
No recording pill. A browser tab cannot run the recorder: capture is the desktop's Rust recorder, and outside Tauri the capture backend refuses everything, so the pill never has a state to show.

keyboard.action: Moves through the crumbs that go somewhere; the current page and plain-text crumbs are not stops
Follows the crumb
Unfolds the hidden crumbs in place and moves focus to the first one

desktop.base: The same <nav> and <ol> with <button> crumbs, the macOS traffic lights when `lights` is on, and the recording pill <button> at the right end; data-tauri-drag-region on the bar
notes: Text and nothing else (ADR-0180): no search, no avatar, no menu. If a control is proposed for this strip, that is the old top bar being rebuilt one button at a time and needs its own decision.

The one exception is the recording pill (ADR-0437): a live microphone is a statement about the hardware and the person's privacy, not navigation chrome. It renders nothing when idle, carries no Pause or Stop (ADR-1101), and clicking it opens Recordings, where those controls live. It is the only elapsed clock in the window, on every screen.
The pill is 26px inside the 44px strip and must never grow it, or every pane below moves down.

Since ADR-5322 the strip spans the whole window, above the nav rail. In the Mac app it is the title bar: the traffic lights float over its left end (the first crumb starts at 96px, or 16px in full screen), the nav and the list carry data-tauri-drag-region so the empty space drags the window and a double-click zooms it, and the crumbs stay ordinary buttons. If the Title bar spec is adopted, the lights and the drag region move up to it and this row starts at 16px.

The trail is worked out from where you are, in the same order as the screen switch (trailOf mirrors ActiveScreen); it is never stored. Channels, Projects, Meetings, My tasks, Recordings, Inbox and Assistant are roots; a DM sits under Channels \ Direct messages.

The separator is a backslash, by the owner's call (ADR-0197), not a chevron. A private channel leads with a 12px lock at 55% opacity and a 6px gap, as the sidebar row draws it; a public channel's # is part of the label.
New in this spec: folding middle crumbs into … and the 200px cap on a mid-trail crumb. Today trails are at most three crumbs and never fold.
In the catalogue, pressing … unfolds the trail (it sets `expanded`) so the hidden crumbs come back in place and focus moves to the first of them.

keyboard.action: Moves through the crumbs that go somewhere, then the recording pill
Follows the crumb; on the pill, opens Recordings
Unfolds the hidden crumbs in place and moves focus to the first one

mobile.alternative: A phone has no width for a path. A pushed screen's Mobile header carries a back control and the screen's own title, which is the current page; the navigation stack is the trail. Back, the iOS edge swipe and Android back walk up it, and a long-press on the iOS back button lists every screen behind, which is the phone's version of the folded … . The recording time is on the recorder screen itself.

flows.title: Go back up to the project
The recording pill opens Recordings

breakdown.name: Breakdown
breakdown.description: A whole split into its parts: one bar with a thin gap of the card between the parts, the total as the card's headline (with an optional change badge), and the parts listed under it, each with its colour, name, value and share. Pointing at a part, or at its row, lights it and steps the rest back. Past eight parts the rest fold into one called "Other". Drawn with plain views, no chart library. "View as table" shows every row, unfolded.

data.description: Rows, one per part: [{ channel: "#support", tickets: 312 }, …]. The same rows can feed a donut, a table and a stat. In the order they are given: the bar reads best largest first.

name.description: The field of each row that names its part.

value.description: The field of each row that is its value. A value under zero, or one that is not a number, counts as 0: a share is never negative.

title.description: The card's title. It names the figure on the page, and is the first words of what a screen reader hears.

subtitle.description: One line under the title: what it covers. Empty draws none.

format.description: A format name, its options or a function: what core's `fmt` takes. The total, each part, the summary and "View as table" print through it. The shares are always whole percents.

valueLabel.description: The value column's name in "View as table". Default "Value".

delta.description: The change in the total, as a number the delta format prints: `0.034` is `+3.4%`. Left out, the headline has no badge.

deltaFormat.description: A format name, its options or a function for the badge. Default a signed percent.

inverse.description: Down is good (open tickets, response time): the badge's colours swap, the arrow does not.

period.description: What the change is against, after the badge: "tickets, vs September".

selected.description: The part that is picked, by its name: its segment of the bar and its row stay lit and the others step back until it is picked again. Pointing at a part or tabbing to its row lights it too, for as long as the pointer or the keyboard is there. Left out, the chart keeps its own, starting with none. Controlled when the app passes it with `onSelectedChange`.

onSelectedChange.description: A segment of the bar or a row was pressed. Called with the part's name, or with null when it was already the one picked.

height.description: The height of the loading and empty states, in px (points on the phone). The bar and the list take what they need.

empty.description: The title of the empty state when there are no rows. Say why: nothing yet and nothing matching a filter are different sentences.

emptyLine.description: One sentence under it: what to do about it.

loading.description: Grey bars of uneven heights in place of the bar and the list, from the kit's Skeleton, and no "View as table". The header stays, so the card does not jump when the data arrives. Screen readers hear it once.

a11y.role: figure (web), one image and a list (phone)
a11y.label: The summary: "Where October's tickets came from: #support 312 (40.6%), #billing 158 (20.5%), #platform-eng 121 (15.7%), #onboarding 96 (12.5%), Email 82 (10.7%); total 769."
notes: The bar is an image named by the sentence core's `segmentsOf` and `summarizeSegments` write from the rows: every part, its value and its share, and the total. It is heard, not printed: the list under the bar prints every part's name, value and share, so colour is never the only way in.

Each row is a button that says its own sentence ("#billing, 158, 21%"), pressed while it is the one picked, and a stop in the Tab order, so a keyboard can light and pick a part as a pointer does. The segments are not separate stops: the rows are the way in, and name the same parts.
The headline's number and badge say the total and the change in words ("Up 3.4%, good"), and the list's shares are whole percents with the exact ones in the summary.
"View as table" is the other way in: every row, with real headers, and nothing folded into "Other".

examples.name: Where October's tickets came from
examples.description: Five parts: the total as the headline, one bar, and the parts listed with their value and share.

examples.name: A part picked
examples.description: `selected` is `#billing`: its segment and its row stay lit and the others step back.

examples.name: Fewer is better
examples.description: `inverse`: down is good, so a fall in tickets is the green badge.

examples.name: Eleven channels
examples.description: The first eight keep a colour of the palette; the other three are one part, Other, in grey.

edgeCases.title: No rows
edgeCases.handling: An empty `data` draws the kit's EmptyState in the plot's place and says why (the title and line are props); the card keeps its header, and has no headline and no "View as table", since there is nothing to total or show. The figure's label says there is no data.

edgeCases.title: One part
edgeCases.handling: One row is the whole bar, rounded at both ends, its share 100% and the total its value.

edgeCases.title: All zero
edgeCases.handling: A whole of nothing has no shares to cut: the bar is its empty track in grey, the total says 0, every share is an en dash and the summary says every value is 0.

edgeCases.title: More than eight parts
edgeCases.handling: The palette has eight colours, and a ninth would wrap onto the first, so the first eight keep their own and every row after them is summed into one more, labelled "Other", in a neutral grey (`chart.other`) that is no colour of the palette. Pass the rows largest first so what is folded is what is smallest. It is one row in the list and one segment on the bar, and the summary says how many it holds ("Other, 3 more, 47 (6.1%)"). "View as table" shows every row.

edgeCases.title: A part that is a sliver
edgeCases.handling: A segment is never narrower than `chart.splitMinW`, so a part that is a fraction of a percent of the whole still shows; its row says the real share, and a part of 0 has no segment at all but is in the list at 0%.

edgeCases.title: A long name
edgeCases.handling: A name too long for its row is cut with an ellipsis; the summary, the row's accessible name and the table have the whole name.

edgeCases.title: Loading
edgeCases.handling: Grey bars of uneven heights fill the plot and the card keeps its header. There is no headline, no list, no table button and no summary yet. A screen reader hears "Loading chart" once.

web.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a <section>: the title, the total as a headline (MetricValue, Delta) and "View as table" (Button); a ChartFrame holding a flex row of <span> segments (flex set to each part's value, `chart.splitGap` apart) and a <ul> of <button> rows (aria-pressed) laid out in columns
notes: No chart library: the bar is views, so it reads the same on every platform and costs nothing. Each segment's width is its share of the whole; a part that is a sliver of it is held to `chart.splitMinW` so it still shows, and a part of 0 is in the list only.

The first and last segments are rounded at the bar's outer ends (`radius.pill`) and the ones between are square, so the gaps read as cuts in one bar. One part is a whole rounded bar; all zero is the empty track in grey.

Pointing at a segment or a row, or tabbing to a row, lights that part: the other segments fade to 38% over 150ms on the kit's ease-out, and its row takes the hover fill. The states come from the kit's interaction hook and pointer events, never `:hover`. A click picks it and keeps it lit.
The bar wipes in once from the left (the kit's `grow-x` entrance, 280ms on ease-out). Reduced motion turns it off.

The list lays out in as many columns as fit, each at least `chart.partMinW` wide. Past eight parts the rest fold into "Other", in a grey that is no colour of the palette (core's `segmentsOf`, as DonutChart).

keyboard.action: Moves through the parts in the list, then to "View as table". A part that has focus is lit, with its segment
On a part: picks it, or puts it back when it was picked

desktop.base: The same Card, bar and list as web, at desktop density
notes: The same panel as the web's. The pointer's hover lights a part, and a click picks it.

keyboard.action: Moves through the parts in the list, then to "View as table". A part that has focus is lit, with its segment
On a part: picks it, or puts it back when it was picked

mobile.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a View: the same header, headline and Button; a ChartFrame holding an Animated row of Pressable segments and, below it, one Pressable row per part (a swatch, the name, the value and the share), each at least 44pt tall
notes: No chart library: the bar is views, the same as the web's. The list is one column, full width, each part on one line (the web's two-line cell does not fit a phone's rows).
A phone has no hover, so a tap on a segment or on a row picks the part (the other segments step back to 38%, and `onSelectedChange` is called) and a tap on it again puts it back.
The bar grows in over 280ms from its centre unless the person reduces motion (the kit's `grow-x` entrance, as `Enter` draws it).

gestures.action: Picks the part: the others step back and its row is lit. Tap it again to put it back
The same as tapping its segment

flows.title: Look at #billing

button.name: Button
button.description: The one way to start an action. Flat in every tier, with an optional icon either side and a loading state that keeps its width so the layout never jumps.

variant.description: primary is the brand fill — one per view. danger is for an action that cannot be undone.

loading.description: Shows a spinner in place of the leading icon and blocks presses. The label stays, so the width does not change.

full.description: Stretches to its container. The default on mobile sheets and forms.

shortcut.description: A keyboard hint drawn after the label, written once as Mod+Enter; each OS gets its own glyphs.

type.description: What the button does inside a form: submit sends it, reset clears it, button (the default) does neither. A loading submit button does not submit.

a11y.label: {label}
notes: Loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled (the phone: accessibilityState.busy) and keeps the button in the tab order, so focus is not lost; only `disabled` removes it. Pressing a loading button does nothing, and the wait is announced once, politely, as "Loading". The spinner itself is hidden from assistive technology.
Icon-only buttons are IconButton, which requires a label.
`type="submit"` makes it the form's submit button; a loading submit button does not submit.
On the phone a small button (sm) keeps its drawn size and its touch area is grown to 44pt.

examples.name: Ink, pressed
examples.description: Ink turns to the brand colour on hover and a step deeper while pressed, like the other variants.

edgeCases.title: Label longer than the space
edgeCases.handling: One line, truncated with an ellipsis. The full label stays the accessible name; on web and desktop it is also the tooltip.

edgeCases.title: Double press while a request is in flight
edgeCases.handling: loading disables the button the moment the press lands; the caller sets it synchronously, before awaiting. Requests carry an idempotency key so a retry after a network drop cannot post twice.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: Height is a minimum, not fixed — the label grows and the pill grows with it. Font scale is capped at 1.3× (maxFontSizeMultiplier) as in the current app.

edgeCases.title: Shortcut the browser already owns
edgeCases.handling: Never advertise ⌘W / ⌘T / ⌘N / ⌘L / ⌘R on the web — the browser takes them first. The desktop app may bind them; the web app uses an alternative and the hint shows that.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left languages
edgeCases.handling: Leading and trailing icons swap sides; directional icons (arrow-right, send) mirror. Styles use start/end, never left/right.

web.base: A <button>, inline styles over `t`; hover, press and keyboard focus from useInteraction
notes: A link styled as a button is <a href>, not a button with onClick — middle-click and ⌘-click must open a tab.
Shortcut hints are shown only when the shortcut is NOT one the browser owns (⌘W, ⌘T, ⌘N, ⌘L are the browser's).

keyboard.action: Activates
Focus ring drawn only for keyboard focus (:focus-visible)

desktop.base: The same <button> as the web, at desktop density; shortcut glyphs per OS from usePlatform()
notes: Today's desktop Button has no loading state; this spec adds one so a slow save no longer needs a separate spinner.
Shortcut hints render with native glyphs: ⌘↩ on macOS, Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Linux.

keyboard.action: Activates
Activates the primary button of a dialog or composer

mobile.base: Pressable + Text over createStyles(t), font("semibold"), ActivityIndicator while loading; scales to 0.97 on press-in
notes: md and lg are the 56pt call-to-action used on V2; sm (34pt) is for inline actions only and gets hitSlop to reach 44pt.
Light impact haptic on press-in, never on disabled.
No hover state exists on a phone — the React Native kit has none.

gestures.action: Activates; scale to 0.97 on press-in
Cancels

flows.title: A destructive CTA opens a confirm

card.name: Card
card.description: A white surface for one thing — a project, a task, a meeting, a note from Fabric. The radius steps down as cards nest (pane 16 → rail 14 → inner 12), and a clickable card answers the pointer with a grey fill while nothing moves.

children.description: Whatever the card holds. The card adds the frame and an 8px gap between direct children; it never styles the content.

level.description: The nesting level, named instead of the radius so a 16px card inside a 16px pane cannot be written by accident. Mobile cards are always 16.

elevate.description: Pick by the ground: card on the cream page, hairline on a tinted surface, none for a card inside a panel. Mobile cards are flat; the hairline border separates them.

tint.description: brand is a coral-tinted note — "Fabric wrote this" — never decoration. recessed is a box on white (an inset inside a panel).

interactive.description: The whole card opens something. Hover fills it with the hover surface; the border and the shadow hold still.

label.description: Accessible name of the card's press target when interactive, e.g. "Open Checkout revamp". Left out, the web target is named by the card's first heading, else by its text; the phone's by what the card holds.

href.description: A card that navigates: the stretched target is an <a href>, so ⌘-click and middle-click open it in a new tab. A plain click calls onPress (and stays on the page) when there is one.

pad.description: default is 16 on web and desktop, 12 on mobile (the app-wide row inset). none is for a card that is a scroll container or holds full-bleed rows.

accent.description: A 3pt leading colour rail. Mobile only, and used sparingly — the desktop has rejected coloured card edges; it signals state with a Tag inside.

notes: A non-interactive card has no role; its heading carries the structure.

An interactive card has exactly one press target with a name: `label`, else the first heading inside the card, else the card's text. Its long-press alternative is also offered as an accessibility action ("Select") because VoiceOver and TalkBack users cannot long-press reliably.

props.label: Open action item: Send the vendor contract to legal

edgeCases.title: A card inside a card
edgeCases.handling: Name the level, not the radius: pane (16) holds rail (14) holds inner (12). The inner card takes elevate="none" — a shadow says it left the surface, which a row inside a panel does not do, and in a 320px rail the blur eats the gap between neighbours.

edgeCases.title: Hover must not move anything
edgeCases.handling: Only the fill changes (to the hover surface; brand.soft-hover on a brand card). No lift, no border colour, no scale — a lift in a tight rail reads as the neighbours dimming, and a border that changes colour flickers as the pointer crosses the edge. Only background-color and color transition.

edgeCases.title: No hover on touch
edgeCases.handling: The press is the feedback: scale 0.99 while the finger is down. Anything a desktop card reveals on hover (a ⋯ menu, a quick action) is reached by long-press on the phone, or is always visible.

edgeCases.title: Buttons inside a clickable card
edgeCases.handling: The nested control wins: on web and desktop it sits above the stretched press target (position: relative) and stops propagation; on mobile the inner Pressable claims the responder, so the card does not open. Never put a card's only primary action inside it AND on the card itself.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard and screen reader
edgeCases.handling: One tab stop per card (the press target), with the focus ring drawn around the whole card via focus-within. Its name is label, not the concatenated card text; nested buttons are the next tab stops.

edgeCases.title: Content still loading
edgeCases.handling: The card frame renders immediately at its final size and holds Skeleton shapes (shown after 300 ms). Never a spinner inside a card, and never a card that pops in after its neighbours.

edgeCases.title: Offline or stale
edgeCases.handling: A card drawn from the desktop's SQLite cache or the phone's snapshot looks exactly like a live one — no greying. Staleness is said once at the pane level (an InlineBanner), not on every card.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: The surface steps lighter than the page (#222124 on #161618), the shadows deepen, and the brand tint becomes a dark coral (#382525). Contrast against a recessed panel comes from the hairline, which is why the border is never removed.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: The accent rail moves to the leading edge, which is the right in RTL. It is a border-start, never border-left.

web.base: A <div> with a stretched <button> under the content as its one press target (nested controls sit above it); hover from useInteraction fills it, keyboard focus rings the whole card; inline styles over `t`
notes: An interactive card is a stretched link: one <a href> (with `href`) or <button> covers the card, and nested controls sit above it with position: relative. A <button> wrapping the whole card would make every nested button invalid HTML.
A card that navigates (`href`) is an <a>, so middle-click and ⌘-click open it in a new tab.
With no `label`, the target is named by the card's first heading (aria-labelledby) or, with none, by the card's text; give a `label` when that is not what the card is for.

keyboard.action: Focuses the card's press target once; the ring is drawn around the whole card
Opens it

desktop.base: The same <div> as web: level / elevate / tint over `t` at desktop density
notes: The house treatment inside a panel is level="inner" elevate="none" interactive: white on white, the hairline as the whole separation, and a hover that fills to the hover surface while NOTHING moves (owner, 2026-08-28; ADR-0322). The border does not change colour on hover.
A brand card hovers one step further, to brand.soft-hover — it is already soft-filled, so the plain hover would be a no-op.
`ref` reaches the root <div> (React 19: a prop), because a card is often the scroll container whose position has to be restored.
A Panel (flat region, no radius) is a different component: a region is a Panel, a thing is a Card (ADR-0307).

keyboard.action: Opens the card

mobile.base: A View, or a Pressable when interactive (role, label and a "Select" accessibility action for long-press on it), scaling to 0.99 while pressed; StyleSheet over useTheme()
notes: Radius 16, 12pt inner padding (owner, 2026-09-10: 12 is the app-wide inset) — not the 16pt screen gutter, which is a different measurement.
Children are clipped to the radius (overflow: hidden) — RN does not clip on its own, and a full-bleed footer would square off past the corners.
accessibilityRole/Label/State go on the Pressable, not the Box inside it, or a screen reader never hears them. A selected recording is told by the card's accessibilityState alone (ADR-8910).
No hover on a phone: the press feedback is a 0.99 scale, and long-press is where a hover-revealed menu lives on desktop.

gestures.action: Opens it; scales to 0.99 while pressed
Acts on it instead of opening it — enters multi-select in Recordings, with a light haptic

flows.title: Press a card to open what it holds

checkbox.name: Checkbox
checkbox.description: The checkbox: one rounded square, one size, brand-filled when ticked. It means "several of these can be on" — a single choice among options is a radio, marked with a dot, never a tick. Ticked, unticked, or mixed for a parent whose children disagree.

label.description: The accessible name, and the visible text unless hideLabel is set.

description.description: A second line under the label. Say what ticking it does, or why it cannot be changed.
description.sample: Only members can find this channel.

indeterminate.description: Some but not all of the items this box stands for are ticked. Drawn as a dash; aria-checked="mixed". Ticking it ticks them all.

hideLabel.description: Draw the box alone — the task table's done toggle. The label is still the accessible name and the tooltip.

a11y.label: {label}
notes: aria-checked is true, false or mixed; the box is aria-hidden so the state is not announced twice.

The description is the control's aria-describedby (the phone: its accessibilityHint), so "Private channel, checkbox, checked. Only members can find this channel." Inside a FormField the field's description and error are read after it, and the control is marked aria-invalid and aria-required.
A box drawn alone has a target of at least 24px on the web in the neutral theme, and 44pt on the phone (its touch area is grown, not its drawing).

props.label: Private channel
props.description: A channel filed under a project stays private.

edgeCases.title: A parent over a partial selection
edgeCases.handling: Select-all over 3 of 7 people shows the dash and aria-checked="mixed". Pressing it ticks all seven — never clears them, because the person reaching for it nearly always means "all". Pressing again clears all. The description says the count.

edgeCases.title: A long label
edgeCases.handling: The label wraps; it is never truncated, because the end of a consent or a setting is often the part that matters. The box stays aligned with the first line.

edgeCases.title: A save in flight, or refused
edgeCases.handling: The tick flips at once. If the server refuses, it flips back and a toast says "Couldn't update Private channel. Try again." Rapid toggling coalesces: one request in flight, and the last value wins. No spinner replaces the box.

edgeCases.title: Disabled must say why
edgeCases.handling: A greyed box with no reason is a dead end: pair disabled with a description that names the rule or who can change it. A tooltip is not enough — it is unreachable on a disabled control by pointer and by keyboard.

edgeCases.title: Unticked edge contrast
edgeCases.handling: The unticked ring is border.default (rgba(51,51,51,.24)), about 1.6:1 on white — under WCAG 2.2's 3:1 for a control's boundary. The label beside it carries identification, so the box is still usable, but the gap is recorded here rather than hidden. Proposed fix for the owner: text.placeholder (3.3:1) for the unticked ring only.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: The label and description grow and wrap; the 20pt box does not scale and stays on the first line. The row's 44pt minimum grows with the text.

edgeCases.title: Changed on another device
edgeCases.handling: An account-level setting ticked on the phone arrives as an event and the box updates in place without stealing focus. A device-level one (Notification sound) does not sync — it is about this machine.

web.base: <button role="checkbox"> holding the box and the label, inline styles over `t`; hover, press and focus from useInteraction; `checked` through useControllable (a press also clears `indeterminate`); the tick pops in with enter("pop")
notes: Never the OS checkbox (<input type="checkbox"> with accent-color): it matches nothing in this design and differs per browser.
In forced-colors mode (Windows High Contrast) the box keeps its border in ButtonText and the tick in HighlightText on Highlight, so the state survives with no brand colour.
Pressing toggles `checked` (through useControllable, so the catalogue preview is interactive): the fill cross-fades and the tick pops in. A mixed box becomes checked and loses its dash.

keyboard.action: Toggles
Moves to the next control; a list of checkboxes is a tab stop each

desktop.base: The same <button role="checkbox"> as web, at desktop density: the 15px box with a 2px ring and a 9px tick at stroke 3.4
notes: ONE size: 15px, 2px ring, 4px corner, a 9px tick (0.6 of the box, so it fits inside the rings). There is no size prop and its absence is the feature (owner: "Checkbox sizes are diff. Need the consistency"). A bigger target grows the row's padding, never the box.

Two structural uses, one drawing: when the BOX is the control (the task table's done toggle) it is this button with hideLabel; when the ROW is the control (filter menu rows, the ⚙ menu's Notification sound) the row carries role and state and the box is an aria-hidden picture. Never nest one button in another.
Inside a menu the row is role=menuitemcheckbox with the box TRAILING the label, and clicking does not close the menu — the tick changing is the confirmation.
The round/square split is retired (ADR-0527): a round box coming back needs the owner, not a revert.
Pressing toggles `checked` and clears `indeterminate` (mixed → checked, as Radix does); the coral fill fades in over 150ms and the tick pops.

keyboard.action: Toggles

mobile.base: Pressable (accessibilityRole checkbox, checked "mixed" for the dash) over a StyleSheet from useTheme(); the box scales to 0.92 while pressed and the tick pops in through <Enter motion="pop">; `checked` through useControllable. The tick keeps the kit Icon's stroke; haptics are left to the app
notes: 20pt box, 5pt corner, 12pt tick, in a row at least 44pt tall; the whole row is the tap target.

Open decision: V2's Forward and Add participant sheets draw a ticked CIRCLE at the row's end (ADR-9416), while the desktop retired circles for the square (ADR-0527). This spec draws the square everywhere; the owner should confirm which one shape the phone keeps.
Light selection haptic on toggle.
Tapping toggles `checked` (mixed → checked); the box eases back from its 0.92 press scale while the tick pops in.

gestures.action: Toggles; the box scales to 0.92 while pressed

flows.title: Tick Make it private in New channel
Pick the conversations to forward to

chip.name: Chip
chip.description: A small labelled pill in three kinds. filter narrows a list — the phone's All · Channels · Project · DMs row — and goes ink when chosen. suggestion is the app offering something that does not exist yet: a plain card fill, a hairline, never the brand colour. object is a real saved thing: the soft brand fill with a brand edge. Any of them can carry a count or a remove ✕.

variant.description: filter narrows what you are looking at. suggestion is a prompt under the composer. object is a saved thing (a project, a saved search) and is the only chip allowed the brand colour.

selected.description: filter: the chosen filter — ink fill. suggestion: the highlighted prompt — the hover look, never the brand colour.

count.description: How many are in there — a quiet number after the label, never a brand-coloured badge. 0 draws nothing.

removable.description: Adds a ✕ with its own label ("Remove From: Priya Raman") as a second target.

removed.description: The ✕ was pressed: the chip is gone. Set by the chip's own ✕ in the catalogue; in the apps the caller drops the chip from its list on onRemove.

onSelectedChange.description: Called with `selected` as the press leaves it: flipped.

onPress.description: The chip was pressed. Its `selected` changes through `onSelectedChange`.

a11y.label: {label}
notes: A filter chip's main button exposes its state as aria-pressed (the phone: a toggle button with checked). A suggestion and an object chip are plain buttons.
The count joins the label ("DMs, 3"); the ✕ is a second button named "Remove {label}", never just "Remove".

Backspace or Delete on a removable chip removes it. When the chip that has focus goes, focus moves to the next chip, else the previous one, else the row that held it; a keyboard user is not dropped to the top of the page.
Selection is not colour alone: a chosen chip changes its fill and exposes aria-pressed. Keyboard focus draws a ring on the chip.

edgeCases.title: The row runs off the edge
edgeCases.handling: A filter row scrolls sideways rather than wrapping or shrinking chips. The last chip is allowed to run off the edge — the cut-off chip is the cue that there is more. Choosing a chip scrolls it fully into view, the gutter included.

edgeCases.title: A long label
edgeCases.handling: One line, truncated with an ellipsis at 240px; the full text is the tooltip on desktop and the accessible name everywhere. Suggestions are written to fit — the truncation is a safety net, not a layout.

edgeCases.title: A huge count
edgeCases.handling: Caps at 99+ so the chip does not grow past its neighbours; the exact number stays in the accessible name. A count is how many, not how many need you — it is never coral, even for DMs.

edgeCases.title: Removing a chip
edgeCases.handling: The ✕ is a separate target with its own name. After removal focus moves to the next chip, or to the search field when none is left, so a keyboard user is never dropped at the top of the page. The list re-filters at once; there is no confirm — adding the filter back is one step.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: No tap bounce and no scale on press; the fill still changes at once, which is the feedback.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: 33pt is a minimum: chips grow with the text and the row scrolls further. The glyph stays 16pt.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: The chosen filter's ink fill inverts to a light chip with dark text; the object chip drops its coral edge for the suggestion's and keeps the coral in its fill and label, because coral-800 reads as a dull maroon rim on dark.

edgeCases.title: Touch on a laptop
edgeCases.handling: pointer: coarse raises the chip to 36px and the ✕ to a 32px target; hover fills still apply to a mouse on the same device.

web.base: A row holding two sibling <button>s — the chip (aria-pressed on a filter) and its ✕ — never nested; inline styles over `t`, the root taking the hover and press of either; `selected` through useControllable; Backspace / Delete on a removable chip removes it
notes: A single-choice filter row is a ToggleGroup (or tablist when it switches a list in place); a multi-choice row is independent Toggles with aria-pressed.
The ✕ is its own button, never inside the chip's button — nested buttons are invalid HTML and the parser splits them.
Pressing the chip toggles `selected` and the ink fill fades in; pressing the ✕ sets `removed` and the chip goes. Both are `on.press` actions, so the catalogue preview is interactive.

keyboard.action: Activates the chip
On a focused removable chip, removes it and moves focus to the next chip, or to the search field if none is left
Moves between chips in a filter row (roving focus)

desktop.base: The same two-button row as web, at desktop density (34px)
notes: suggestion is the search field's resting box, token for token: --border-subtle hairline, --radius-control, --shadow-hairline in every state. Hover moves the fill and nothing else — no coral, in hover or active (ADR-0322).
Home's three suggestion chips share the row EQUALLY (flex 1 1 0, min-width fit-content), so a narrow row wraps instead of clipping. object chips do not take an equal share.
object is coral-soft with a coral-200 edge in Light; in Dark it wears the suggestion's edge and keeps the coral in the fill and label.
Desktop has no filter chips today — the command palette's kind filter is ChoicePills (radio-group pills). Filter chips arrive with search filters (From:, In:).
Pressing toggles `selected` (150ms fill and ink cross-fade); the ✕ sets `removed`, and the caller drops the chip on onRemove.

keyboard.action: Activates
Removes a focused removable chip

mobile.base: A View with a Pressable chip (togglebutton for a filter) and a Pressable ✕ with hitSlop, StyleSheet over useTheme(); the 0.96 press bounce; `selected` through useControllable. The scrolling filter row is the caller's
notes: A 33pt pill: a 16pt glyph and a 14pt label 8 apart, 16 either side, and a 1pt Rim drawn over the edge so it takes no room.
Chosen is ink (surfaceInverse) with inverse ink; the rest are white with text.faint. Coral until the V2 Figma of 2026-10-16 (ADR-9406).
The fill does NOT travel between chips: the chosen chip fills itself at once and the tapped chip gives a small bounce. A sliding pill was tried and turned down ("No smooth motion").
The row scrolls sideways (at 393pt the last chip runs off the edge) and choosing a chip scrolls it fully into view.
Tapping toggles `selected`, with the 0.96 press bounce; the ✕ sets `removed`.

gestures.action: Chooses the filter with a small bounce (none under Reduce Motion)
Scrolls the row
Removes; the ✕ has a 44pt hitSlop

flows.title: Filter Messages with the chip row
A suggestion chip asks Fabric

combo-chart.name: ComboChart
combo-chart.description: What happened as bars, and what was expected as a dashed line over them, with an optional target line: revenue against its forecast, tickets against capacity. One card, one legend with a switch for each, one tooltip with both numbers. It is the common composed chart; a chart with more parts is written with the library and the same chart tokens (`rechartsTheme()`, `giftedTheme()`).

headingLevel.description: The heading level of the card's title, 1 to 6, so the chart keeps the page's heading order: a card under an h2 is an h3, one under an h1 is an h2. The phone has one kind of header and reads it for nothing. The card is not a landmark: the figure inside is named by the summary.

data.description: Rows, one per category: [{ month: 1777593600000, mrr: 152400, forecast: 150000 }, …]. The same rows can feed a table, a stat and a line chart.

x.description: The field of each row that is the category: a date or a word.

bars.description: The field drawn as bars: what happened. Bars keep zero.

line.description: The field drawn as a dashed line across the bars, with a dot on each point: a forecast, a plan, a capacity.

title.description: The card's title. It names the figure on the page, and is the first words of what a screen reader hears.

subtitle.description: One line under the title: what it covers. Empty draws none.
subtitle.sample: Bars, a dashed line and a target

headline.description: A number to lead with, under the title: { value, format, delta, deltaFormat, inverse, period }. It is a MetricValue (in the chart's format unless it names one), a Delta badge and what the change is against ("resolved in October"). Left out, the card has none.

format.description: A format name, its options or a function: what core's `fmt` takes. The axis, the labels at the ends of bars, the tooltip, the summary and "View as table" all print through it, so they agree.

xFormat.description: The category's format, for a date: "month", "day", or options such as { type: "month", timeZone: "UTC" }. A timestamp under a date format is read as a point in time, so the summary reads as a trend. Left out, the category prints as it is.

labels.description: A field's name for people, for the legend, the tooltip and the table's headers: { opened: "Opened" }. A field with no entry prints its own name.

height.description: The plot's height, in px (points on the phone). The card is as wide as the space it is given.

empty.description: The title of the empty state when there are no rows. Say why: nothing yet and nothing matching a filter are different sentences.

emptyLine.description: One sentence under it: what to do about it.

loading.description: Grey bars of uneven heights in place of the plot, from the kit's Skeleton, and no "View as table". The header stays, so the card does not jump when the data arrives. Screen readers hear "Loading chart" once.

hidden.description: The series the legend has turned off, by field: ["resolved"]. Left out, the chart keeps its own, starting with every series on. Controlled when the app passes it with `onHiddenChange`.

onHiddenChange.description: A legend entry was pressed. Called with every series that is off now. The last series showing cannot be turned off, so pressing it calls nothing.

target.description: A reference line at this value: a goal. The scale takes it in. Left out, there is none.

targetLabel.description: What the target line says, at its left end: "Q4 target $180K". Empty draws a line with no words.

a11y.label: The summary: "Revenue against forecast, May to Oct: MRR rose from $152.4K to $184.2K, highest in Oct; Forecast rose from $150K to $185K, highest in Oct."
notes: The figure is named by the sentence core's `summarize` writes from the rows; it is heard, not printed, and the tooltip and "View as table" give the numbers without colour. Bars and a dashed line differ in more than colour, so the two are told apart without it.
"View as table" shows the same rows in Table: the bars' field and the line's, as columns.
The legend says what it toggles: a button per series, pressed while it is on, struck through when it is off. The last one showing cannot be turned off.
The target line is labelled in words at its end, and is in the summary's scale, so a goal above every bar still shows.
On the web the plot is a stop for the arrow keys (recharts' accessibility layer): the tooltip moves category to category, and the plot draws a focus edge while the keyboard is in it.

examples.name: Revenue against forecast
examples.description: MRR as bars, the forecast as a dashed line, and Q4's target.

props.title: Revenue against forecast
props.subtitle: Bars, a dashed line and a target

examples.name: With a headline
examples.description: The number the card leads with, and how it moved.

examples.name: The forecast turned off
examples.description: `hidden` is the legend's state: the line is off and the entry is struck through, but the axis does not move.

edgeCases.title: No rows
edgeCases.handling: An empty `data` draws the kit's EmptyState in the plot's place and says why; the card keeps its header and has no "View as table" and no legend.

edgeCases.title: One category
edgeCases.handling: One row draws one bar and the line's single point as a dot on it. The summary says what each is, not a trend.

edgeCases.title: A forecast under the actuals
edgeCases.handling: Nothing assumes the line is above the bars: they share one axis, and the tooltip lists both numbers whichever is bigger.

edgeCases.title: A target outside the data
edgeCases.handling: The scale takes the target in, so a goal above every bar still draws, and its label stays inside the plot.

edgeCases.title: Loading
edgeCases.handling: Grey bars of uneven heights fill the plot and the card keeps its header. There is no legend, no table button and no summary yet.

web.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a <section>: the title, an optional headline, "View as table" (Button); a ChartFrame holding recharts' ComposedChart with a Bar, a dashed Line behind it (its dots over the bars) and a ReferenceLine; the Legend (toggle buttons) in the header beside the Button, as the reference dashboard has it
notes: Shipped from the data subpath: recharts is reached only from there. The chart is handed an explicit width and height.

The same `rechartsTheme(useChartTokens(), useReducedMotion())` as LineChart and BarChart, exported beside the chart: the grid, axes, bar and line geometry and the dash patterns are the tokens', so a ComposedChart written with recharts matches this one.
Both series are in the scale whether or not the legend has them on, so turning the line off does not make the axis jump.

The line is drawn as PeriodCompare's last period is (`chart.previousW`, the series dash, round ends) and behind the bars (in recharts' own area layer, over the grid and under the bars), so a bar keeps its own top where the two meet. Its dots stay over the bars: solid in the line's colour, ringed by the card.
ComposedChart draws its cursor as a line whatever it is given, so the hovered category is marked by the line charts' dashed crosshair, not BarChart's wash.

keyboard.action: Moves into the plot, then on to the legend's entries and "View as table"
In the plot: moves the tooltip to the next category
In the plot: moves the tooltip to the previous category
On a legend entry: turns the series off or back on

desktop.base: The same Card, recharts' ComposedChart and Legend as web, at desktop density

keyboard.action: Moves into the plot, then on to the legend's entries and "View as table"
In the plot: moves the tooltip to the next category
In the plot: moves the tooltip to the previous category
On a legend entry: turns the series off or back on

mobile.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a View: the same header and Button, a ChartFrame holding react-native-gifted-charts' BarChart with `showLine`, `lineData` and `lineConfig` for the dashed line, `lineData2` and `lineConfig2` for its dots, `referenceLine1` for the target and `renderTooltip` for the card; the Legend's toggles above the plot
notes: `giftedTheme(useChartTokens())` is the chart tokens as gifted-charts' own props, exported beside the chart; a chart the kit does not ship, written with gifted-charts and the same call, matches this one.

The line is drawn by the bar chart over the bars, as PeriodCompare's last period is (`chart.previousW`, dashed). gifted-charts draws a point as one circle with no stroke, so each dot is two: a disc of the card on the first line, and the dot in the line's colour on a second line that draws no stroke.
The points sit on the bars' centres: gifted-charts steps a line by a bar's width plus its `spacing`, so the kit passes the gap between bars, not the whole category.
The line draws in with the bars unless the person reduces motion. Under react-native-web (the catalogue, `pnpm check`) gifted-charts' animation is off.

gestures.action: Focuses its category: the tooltip card shows both numbers
Turns the series off or back on

command-palette.name: Command palette
command-palette.description: ⌘K: one field that finds people, channels, projects, meetings and actions, grouped, with recent picks first. It drops from the top so the field never moves as results change, and Enter with no match hands the question to Fabric instead of failing.

placeholder.description: The field's placeholder. Default: the `placeholder` string ("Search"); AntFabric's copy says "Search people, channels, projects, or DM someone…".

filters.description: The filter pills under the field, one per entry. Empty draws no filter row. AntFabric's are its kinds; All is the resting state, not a fifth filter.

filter.description: The pill that is on. A value no filter names leaves all of them off.

selected.description: The key of the highlighted row, when it has moved off the row groups marks selected (pressing or arrowing to a row). Empty follows each row's own selected.

ask.description: Enter asks the agent when nothing matches: the ask row, the hint along the foot and the empty state's "Press Enter to ask". Off, the empty state is "No matches" and the foot has no hint.

agentName.description: The agent's name. It only words the ask row, the empty state and the foot's hint, and names the agent's face; `ask` is what shows them.

groups.description: Result groups in order: Recent (only while the query is empty), People, Channels, Projects, Meetings, Actions. Each { key?, label, items }; an item is { key, label, hint, icon, avatar, identity, presence, agent, status, shortcut, webShortcut, selected }: avatar draws the label's face in the slot instead of icon.

loading.description: The directory is still answering. Rows already known (from the cache) stay; a Searching row sits under them.

showHints.description: The keyboard hint strip at the foot.

onAsk.description: Enter with no row selected: the query goes to the agent (with `ask` on, named by agentName).

a11y.label: Command palette
notes: The field is a combobox controlling the results listbox (aria-expanded is true while there are results or the ask row); rows are options with aria-selected, and aria-activedescendant moves with the arrows (to the ask row when it is the only row) so focus never leaves the field.

Each group is a group named by its label. The number of results is announced politely 400 ms after typing pauses ("6 results", through the page's one polite live region), never per keystroke; the empty state says its own words in a status.
Avatars and glyphs are decorative; a row's name says its kind: "release-train, Channel".

Focus moves to the field when the palette mounts, Tab stays inside the panel, Esc clears the query and then closes, and focus returns to the opener when the palette unmounts. The Esc chip, the footer hints and the busy spinners are hidden from assistive tech (the loading line says it).

examples.name: Opened, nothing typed
examples.description: Recent first, then each kind, then actions.

edgeCases.title: Nothing matches
edgeCases.handling: Not a dead end: the empty state says so and offers Ask Fabric as the selected row, so Enter sends the query to the assistant. Copy: "No matches. Press Enter to ask Fabric".

edgeCases.title: The directory is slow
edgeCases.handling: Channels and projects come from the local cache at once; people wait on the directory. After 300 ms a "Searching people…" row appears under what is known (and stays at least 400 ms). After 8 s it reads "Still searching — showing people on this device". The highlight never jumps when late rows arrive above it: it stays on the row it was on.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: The desktop searches its SQLite cache and says so in one line; the web searches what this tab already loaded. Opening a result works from the cache; Ask Fabric is disabled until the connection returns.

edgeCases.title: Typing with an input method (Japanese, Chinese, Korean)
edgeCases.handling: Enter during composition (isComposing, or keyCode 229 in WebKit) commits the characters and never runs a row; search runs on the committed text only, so a half-composed query does not flash results.

edgeCases.title: Ctrl+K belongs to the browser
edgeCases.handling: The page claims Ctrl+K when it has focus; when it does not (address bar focused, devtools, fresh tab never clicked) the browser's search wins. / is the fallback no browser owns, and the rail's search field always works. Never advertise a shortcut that only sometimes works without its alternative beside it.

edgeCases.title: Changing the filter
edgeCases.handling: The highlight resets to the first row. Kept at its old index, it would land on a different row than the one it was on, and Enter would open that.

edgeCases.title: A recent that no longer exists
edgeCases.handling: A channel you left, an archived project, a deactivated person: recents resolve through the live rows, so they drop out silently instead of rendering a row that opens nothing. The recent is pruned on the next save.

edgeCases.title: Long names and statuses
edgeCases.handling: The status truncates first, then the name; the kind hint on the right never truncates. Rows keep one height.

edgeCases.title: Opened while something else is open
edgeCases.handling: Mod+K does nothing while a modal dialog is open — the dialog owns the keyboard. An open menu closes on the way in. The shortcuts card (Mod+/) closes the palette on its way in, so the two are never stacked.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion, dark mode
edgeCases.handling: With reduced motion the panel appears without the rise. In dark mode the highlight is the dark hover surface, and an avatar's presence ring follows the row's background so the selected row never shows a pale disc behind the dot.

web.base: A <div role="dialog"> on a 5px-blurred scrim: a combobox <input> (aria-activedescendant) over a role="listbox" of option <button>s in labelled groups, with Avatar, Icon and Kbd in the rows; inline styles over `t`; ↑ ↓ Enter and Esc in the field; `query` through useControllable(query, onQueryChange) and `filter` through useControllable(filter, onFilterChange), `selected` kept inside; pops in with enter("pop")
notes: Mod+K on Windows and Linux is Ctrl+K, which Chrome and Edge bind to "search the web" in the address bar and Firefox to its search field. A focused page can claim it, so the web listens on window in the capture phase and calls preventDefault — but the browser still wins whenever focus is in its own chrome (address bar, devtools) or the page has not been clicked since load.

So the web also opens the palette with / whenever focus is not in a text field — a key no browser binds — and the search field in the rail is always one click away. The rail's tooltip names both: "Search (Ctrl+K or /)".
Rows whose desktop shortcut the browser owns show the web alternative: New message is ⌘N on desktop (a new browser window on the web), so the web draws Mod+Alt+N.
Recents live in localStorage for this origin and sync across open tabs through the storage event; opening the palette in one tab never opens it in another.
Below 640px of viewport it is a full-screen search page, not a floating panel.

keyboard.action: Opens (Mod+K toggles); / works only when focus is not in a text field
Moves the highlighted row across groups; focus stays in the field (aria-activedescendant)
Opens the highlighted row, or asks Fabric when nothing matches
Clears the query if there is one, otherwise closes and returns focus

desktop.base: The same dialog as web at desktop density, drawing the desktop shortcut rather than webShortcut
notes: Drops from 14vh instead of centring, so the field stays put as the result count changes under it.
Width is W_MODAL, imported rather than copied — the value moved five times in two days, and a literal here would have been left behind at every step. Height caps at 70vh and the list scrolls.
Rows are one fixed height: a person's status sits inline after the name, never on a second line, so the list does not jump while typing.
Recents come from lib/palette-recents (app data on disk) and resolve back through the live rows, so a recent that no longer exists cannot render.
The rail's search field ("Search people, channels, projects (⌘K)") opens the same palette.
In the catalogue the panel pops in over a fading scrim; pressing a kind pill sets `filter` and pressing a row moves the highlight to it (`selected`). Opening the row is the kit's.
This spec adds the Actions group, the Ask Fabric row on no match, the footer hints and the offline note; today the empty state is the line "No matches. Press Enter to ask Fabric" alone.

keyboard.action: Toggles the palette from anywhere, including inside the composer
Moves the highlight; hovering a row moves the same highlight, so pointing and arrowing never disagree
Runs the highlighted row and records it as a recent; with no match, hands the query to Fabric
Closes

mobile.alternative: A phone has no ⌘K and no floating palette. Search is the field at the top of the Messages tab ("Search Conversations", and "Search Channels", "Search Project Channels", "Search DMs" on each filter), which narrows the list by name and project tag — never by message text, because the platform has no message-search endpoint. Finding a person to message is the New message sheet; a question in words goes to Fabric on the Assistant tab.

flows.title: ⌘K, type a few letters, open a channel
No match hands the question to Fabric

composer.name: Composer
composer.description: Where a message is written. On web and desktop it is the rich input with a formatting toolbar, attach, emoji, @mention and send; on the phone it is the ComposerBar that rides the keyboard. It knows when it cannot send — empty, uploading, too long, offline, read-only, archived — and says why.

placeholder.description: "Message #<channel>", "Message <person>" in a DM, "Reply…" in a thread, "Edit message" while editing.

value.description: The draft. Kept per conversation, across channel switches and restarts.

mode.description: editing: changing one of your messages. thread: the reply box, with "Also send to #channel". offline: sends refused, draft kept. readonly / archived: no box at all, a notice instead.

sendKey.description: Preferences → Messages: Enter sends and Shift+Enter is a new line (default), or Mod+Enter sends and Enter is a new line. Mod+Enter always sends in both.

uploading.description: A staged file is still uploading. Send waits for it.

attachments.description: Staged files, links and voice notes, as Attachment { key, kind, name, fileType, badge, typeLabel, size, status, progress, src, title, domain, description, url, duration }, drawn as attachment cards above the text: every field reaches the card, as Message passes it.

lengthHint.description: Silent until the draft is within 1,000 of the 16,000-character limit: "1,000 left", then "240 over".

tooLong.description: Past the limit: the hint turns red and Send is disabled.

alsoSend.description: Thread only: also post this reply to the channel.

alsoSendTo.description: The conversation the reply would also go to.

formatting.description: Web and desktop: the formatting toolbar above the text (can be hidden from Preferences; the shortcuts still work). Phone: the Formatting button beside Attach.

commands.description: The slash-command button. Hidden while editing.

record.description: The mic beside Send. Hidden while editing, disabled offline.

tools.description: The product's own tools: IconActionItem { key, label, icon, badge?, disabled? }, drawn as icon buttons after the built-in ones and before Send. The icon is required: a product's tool cannot draw a blank button.

focused.description: Draws the focused edge (the catalogue cannot focus).

disabled.description: The composer takes no input: the field and every tool are disabled, and Send waits.

maxLength.description: The most characters the field takes, enforced by the platform. Pair it with lengthHint to show how many are left.

autoFocus.description: Focuses the field when the composer mounts (after Reply or Edit opens it). Not under a host that draws overlays as pictures.

avoidKeyboard.description: Lifts the composer above the keyboard (a KeyboardAvoidingView, padding on iOS). Off by default: a screen that already resizes for the keyboard must not do it twice. Home-indicator spacing is the screen's (SafeAreaView or safe-area insets around the composer).

onValueChange.description: The draft as it is typed, and "" when Send clears it. Given `value` too, the box is controlled (the app keeps the draft per conversation); otherwise it keeps its own.

onAlsoSendChange.description: Thread only: called with `alsoSend` as a press on "Also send to" leaves it.

onSend.description: Enter (per sendKey), Mod+Enter, or Send, with a sendable draft: the words as typed. The box clears in the same tick. Save while editing.

onAttach.description: Desktop/web: the file picker (multiple). Mobile: the "Add to your message" sheet — Upload File, Upload Image, Take Photo.

onRecord.description: The mic is pressed: the app's recorder takes over (hold to record, slide to cancel).

onEmoji.description: The Emoji button was pressed: the app opens its picker.

onMention.description: The Mention someone button was pressed: the app opens its picker.

onCommands.description: The slash-command button was pressed: the app opens its command list.

onFormat.description: A formatting button was pressed (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, link, ordered-list, bulleted-list, code, code-block): the app wraps the selection.

onFormatting.description: The Formatting button was pressed: the app opens its formatting face.

onAction.description: A product tool was pressed. Called with the whole item, so the product switches on `action.key`.

onAttachmentOpen.description: A staged attachment's card was pressed: the app opens its preview.

onAttachmentDownload.description: A staged attachment's download was pressed.

onAttachmentCancel.description: A staged attachment's remove (or cancel, while it uploads) was pressed: the app takes it out of `attachments`.

onAttachmentRetry.description: A failed attachment's Retry was pressed: the app starts its upload again. Given this, the card is controlled by the attachment's own `status`.

notes: The text box is labelled by its purpose ("Message", "Thread reply", "Edit message"); on the phone the placeholder is its hint, so the channel name is heard too.
Send exposes its disabled state. Pressing Send or Enter while a file uploads announces "Waiting for the upload to finish"; the hint under the box says the same.
The length counter is drawn, not read on every keystroke: it is announced when the draft crosses 100, 50 and 10 characters left, and when it goes over.
The formatting toolbar is one group: arrow keys, Home and End move between its buttons (web and desktop).
The offline line is a polite live region, so a screen-reader user hears why the send did not go.
Read-only and archived notices replace the box entirely, so there is no field to land in that cannot be used.
`disabled` disables the field and every tool. On the phone the toolbar buttons are 36pt drawn with a touch area that stops short of 44pt until IconButton grows its hit area from the drawn size.
