edgeCases.title: Pressing Enter while composing in an IME
edgeCases.handling: Enter that commits a Japanese, Chinese or Korean composition (isComposing / keyCode 229) never sends. Only an Enter after composition ends does.

edgeCases.title: A picker is open
edgeCases.handling: While the @, #, : or / picker has candidates, Enter and Tab choose the highlighted one and Escape closes it; nothing sends. On mobile the pickers are sheets above the keyboard and the bar's buttons open them directly.

edgeCases.title: Double press on Send
edgeCases.handling: The box is cleared and Send disabled in the same tick as the press, before the request; the message carries a client id so a network retry cannot post it twice.

edgeCases.title: Offline, then back
edgeCases.handling: Typing is never blocked offline. Send is refused with the plain sentence and the draft stays exactly as typed; when the connection returns the notice goes and Send lights up again. Nothing is sent automatically from the composer — a message you could not see leave should not leave on its own.

edgeCases.title: Edit that empties the message
edgeCases.handling: Saving an edit with no text left asks "Delete this message?" instead of posting an empty edit. Esc (or Cancel on mobile) restores the original and leaves the draft that was in the box before editing untouched.

edgeCases.title: Session expired or removed from the channel
edgeCases.handling: A 401 refuses the send with "Your session expired. Sign in again." and keeps the draft for after sign-in. Removed from a private channel mid-draft: the box is replaced by "You are not in this channel." and the draft is kept locally for a day.

edgeCases.title: Microphone denied
edgeCases.handling: Holding the mic with permission denied shows "AntFabric can't use the microphone. Allow it in Settings." with Open Settings; it never re-prompts in a loop. The mic stays visible so the reason is discoverable.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: The 112pt cap holds, so fewer lines show and the field scrolls inside; the bar's 36pt targets do not shrink and the formatting face scrolls horizontally rather than pushing Send off the card.

edgeCases.title: Narrow pane
edgeCases.handling: Under 420px the formatting toolbar collapses behind an Aa button (as on mobile) and the hint below is dropped; Send and the counter never move.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: The box takes dir=auto from its first strong character, so an Arabic message is typed right-to-left in an English workspace; the toolbar and Send mirror with the UI direction, and the send glyph flips.

web.base: A plain <textarea data-af-input> (field-sizing: content, and a measured height as a fallback) in a card drawn with inline styles over `t`; the toolbar and footer are the kit's IconButton, staged files the kit's AttachmentCard (compact). Enter / Shift+Enter / Mod+Enter / Escape on the textarea, IME-safe. Rich text, the emoji panel and the @ / # / : / slash pickers are the app's.
notes: Centred at clamp(680px, 34vw, 880px) — the desktop's --content-w-composer — so a 2560px window does not stretch a line of text across the screen.

Drafts are saved to IndexedDB per workspace and conversation on every pause in typing, so a reload or a crashed tab keeps them. Two tabs on one channel share the draft (BroadcastChannel); the last edit wins.
Closing the tab with an unsent draft does not warn (it is saved); closing it mid-upload does (beforeunload).
Shortcuts the browser owns are never used: link is Mod+Shift+K because Mod+K is the quick switcher, and nothing here uses ⌘W / ⌘T / ⌘N / ⌘L.
Paste of an image or file stages it; dropping files anywhere on the conversation shows "Drop files to attach to #platform-eng".

Not in the kit yet: formatting marks and their shortcuts (the toolbar draws but does nothing on a plain textarea), the emoji, @ / # / : and slash pickers, ↑ to edit your last message, paste and drop staging, and the Aa collapse under 420px.

keyboard.action: Sends (Enter-sends setting); picks the highlighted person when the @ picker is open
New line; inside a list, the next item — an empty item leaves the list
Always sends
Bold / italic / underline
Strikethrough
Inline code
Add a link
In an empty box: edit your last message
Closes a picker; while editing, cancels the edit

desktop.base: The same file as web (one component): the textarea grows 22–220px, then scrolls; IconButton footer; ⌘ glyphs in the hints from usePlatform().os. The RichInput, EmojiPanel and MentionPicker are the app's.
notes: Footer today: + Attach files, Insert emoji, Mention someone, Slash command, the silent-until-needed LengthCounter, and a Send that turns into a coral circle once there is something to send (ADR-8930).
The channel composer spans the pane today (padding 0 18 16); the clamp width is what Home and Fabric use. Confirm whether channels should adopt it.

Offline (ADR-0704): Enter is refused with "You're offline. Your message wasn't sent. It's still here for when you're back." and the draft stays. The typing slot above says AntFabric is offline for as long as it is.
Drafts live in the SQLite cache per conversation and survive quitting the app and close-to-tray.
Uploads go up on pick, not on send, so a large file never makes Enter feel broken; Send waits ("Waiting for the upload to finish").

In the catalogue, Send clears `value` when the draft is sendable (the coral circle goes back to a faint glyph), and the thread's 'Also send to' row toggles `alsoSend`. The editing and offline lines rise in above the box.

keyboard.action: Sends (or picks in an open picker)
New line, list-aware
Always sends
Bold / italic / underline / code
Add a link
In an empty box: edit your last message
Closes a picker, then cancels an edit

mobile.base: A multiline TextInput (34–112pt, then it scrolls) in a View (radius 20) + the bar of the kit's IconButtons at 36pt with no gaps; staged files are the kit's AttachmentCard (compact). Keyboard avoidance and haptics are the screen's.
notes: Keyboard-aware: the composer rides the keyboard (useKeyboardInset), sits on the home-indicator inset when it is down, and tapping the timeline dismisses the keyboard without losing the draft.

Grows from one line to 112pt, then scrolls inside. Today's channel composer grows to 20% of the screen (4–8 lines, models/composerHeight.ts) and the Fabric composer stops at 112 — this spec uses 112 everywhere; confirm with design.
Return inserts a new line; only the Send button sends. With a hardware keyboard on iPad, Enter sends and Shift+Enter is a new line, as on desktop.

The bar: + opens "Add to your message" (Upload File, Upload Image, Take Photo); Aa swaps the bar to the formatting face (B I U S, lists, link) with a 180 ms slide; ☺ emoji; @ mention; / commands; the mic records a voice note (new — the app has no voice notes yet).
Idle Send is a bare faint glyph; only a sendable draft lights the coral circle. Editing swaps it for a check labelled Save.

Offline the phone refuses the send ("You're offline, so this hasn't been sent. It's still here.") and keeps the text; the line above the composer says AntFabric is offline, after a 5 s grace so a blip never flashes.
Not in the kit yet: the Aa formatting face, Enter-sends on an iPad hardware keyboard, and the mic's hold-to-record gesture (a tap calls onRecord; the recorder is the app's).

gestures.action: Sends; light haptic. Disabled (no response) when there is nothing sendable
Records a voice note; slide left to cancel, release to stage it
Dismisses the keyboard interactively

flows.title: Send a message
Offline: the send is refused and the draft stays

connection-banner.name: Connection banner
connection-banner.description: Says what the connection is doing, quietly, for as long as it is true: the desktop's amber offline strip, the phone's offline / back-online / syncing card and Online pill, a reconnecting line with the attempt count, and the degraded-service note when names cannot be resolved.

state.description: offline: this device has no network. reconnecting: the network is there but AntFabric is not answering. degraded: connected, but one service (the directory) is failing.

surface.description: pill is the phone header's Online / Offline indicator; it is read-only.

attempt.description: Reconnect attempt number. Shown from the second attempt.

pending.description: Things waiting to sync (AntFabric: recordings waiting to upload). Changes what offline and back-online say.

onRetry.description: Try now was pressed: reconnect at once and reset the backoff. The phone has no Retry; its queue drains on the reconnect edge.

notes: A change of state is spoken politely, never interrupting, and never as an alert: nothing here is an error. On the web the strip's message, the degraded note and "Back online" go through the page's own announcer when the state changes (a strip mounted holding its text is not read, and the way back would otherwise be silent). On the phone the card's title and message are spoken by the screen reader's announcement call, and the card is role=status.

The pill is a status element that stays on the page, so its text changing is read: web role=status with aria-live=polite, on the phone role=status and an announcement of its new name. Its label is a sentence ("No connection to the backend"), not the colour.
The strip's spinner is hidden from assistive technology; the message says what is happening.

edgeCases.title: A blip is not offline
edgeCases.handling: Nothing is shown for the first 5 s of a socket drop (OFFLINE_GRACE_MS). A dev server restart, a wake reconnect (250 ms) or a gateway redeploy never flashes the strip or raises the offline toast. Sends inside the grace still go over REST; the grace holds the announcement, never the work.

edgeCases.title: Coming back
edgeCases.handling: Web and desktop say nothing — the strip leaving is the signal, and a resync runs with its own "Refreshing…" toast only when the person asked for one. The phone says "Back online" for 5 s, with "Meeting synced · AI processing started" only if a recording was waiting.

edgeCases.title: Reconnecting for a long time
edgeCases.handling: Backoff runs 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s … up to 30 s between attempts; the line shows the attempt number from the second one and Try now resets the backoff. The strip never escalates to a modal: the workspace under it stays usable from what is on the device.

edgeCases.title: Trying to send while offline
edgeCases.handling: Refused, not queued, with the draft kept: "You're offline. Your message wasn't sent. It's still here for when you're back." A send that silently waits cannot be told from one that was lost.

edgeCases.title: An expired session is not offline
edgeCases.handling: The socket's 4401 and a confirmed 401 go to the sign-in flow (Session state), never to this strip. Showing "Reconnecting…" to someone whose session ended would keep them waiting for something that cannot happen.

edgeCases.title: One service failing
edgeCases.handling: When the directory read fails, names fall back to "Unknown user" and this note sits above the conversation list. It has no close button and names no cause (a 403, a 500 and a timeout look the same here); it goes away by itself when the 5-minute refresh succeeds.

edgeCases.title: Narrow windows and 130% text
edgeCases.handling: The strip wraps to two centred lines rather than truncating — the second half of the sentence ("will reconnect on its own") is the reassurance. On a phone the card grows with Dynamic Type.

web.base: A role="status" strip, inline styles over `t`, that slides down with enter("slide-down"); Try now is a <button> with hover and focus from useInteraction. The app feeds `state` from navigator.onLine, the online/offline events and the realtime socket
notes: Two signals, two states: the browser's offline event means the device has no network and shows "You're offline" at once; a socket that drops while navigator.onLine is true waits out the 5 s grace and then says "Reconnecting…", because the network is fine and AntFabric is not.
No device cache on the web: offline shows what was already loaded in this tab, and says so.

keyboard.action: On Try now: reconnects immediately and resets the backoff

desktop.base: The same role="status" strip as web, in warning.soft over a warning.border edge, for inside the content column (never across the rail); the degraded note is a recessed card for the sidebar above the conversation list
notes: Amber and centred on purpose (owner, 2026-09-22): amber is degraded-but-working; not danger, because nothing failed; not coral, because the strip asks for no action.
Dark themes wash the amber anchor at 10% with a 25% edge instead of the light ramp — the desktop's --banner-warning-* tokens carry both. Here warning.soft and warning.border carry both themes.
Nothing is said on the way back: the strip going away is the signal.
Reconnecting with an attempt count and Try now is new; today the strip covers both cases with the offline sentence.
The composer has its own line for this (OFFLINE_NOTICE, where "X is typing…" sits); this strip is for every other screen.
The strip slides down into place when it appears. Try now starts a fresh attempt at once, so the count moves on (it sets `attempt` + 1 in the catalogue).

mobile.base: <Enter motion="slide-down"> card (role status, polite live region) with an Icon and two Texts, StyleSheet over useTheme(), for under the screen header; the pill is a read-only labelled View for HeaderActions
notes: Offline is a normal mode for a capture app, so it reads as reassurance on a neutral surface — no alarm colour, no Retry: the capture queue drains itself on the reconnect edge.
"Back online" stays 5 s (RECONNECT_NOTICE_MS) and only claims a sync when something was waiting.
The card slides down into place when it appears.
The pill is read-only. It used to be a tap-to-force-offline toggle, which pinned the app offline; that override is gone.
The phone refuses sends while offline; the draft stays in the composer.

flows.title: The connection drops, the strip says so, and goes when it's back
Reconnecting: try now instead of waiting

context-menu.name: Context menu
context-menu.description: What you can do to the thing under the pointer or finger. A right-click on web and desktop opens our own menu at the pointer; a long-press on a phone opens the message actions sheet. Same quick reactions and the same rows on all three, in the same order.

quickReactions.description: The quick set, as emoji, in order. Empty draws no reaction row and no +. AntFabric's set is six — the same list doubles as "frequently used" at the top of the full emoji panel.

picked.description: Which of quickReactions are the person's own, as emoji: pressing one takes its emoji out, pressing another puts it in (and both call onReact). In the kits pressing a reaction calls onReact and the menu closes.

items.description: Menu rows, in Menu's item shape. Every row is gated by what the server allows (abilitiesFor); a delete you cannot do is a disabled row that says why.

label.description: The rows' accessible name. Default: the `actions` string ("Actions").

title.description: The sheet's title on the phone, and its accessible name. Empty draws none and the sheet is named by label.

picking.description: The full emoji panel is open under the quick set (the + was pressed).

showTarget.description: Draws the message that was right-clicked, highlighted, with the menu at the pointer.

body.sample: Release train is cut: 4.12.0 is on staging. Smoke tests start at 3.

a11y.label: Message actions
notes: Quick reactions are toggle buttons with aria-pressed, named "React with 👍" / "Remove your 👍".
Long-press is not discoverable with VoiceOver or TalkBack, so the message row exposes the same actions as accessibility actions (rotor / actions menu); "Message actions" opens this sheet.

Phone: the sheet is a modal view; Android's back button closes it, screen-reader focus starts at the title (else the handle), the handle's touch area is the 44pt target, the emoji panel's search field is lifted above the keyboard on iOS, and each emoji in the panel is a pressable button that reacts. The panel's emoji lists are the kit's own fixed sets and the search field filters nothing yet.

On web and desktop the menu rows are a Menu: focus moves to the first enabled row when the menu mounts, ↑ ↓ Home End and type-ahead move between rows, Esc closes, and focus returns to what had it (the message it was opened on) when the menu unmounts.

examples.name: Someone else's message
examples.description: No Edit, no Delete; Forward and Pin stay.

props.author: Amara Okafor
props.body: Can someone from #design-crit look at the onboarding copy before Friday?

edgeCases.title: Right-click in a text field or on selected text
edgeCases.handling: The system's text menu opens, never ours: Cut, Copy, Paste, spelling suggestions and writing tools belong to the OS. The test walks up from the target, so a mention chip or bold run inside the composer counts as text. A disabled or read-only field is not text entry and gets nothing.

edgeCases.title: Right-click where there are no actions
edgeCases.handling: Nothing opens. The WKWebView's own menu (Reload, Back, Inspect Element, Open Link in New Window) is suppressed in the capture phase everywhere outside text entry — Reload would throw away the workspace's whole in-memory state, and the menu tells people they are looking at a web page.

edgeCases.title: Past the 12-hour delete window
edgeCases.handling: Delete stays, disabled, with the reason as its second line. The phone used to draw a faint note in its place; one rule everywhere is simpler: an option that vanishes teaches nothing.

edgeCases.title: A reply inside a thread
edgeCases.handling: No "Reply in thread": a thread is one level deep and the server answers 400 thread_depth to a reply's reply. Two tests decide it — the surface passes no reply handler, and the message's own ability says it cannot carry a thread — so the row cannot leak onto a reply drawn somewhere else.

edgeCases.title: A message with no text
edgeCases.handling: A message that is only an attachment or a meeting card has no Copy text row; the attachment's own menu offers Download and Copy link instead.

edgeCases.title: The message changes on another device while the menu is open
edgeCases.handling: Deleted elsewhere: the menu closes and the row shows "This message was deleted." Edited elsewhere: the menu stays, and Edit opens the latest text, never the version under the pointer when it opened.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Copy text and Forward (which only opens the picker) stay. Reactions, Edit, Pin and Delete are disabled with "You're offline" as the sublabel; the phone refuses writes while offline and the desktop does not queue destructive ones.

edgeCases.title: Opened near the window edge
edgeCases.handling: Anchored at the pointer, then flipped on whichever axis would overflow (left of the pointer at the right edge, above it at the bottom) and shifted to stay 8px inside the window.

edgeCases.title: Long-press while scrolling, or on a link
edgeCases.handling: The press only counts if the finger stays within 10pt for 400 ms, so a scroll never opens the sheet. A long-press on a link inside a message opens this sheet with Copy link and Open link added at the top, not the OS link preview.

edgeCases.title: Touch screen on a laptop
edgeCases.handling: A 500 ms touch-and-hold opens the same menu at the finger, rows at 40px; the reaction strip never relies on hover to show itself.

edgeCases.title: Liquid Glass and earlier iOS
edgeCases.handling: The glass follows the iPhone's own settings with no work from us, because the kit draws it with the system material (GlassView): Clear or Tinted (Settings → Display & Brightness → Liquid Glass) changes how much shows through, Reduce Transparency makes it frosted and nearly opaque while keeping its shape, and Increase Contrast adds a contrasting edge. The app subscribes to AccessibilityInfo 'reduceTransparencyChanged' only to adjust what it draws around the glass. iOS before 26 keeps the blur look. This happens live in the app as the person changes the setting.

web.base: A card that pops in with enter("pop"): a role="group" of reaction <button>s (aria-pressed) above Menu (bare) for the rows; inline styles over `t`, hover, press and focus from useInteraction; `picked` through useControllable; Esc calls onClose. Avatar for the highlighted target
notes: Only targets that have actions get our menu: a message, a sidebar row, a file, a person. Everywhere else, and always inside a text field, the browser's own menu opens.
With text selected inside the message, the browser's menu wins, so Copy works on the selection and Look Up / Translate keep working.
Shift+right-click always gives the browser's menu — the escape hatch for Inspect, Save image, Open link in new tab.
Opens at the pointer and flips or shifts on both axes to stay 8px inside the viewport.

keyboard.action: Opens at the focused message's top-left corner
Moves between rows; ← / → move across the quick reactions
Closes and returns focus to the message

desktop.base: The same card as web at desktop density, with Menu (bare) for the rows
notes: Today a right-click outside a text field does nothing: useSuppressContextMenu (no-context-menu.ts) cancels the WKWebView menu — Reload, Back, Inspect Element — in the capture phase, because every item on it is a no-op or a way to break the app. This spec puts our own menu where there are actions and keeps the suppression everywhere else.

Text entry keeps the system text menu, decided by walking up from the target (input, textarea, contenteditable) — Cut, Copy, Paste, spelling and writing tools are the OS's, and nothing here reimplements them.
The menu's rows are the same as the message row's ⋮ menu, so a keyboard or touch-laptop user who cannot hover the toolbar has the full set.
In the catalogue the panel pops in at the pointer, and pressing a quick reaction marks it yours (pressing yours takes it away) through `picked`; the app also closes the menu.

keyboard.action: Opens on the message cursor (Windows, Linux)
Same as right-click on macOS
Closes this menu only and leaves the message cursor where it was

mobile.base: <Enter motion="slide-up"> (role dialog, accessibilityViewIsModal) over GlassSurface (Liquid Glass on iOS 26+): Pressable reactions, the emoji panel, and Menu (bare) bled to the gutter; `picked` and `picking` through useControllable
notes: A sheet titled "Message": the quick reactions first (the commonest act), then Copy text, Reply in thread, Forward, Edit message, Pin to channel, and Delete message last in red.
Copy text is first among the rows because it is the one row that cannot fail for a reason the message decides; it is dropped for a message with no text.
The + opens the full emoji panel (260pt) under the quick set; the quick set doubles as its "Frequently used".
Forward is never gated on ability: the only permissions are "can I read this" (seeing it answers that) and "can I post there", which the picker and the server decide.

iOS 26+: Liquid Glass — the surface is drawn through expo-glass-effect's GlassView (gated on its availability check; the material itself follows the device's Clear / Tinted, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast settings). iOS 18 and earlier keep today's blur/opaque look. The actions sheet floats inset with fully rounded corners. The desktop right-click menu is our own surface and does not change on macOS 26.
In the catalogue the sheet slides up; a quick reaction marks itself yours (or takes yours away) through `picked`, and + toggles `picking`, fading the emoji panel in where the rows were.

gestures.action: Opens the sheet with a medium haptic; the message stays highlighted under the scrim
Adds it, or removes yours if it is already yours, and closes
Opens the full emoji panel in the sheet; tap again to close it
Runs it and closes

gestures.gesture: Drag down, tap the backdrop, Android back
gestures.action: Closes without doing anything

flows.title: Right-click or long-press a message, then react
Delete from the menu hands off to a confirm

delta.name: Delta
delta.description: How a number changed: an arrow, the change, and a colour that says whether that is good. Up is good unless `inverse`; the hues are the data palette's own, never the brand or a status colour.

value.description: The change, as the number the format prints: 0.044 is +4.4% under the default format. Zero has no direction and draws a dash.

inverse.description: Down is good (open tickets, response time, cost): the green and the red swap. The arrow still points the way the number went.

format.description: A format name ("points"), its options ({ type: "percent", digits: 2 }) or a function: what core's `fmt` takes, so a Delta, an axis and a table cell print one value the same way.

size.description: sm is 11px type beside a stat's period; md is 12px, a KPI tile's; lg is body size, a headline's.

variant.description: text is the arrow and the number in the data ink, for running beside a value. badge sits them on the soft fill of the same hue, for a KPI card's corner or a table cell.

a11y.label: "Up 4.4%, good", "Down 10.1%, good" for an inverse Delta, "No change"
notes: The arrow and the number are drawn, not read: the label says the direction, the size and whether it is good or bad, so the colour is never the only signal.
The label leaves the sign out of the number ("Down 10.1%", not "Down -10.1%") because the word carries it.
A value that is not a number reads "Change unavailable" and draws an en dash.

examples.name: MRR, up
examples.description: Monthly recurring revenue, this month against last.

examples.name: Open tickets, down is good
examples.description: #platform-eng closed more than it opened: the arrow points down and the Delta is green.

examples.name: Response time, up is bad
examples.description: Fabric's median first reply got slower.

examples.name: Win rate in points
examples.description: A change in a share is a difference of points, not a percent of a percent.

edgeCases.title: No change
edgeCases.handling: Zero draws a dash in the muted text colour and reads "No change". It is neither good nor bad, so it takes neither hue.

edgeCases.title: No value yet
edgeCases.handling: NaN (a first period with nothing to compare to) draws an en dash and reads "Change unavailable". It is never drawn as 0%: a missing comparison is not no change.

edgeCases.title: A large swing
edgeCases.handling: A tenfold rise reads +1,240% with the thousands separator; the badge grows to fit. Past a few digits, change the format (a multiple, "12.4×") rather than print a long percent.

edgeCases.title: Down and bad
edgeCases.handling: A fall in revenue is red and reads "Down 6.2%, bad". The colour follows good or bad, the arrow follows the number.

web.base: A <span role="img"> named by the change ("Up 4.4%, good"): the kit's Icon and a text span drawn from its recipe; the tone's ink and fill are picked from the data tokens. No chart library
notes: Shipped from the data subpath, not the root entry: an app that never imports it carries none of the chart code.

desktop.base: The same <span role="img"> as web, at desktop density

mobile.base: A View (accessibilityRole image, labelled with the change) over the kit's Icon and a Text, drawn from the same recipe
notes: The type is one step up on the phone, as every text token is; the arrow follows the icon tokens.

dialog.name: Dialog
dialog.description: A modal question over a blurred scrim. A confirm is a fixed 440px card that names what will be lost, with Cancel and a solid danger CTA; a form dialog is the app's one modal width. On a phone both become a bottom sheet with the buttons stacked full width.

kind.description: confirm: a decision about something already chosen — fixed 440px, glyph tile, no header strip. form: fields to fill — the one modal width, clamp(540px, 37.5vw, 960px), drawn here at 540, with a header strip and a close button.

subtitle.description: A line under a form dialog's title.

body.description: Names what will be lost, in specific words. A prominent destructive button with vague copy is how people delete things they meant to keep.
body.sample: “Ship push opt-in for Android 14” and everything on it (subtasks, comments, attachments) will be removed. This can’t be undone.

icon.description: The confirm's glyph tile: trash-2 for a delete, log-out, unlink, list-x. Empty hides the tile. Form dialogs never have one.

tone.description: danger is the solid danger-coloured CTA for anything that destroys. primary (the brand fill) is for a confirm that ends or disconnects but destroys nothing: Log out, Disconnect Gmail.

confirmLabel.description: A verb plus the object, never OK or Yes.

children.description: Fields or anything else between the body and the actions.

loading.description: The confirm is in flight: its button spins, Cancel, Esc and the scrim do nothing until it settles.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed. The dialog stays open; pressing the CTA again retries.

stacked.description: Drawn over another open dialog — the one level of stacking allowed.

behindTitle.description: The title of the dialog drawn dimmed behind this one while stacked. The dialog draws only what its props give it, so the title behind is the caller's. Empty draws that dialog with no title.

keyboard.description: The on-screen keyboard is up; the sheet sits on it.

modal.description: Drawn over the whole window, above the page: the scrim covers it, the page behind does not scroll and is out of reach, and Esc or a press on the scrim cancels the top dialog. Off, the dialog is drawn where it is mounted and its host does all of that (the catalogue draws it so).

dismissible.description: Esc, a press on the scrim, the phone's handle and Android's back cancel it. Off for a step that must be answered with one of its buttons.

a11y.label: {title}
notes: aria-labelledby the title and aria-describedby the body, so a screen reader reads the question and what will be lost before the buttons.

Web: focus moves in when the dialog mounts, whenever that is (a timer, a deep link, a push), unless the tree is under `autoFocus={false}`; a confirm focuses Cancel, not the CTA, so a reflexive Enter never deletes, and a form focuses its first field. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the panel, Esc cancels (and stops there, so a layer under keeps its own), and when the dialog unmounts focus returns to the control that had it, if that is still on the page.
With `modal` the kit makes the rest of the root inert and hidden from assistive tech and locks the page's scroll while the dialog is open. Without it, the host that mounts the dialog owns those.
The glyph tile is decorative and hidden from assistive tech.

Phone: the sheet is a modal view; Android's back button cancels, VoiceOver's and TalkBack's escape gesture cancels, and screen-reader focus moves to the title on open. A form dialog lifts its sheet above the keyboard.

props.title: Delete this message?
props.body: This also deletes its 3 replies, including replies from other people. This cannot be undone.

examples.name: Non-destructive confirm
examples.description: Ends a session, destroys nothing: the brand fill, not the danger fill.

props.title: Log out of AntFabric?
props.body: You’ll be returned to the sign-in screen. Fabric keeps your ritual and your drafts exactly as they are.

props.title: Disconnect Gmail from AntFabric?
props.body: The Inbox stops copying your mail, and the copy AntFabric keeps is deleted later unless you reconnect. Nothing in your Gmail changes, and your Calendar and Meetings keep working.

examples.name: Form dialog
examples.description: The one modal width, drawn at 540.

props.error: Couldn’t delete the task. Check your connection and try again — nothing was removed.

edgeCases.title: A dialog over a dialog (modal)
edgeCases.handling: Each modal dialog joins the overlay stack: Esc and a press on the scrim cancel only the top one, and the page's scroll comes back when the last one closes.

edgeCases.title: Must be answered (dismissible off)
edgeCases.handling: Esc, a press on the scrim, the phone's handle and Android's back do nothing; only Cancel and the CTA close it. For a step with no safe way out, such as accepting terms before going on.

edgeCases.title: Unsaved changes
edgeCases.handling: Esc, a click on the scrim, the ×, a drag-down on the phone: on a form with edits, each asks first instead of discarding silently. A form with no edits closes at once. The question names what is unsaved, and the safe answer keeps editing.

edgeCases.title: A dialog opened while another is open
edgeCases.handling: One level only: a confirm may open over a form (Discard changes over Edit channel); nothing opens over a confirm. The second scrim is the light one, so the stack never goes black, and only the top dialog is focusable. Esc peels the confirm first. On the phone the form sheet is replaced, not stacked — and iOS silently drops a modal presented while another is still dismissing, so the confirm waits for the first sheet's onDismiss.

edgeCases.title: Body longer than the window
edgeCases.handling: The title and the actions stay put and only the body scrolls, so the buttons never leave the screen. The panel caps at the window height minus 48; drawn here at 280px of body. Below about 590px of viewport the clamp stops deciding and the panel is the window minus its padding.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard on the phone
edgeCases.handling: A sheet with a field lifts above the keyboard on both platforms (Android's edge-to-edge Modal does not resize for the IME, so the sheet measures it) and caps its height to what is left above the keys. Closing dismisses the keyboard too.

edgeCases.title: Pressed twice, slow, or failed
edgeCases.handling: The CTA disables the moment it is pressed; the request carries an idempotency key. The spinner appears after 300 ms and stays at least 400 ms. While in flight, Cancel, Esc and the scrim do nothing — closing would hide the outcome. After 8 s the label reads "Still deleting…". A failure keeps the dialog open with the reason inline, and the same button retries.

edgeCases.title: Esc and focus
edgeCases.handling: Esc is Cancel and closes only the topmost layer — an open menu first, then the confirm, then the form beneath. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the panel; with nothing focusable, Tab does nothing rather than escaping. On close, focus returns to the control that opened it, or to the pane heading if that control is gone. In macOS full screen, Esc is consumed by the app before the system sees it, so cancelling a dialog never also exits full screen.

edgeCases.title: The thing is deleted on another device
edgeCases.handling: If the task, message or channel disappears while its confirm is open (deleted from the phone, say), the confirm closes and a toast says "Already deleted on another device." The CTA is never left pointing at nothing.

edgeCases.title: Window hidden, tab in the background, app killed
edgeCases.handling: Hiding the desktop window to the tray leaves the dialog open exactly as it was; nothing auto-confirms or auto-cancels, and a deep link that arrives meanwhile waits behind it. A background web tab keeps it open. A killed phone app does not restore a transient confirm; form drafts survive.

edgeCases.title: Text at 130%, reduced motion, dark mode
edgeCases.handling: The title wraps to two lines before truncating; on the phone the sheet grows and the body scrolls before the buttons are pushed off. With reduced motion the panel fades in without the rise. In dark mode the scrim is black at 55% and the panel is the raised surface.

web.base: A <div role="alertdialog"> (confirm) or "dialog" (form), aria-modal, labelled by its <h2> and described by the body, on a 3px-blurred scrim; inline styles over `t`; Button and IconButton. Tab wraps inside, Esc cancels, Mod+Enter submits a form, and Cancel (a form: its first field) takes focus on open; pops in with enter("pop") over a fading scrim; `loading` through useControllable
notes: The backdrop blurs 3px. With `modal` the dialog is drawn in the overlay layer of its AntFabricRoot (the theme applies, no overflow clips it): the scrim covers the window, the page behind does not scroll (the body and the box the page scrolls in) and the rest of the root is inert; only the top dialog takes Esc and a press on the scrim. Without `modal` it is drawn where it is mounted, and those belong to the host.
Below 640px of viewport (a phone browser) the same component draws as the bottom sheet the phone app uses, buttons stacked full width.
Closing a tab with a dirty form dialog fires beforeunload, so the browser asks with its own words; the app never invents a custom unload message.
⌘W closes the tab, not the dialog — never advertise it as a dialog shortcut.

keyboard.action: Moves inside the dialog only, wrapping at both ends
Same as Cancel; closes only the topmost dialog
Activates the focused button
Submits a form dialog. A destructive confirm has no shortcut.

desktop.base: The same <div role="alertdialog"> as web at desktop density
notes: W_MODAL = clamp(540px, 37.5vw, 960px): 540 on a 1440 laptop, growing with the screen, capped at 960. It is the one modal width in the app; a confirm (W_CONFIRM, a fixed 440) and the command palette are the documented exemptions, and a test lists them.
Confirm layout: 24 / 20 / 20 padding, 20px corners, a 42px glyph tile, a display-font title, the body at 13px, and the two buttons right-aligned at equal widths (DialogActions).
The CTA is solid danger-coloured for every confirm whose glyph is a bin; Log out, Disconnect and Remove from your list stay on the brand fill because they destroy nothing.

Focus: on mount the first control takes focus (a confirm's Cancel, a form's first field; the panel when it holds nothing focusable), Tab wraps inside, and the opener gets focus back on unmount if it is still on the page.
In the catalogue the panel pops in over a fading scrim, and pressing the CTA sets `loading`: its button spins and Cancel and Close go quiet, as while the request is in flight.
Escape runs through the app's Escape ladder: a popover menu first, then the confirm, then the form under it — one layer per press.

keyboard.action: Trapped inside the panel, wrapping
Closes the innermost layer only
Submits a form dialog

mobile.base: A bottom sheet: <Enter motion="slide-up"> (role alertdialog or dialog, accessibilityViewIsModal) over a fading scrim, StyleSheet over useTheme(); the CTA and Cancel as full-width Buttons, IconButton to close; `loading` through useControllable
notes: Title row 16 under the handle, message 28 above the buttons, then the CTA and an outlined Cancel, both 56pt and full width — Cancel under the CTA, where the thumb rests after reading.
tone danger is the red destructive button; tone primary is for an approval (granting an agent permission), which must not look like a hazard.
No glyph tile on the phone; the title carries the question.
Closing puts the keyboard away too.
In the catalogue the sheet slides up, and pressing the CTA sets `loading`: it spins and Cancel and Close go quiet.

gestures.action: Confirms, then closes

gestures.gesture: Tap Cancel, the ×, the backdrop, or drag down
gestures.action: Cancels
Cancels (dismisses the keyboard first if it is up)

flows.title: Confirm before a message is deleted
Back out without deleting

divider.name: Divider
divider.description: A hairline rule that separates content, horizontal or vertical, with an optional centred label. It is not a section heading, and it is not the day line in a message timeline (that is MessageDivider).

orientation.description: horizontal runs across its container. vertical takes the height of its row, at least an icon tall; it draws no label.

label.description: Words centred on a horizontal rule, such as "Today". Empty draws the rule alone.

inset.description: Space left around the rule so it stops short of its neighbours. none runs edge to edge.

a11y.label: {label}
notes: A vertical divider sets aria-orientation. A labelled one is named by its label.

edgeCases.title: A long label
edgeCases.handling: The label wraps onto more lines, centred, and each rule keeps at least space.xl, so the break still reads as a rule.

web.base: A <div role=separator> with its rule and label drawn from the recipe

desktop.base: The same <div> at desktop density

mobile.base: A View with a rule View and a Text drawn from the same recipe

donut-chart.name: DonutChart
donut-chart.description: A whole split into segments on a ring, with its total in the hole, and under it, past a rule, a legend of every segment's name, value and share: in columns on the web and the desktop, as the reference dashboard draws it, and a row each on the phone. Pointing at a segment or its row puts that segment's value in the hole and steps the rest back; pressing a row picks the segment, and its swatch turns it off, when the shares re-fit. Past eight segments the rest fold into one called "Other". "View as table" shows every row, unfolded.

headingLevel.description: The heading level of the card's title, 1 to 6, so the chart keeps the page's heading order: a card under an h2 is an h3, one under an h1 is an h2. The phone has one kind of header and reads it for nothing. The card is not a landmark: the figure inside is named by the summary.

data.description: Rows, one per segment: [{ channel: "#support", tickets: 312 }, …]. The same rows can feed a table, a stat and a bar chart. In the order they are given: a ring reads best largest first.

name.description: The field of each row that names its segment.

value.description: The field of each row that is its value. A value under zero, or one that is not a number, counts as 0: a share is never negative.

title.description: The card's title. It names the figure on the page, and is the first words of what a screen reader hears.

subtitle.description: One line under the title: what it covers. Empty draws none.

headline.description: A number to lead with, under the title: { value, format, delta, deltaFormat, inverse, period }. It is a MetricValue (in the chart's format unless it names one), a Delta badge and what the change is against ("resolved in October"). Left out, the card has none.

format.description: A format name, its options or a function: what core's `fmt` takes. The axis, the labels at the ends of bars, the tooltip, the summary and "View as table" all print through it, so they agree.

valueLabel.description: The value column's name in "View as table". Default "Value".

centerLabel.description: What the hole says above the total. It says the focused segment's name instead while one is.

size.description: The ring's width and height, in px (points on the phone). Default 200: `chart.donutSize`.

empty.description: The title of the empty state when there are no rows. Say why: nothing yet and nothing matching a filter are different sentences.

emptyLine.description: One sentence under it: what to do about it.

loading.description: Grey bars of uneven heights in place of the plot, from the kit's Skeleton, and no "View as table". The header stays, so the card does not jump when the data arrives. Screen readers hear "Loading chart" once.

hidden.description: The segments the list has turned off, by name: ["Email"]. Left out, the chart keeps its own, starting with every segment on. Controlled when the app passes it with `onHiddenChange`.

onHiddenChange.description: A list row was pressed. Called with every segment that is off now. The last segment showing cannot be turned off, so pressing it calls nothing.

selected.description: The segment that is picked, by name: the hole shows it and the others step back until it is picked again. Pointing at a segment or tabbing to its row lights it too, for as long as the pointer or the keyboard is there. Left out, the chart keeps its own, starting with none. Controlled when the app passes it with `onSelectedChange`.

onSelectedChange.description: A segment was pressed on the ring. Called with its name, or with null when it was already the one picked.

a11y.role: figure (web), one image and a list (phone)
a11y.label: The summary: "Tickets by channel: #support 312 (40.6%), #billing 158 (20.5%), #platform-eng 121 (15.7%), #onboarding 96 (12.5%), Email 82 (10.7%); total 769."
notes: The figure (the ring on the phone) is named by the sentence core's `segmentsOf` and `summarizeSegments` write from the rows: every segment, its value and its share, and the total. It is heard, not printed: the legend under the ring prints every segment's name, value and share, so colour is never the only way in.

The list is the legend, the pick and the toggles: each row is a button that is pressed while its segment is the picked one ("#billing, 158, 20.5%"), so `selected` is reachable by keyboard and screen reader as well as by touching the ring. Each swatch is its own toggle button named "Show #billing", pressed while the segment shows; a segment that is off is struck through and faint, not only dimmer, with an en dash for its share. The last one showing cannot be turned off. The rows and swatches draw a focus ring.
"View as table" is the other way in: every row, with real headers, and nothing folded into "Other".
The ring's hole is drawn for the eye and hidden from a screen reader (it repeats the summary).

examples.name: Tickets by channel
examples.description: Five segments, the total in the hole, the legend in columns under it.

examples.name: With a headline
examples.description: The card leads with a number, its change and what it is against.

examples.name: A segment picked
examples.description: `selected` is `#billing`: the hole shows its value and name, and the other segments step back.

examples.name: A segment turned off
examples.description: `hidden` is the list's state: Email is off, so the shares re-fit to the four that are left and its row is struck through.

examples.name: Eleven channels
examples.description: The first eight keep a colour of the palette; the other three are one segment, Other, in grey.

edgeCases.title: No rows
edgeCases.handling: An empty `data` draws the kit's EmptyState in the plot's place and says why (the title and line are props); the card keeps its header and has no "View as table", since there is nothing to show. The figure's label says there is no data.

edgeCases.title: One segment
edgeCases.handling: One row is the whole ring: a full band with no gap and no rounded corner to cut it apart, its share 100% and the total its value.

edgeCases.title: All zero
edgeCases.handling: A whole of nothing has no shares to cut: the ring is its empty track in the grey the gauge's is, the hole says 0, every share is an en dash and the summary says every value is 0.

edgeCases.title: More than eight segments
edgeCases.handling: The palette has eight colours, and a ninth would wrap onto the first, so the first eight keep their own and every row after them is summed into one more, labelled "Other", in a neutral grey (`chart.other`) that is no colour of the palette. Pass the rows largest first so what is folded is what is smallest. It is one row in the list and turns off as one, and the summary says how many it holds ("Other, 3 more, 47 (6.1%)"). "View as table" shows every row.

edgeCases.title: A negative or missing value
edgeCases.handling: A share is never negative: a value under zero, or one that is not a number, counts as 0, so its segment has no width, its share is 0% and the others still add to the total. The table shows the row as it was given.

edgeCases.title: A long name
edgeCases.handling: A name too long for its row is cut with an ellipsis, and the hole cuts its label the same way; the summary and the table have the whole name.

edgeCases.title: Loading
edgeCases.handling: Grey bars of uneven heights fill the plot and the card keeps its header. There is no list, no table button and no summary yet. A screen reader hears "Loading chart" once.

web.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a <section>: the title, an optional headline, "View as table" (Button); a ChartFrame holding recharts' PieChart with a Pie (paddingAngle, cornerRadius, 90 degrees round to -270) and a Cell per segment, MetricValue in the hole, and a list of <button> rows (aria-pressed) with a swatch, name, value and share
notes: Shipped from the data subpath: recharts is reached only from there. The ring is handed an explicit size, never a responsive container.

Pointing at a segment, tabbing to a row or pointing at one lights that segment: the others fade to 38% over 150ms on the kit's ease-out, and the hole's number eases to the segment's value (MetricValue). The states come from the kit's interaction hook and recharts' own mouse events, never `:hover`.
The ring draws in once over 600ms on the kit's ease-out and tweens when a segment is turned off or the rows change. Reduced motion turns both off.
The legend sits under the ring in as many columns as fit, each at least `chart.partMinW` wide, so a narrow card has fewer columns, not a squeezed ring.

Segments are not keyboard stops: the list is the way in for a keyboard (each row is a button that picks its segment, a swatch toggle beside it turns the segment off, and focusing either lights its segment), and "View as table" has every number.

keyboard.action: Moves through the list's rows, then to "View as table". A row that has focus lights its segment on the ring
On a row: picks the segment, or lets go of it. On a swatch: turns the segment off or back on

desktop.base: The same Card, recharts' Pie and list as web, at desktop density
notes: The same chart as the web's. The pointer's hover lights a segment, and a click picks it.

keyboard.action: Moves through the list's rows, then to "View as table". A row that has focus lights its segment on the ring
On a row: turns the segment off or back on

notes: Shipped from the data subpath: gifted-charts and react-native-svg are reached only from there.

The list is below the ring, full width, each row at least 44pt tall. gifted-charts' pie has no hover and its own focus grows a segment out of the ring; the kit does not use it and steps the other segments back instead (their colour at 38%), as the web does.
The ring pops in over 220ms unless the person reduces motion: gifted-charts' pie draws no sweep of its own.
gifted-charts' slices have square ends, so the segments are cut apart by a stroke in the card's colour rather than rounded.

gestures.action: Picks it: the hole shows its value and name and the others step back. Tap it again to put it back
Picks the segment, as touching it on the ring does; tap it again to put it back
Turns the segment off or back on

empty-state.name: Empty state
empty-state.description: What a surface shows when there is nothing in it, or nothing it can show you: a drawing of what will be here (or a glyph for an error or a refusal), a short title, one line on what happens next, and at most one offered action.

art.description: The drawing for a data surface: the shape you will see once there IS something here, never a mascot. none for an error or a refusal, which takes an icon instead.

icon.description: A glyph in a disc, for the states that are not a data surface — a failure, a lock, sign-in, search. Ignored when art is set.

title.description: What is not here. A noun phrase, not a sentence.

line.description: What will be here and how it gets here. One sentence; never narrates a button that is already visible (ADR-0675).
line.sample: Public channels in your organisation and the direct messages you start will appear here.

actionLabel.description: The offered next step — only on surfaces where the thing is actually made. Empty hides the button.

actionIcon.description: Almost always empty: a labelled button carries no glyph (ADR-0381), except where it repeats a header CTA that has one.

compact.description: The ~248px assistant rails and the sidebar: less padding and a narrower measure. Same drawing, same type ramp.

notes: The drawing and the disc are aria-hidden; the title and the line carry the meaning.
The title is a heading (level 2 in a pane). Focus is not moved to an empty state when it appears — it would steal focus from the search field or the composer.

props.line: Start a direct message with the pen button. Public channels in your organisation appear here too.

props.title: Couldn't load conversations
props.line: The request failed. Check your connection and try again.

props.title: You're not in this channel
props.line: It is private, so there is nothing to join — ask an owner or an admin to add you.

props.title: You're not in this channel
props.line: It is private, so there is nothing to join. Ask an owner or an admin to add you.

examples.name: Sign in to see your messages

props.title: Sign in to see your messages
props.line: Channels and direct messages are the ones you belong to on the desktop.

props.title: Nothing matches
props.line: No message or file in this conversation mentions “rollback”.

props.title: Nothing on your list
props.line: Tasks assigned to you, and the ones Fabric pulls from meetings, land here.

props.title: You're all caught up
props.line: Mentions, replies and reactions to your messages will show up here.

props.title: No files yet
props.line: Files shared in #design-crit appear here, newest first.

edgeCases.title: Still loading is not empty
edgeCases.handling: Never show "No conversations yet" while the first read is in flight — that tells a new hire their workspace is empty. The surface shows a Skeleton (after 300 ms) until the read settles, and only an answered, empty read draws this.

edgeCases.title: A failed read is not an empty list
edgeCases.handling: The error state ("Couldn't load conversations" + Try again) appears only when nothing is on the device. With a cached list, the list stays and an InlineBanner says the refresh failed. The line never prints an HTTP status, a path or a service name — only what to do.

edgeCases.title: Offline on first launch
edgeCases.handling: With no cache there is nothing to show and nothing to retry by hand: no button, and the surface loads by itself the moment the connection returns.

edgeCases.title: Session or SSO expired
edgeCases.handling: The same words as the toast ("Your session expired. Sign in again."), with Sign in as the action. Retrying cannot revive a session, so there is no Try again here.

edgeCases.title: Long search query
edgeCases.handling: The quoted query is cut at 40 characters on a word boundary with an ellipsis; the full query stays in the search field. The line wraps (text-wrap: pretty) rather than truncating the sentence.

edgeCases.title: Narrow rail
edgeCases.handling: compact cuts the padding to 28 × 18 and the measure to 214px so the drawing stays above the fold in a 248px column; the drawing itself never shrinks below 160 × 116.

edgeCases.title: An action that is not this surface's to offer
edgeCases.handling: No button where the thing is not made here: a channel's empty state has none because the composer is directly below; Recordings has none because recording starts from the tray; a feature that is switched off (Rituals) offers nothing.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: Title and line wrap; the drawing stays 160 × 116 and the whole block scrolls if it no longer fits above the keyboard.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: Every colour in the drawing is a theme role (--art-* on desktop, art* on mobile), so the set retints rather than glowing white on charcoal. A hex in a drawing would be the one wrong-coloured thing after a palette change.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: Text is centred so nothing moves; the drawing is mirrored so the conversation bubbles and the unread edge sit on the reading side.

web.base: A centred flex column with enter("fade"): the 160 × 116 drawing as absolutely placed boxes over `t`, or a glyph in a disc; an <h2> title; the kit's Button (secondary, lg)
notes: Search empties are announced through the search field's own live region ("No matches"), not by this component.
The title is an h2 inside the pane's landmark, so a screen-reader user can jump to it.

desktop.base: The same column as web, at desktop density
notes: One empty state for every data surface (ADR-0298). No container: no fill and no dotted outline (owner, 2026-08-31) — a drawing and words centred on whatever it sits on.

Eight drawings, one system: near-white objects with a hairline edge and a soft shadow, layered, real UI chrome, exactly one --fg-faint accent. Every colour is an --art-* role so the set retints per theme; this catalogue approximates them with surface/border tokens because tokens.json has no art.* roles yet.
The action is TERTIARY (white with an outline, no lift) and size lg, only where the thing is made. Recordings has none (started from the tray); a channel has none (the composer is right below).
PaneEmpty is the compact adapter the My Tasks and Rituals rails both call, so they cannot drift into two ideas of empty.
Centred with flex: 1 AND min-height: 100%, because some panes are flex scrollers and some are block scrollers.

mobile.base: A View with <Enter motion="fade">: the drawing as absolutely placed Views (the page fold is a border triangle), or a glyph in a 64pt disc; a header Text; the kit's Button (secondary, md)
notes: V2 (2026-10-15): a 20pt SemiBold title over a 14pt faint line as wide as the gutter allows; 56pt above and below.
The action is centred (alignSelf: center) — Button defaults to flex-start, which left every empty-state action at the left edge.
Error and refusal states use a glyph in a 64pt disc instead of a drawing.

flows.title: The empty state's one action opens the form
A failed read offers Try again, not an empty list

fab.name: Floating action button
fab.description: A disc that floats over a screen for its one standing action. On the phone: the 56pt ink New message button over Messages, and the 56pt Fabric disc beside the bottom bar. On the desktop: the 40px white help disc in Home's corner. Its caller only positions it.

variant.description: ink is the inverse-surface disc, a product's primary action (AntFabric's New message). tint is the brand-tint disc, the one prominent action (AntFabric's Fabric disc). raised is the card-filled disc with a hairline and the float shadow — the one icon button that keeps a container (AntFabric's desktop help disc; ADR-5911's exception).

label.description: The accessible name, and the tooltip on desktop. Never optional — the disc has no text.

src.description: An image drawn instead of the icon — a brand mark (32pt) on the tint disc.

wiggle.description: A press wiggles the glyph for 0.8 s and onPress fires when the wiggle ends, because the sheet it opens covers the disc. One pending press at a time; at once under Reduce Motion.

a11y.label: {label}
notes: The label is the whole accessible name: "New message", "Fabric", "What can Fabric do?". The web adds it as the tooltip.
Keyboard focus draws the focus ring on the disc.

On the phone the disc is rendered before the list in the tree and positioned absolutely, so VoiceOver and TalkBack reach it without swiping past every conversation. `wiggle` waits for the animation before it fires `onPress` unless Reduce Motion is on, which is read when the disc is pressed.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard is up
edgeCases.handling: The ink disc steps aside — it is not rendered while the keyboard is showing, together with the bottom bar — so it never sits on the keyboard or over the field being typed into. It returns when the keyboard goes.

edgeCases.title: Double tap while the pen wiggles
edgeCases.handling: The first tap starts the 0.8 s wiggle and arms one pending open; further taps are ignored until it fires. Unmounting clears the timer so a sheet never opens over a screen that has gone.

edgeCases.title: Bottom bar squeezed by scrolling
edgeCases.handling: The ink disc drops 26pt with the bar's own spring, to sit 12pt above the squeezed 42pt circle. The Fabric disc fades and shrinks to 0.6 and is removed from the accessibility tree; tapping the squeezed bar or scrolling up brings both back.

edgeCases.title: Covering the last row
edgeCases.handling: The list under a disc gets bottom padding of disc + gap, so the last conversation's preview and time can always scroll clear of it. The desktop help disc is fixed to the window corner; Home's content keeps 72px clear at the bottom-right.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Compose still opens — drafts are local, and the sheet itself refuses the send with "You're offline. Your message is saved here." The disc never greys out for connectivity: a dead disc with no reason is worse than a sheet that explains.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: The ink disc inverts with its tokens — a light disc with a dark pen on a dark list. The Fabric disc's tint becomes #382525. The raised disc takes the tertiary button's dark fill and the dark --shadow-float, so it still lifts off the dark page.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: The disc does not scale — it holds no text and 56pt is already over the 44pt target. Its accessible name is read at the user's size by the screen reader.

edgeCases.title: Liquid Glass and earlier iOS
edgeCases.handling: The glass follows the iPhone's own settings with no work from us, because the kit draws it with the system material (GlassView): Clear or Tinted (Settings → Display & Brightness → Liquid Glass) changes how much shows through, Reduce Transparency makes it frosted and nearly opaque while keeping its shape, and Increase Contrast adds a contrasting edge. The app subscribes to AccessibilityInfo 'reduceTransparencyChanged' only to adjust what it draws around the glass. iOS before 26 keeps the blur look. This happens live in the app as the person changes the setting.

web.alternative: No floating disc in the browser. New message is the row at the top of the sidebar (Mod+Alt+N — ⌘N opens a browser window) and Fabric help is the ? icon button in the top bar. A FAB is the phone's answer to having no persistent chrome; the web app always has a sidebar, and a disc pinned to a browser's bottom corner sits over page content at 200% zoom and beside the browser's own download and status UI. Below 600px wide the sidebar collapses and New message moves into the top bar as an icon button, still not a floating disc.

desktop.base: <button> with the label as aria-label and native title tooltip, inline styles over `t`; hover, press and focus from useInteraction; on macOS 26 ink and raised draw glass() and swell under a press
notes: Desktop draws only raised: Home's "What can Fabric do?" disc, position fixed 20px from the window's right and bottom edges (the WINDOW, not the centre column), z-index 50 — above the panes, below every scrim, so the card it opens covers it.
40px, --border-subtle hairline, the tertiary button's fill and --shadow-float. The shadow is part of the shape; the caller only positions it.
A second desktop caller of this shape is a design question, not a reuse opportunity — every other icon button is the flat 28px circle.
New message on desktop is the sidebar row (Mod+N), not a floating disc.

keyboard.action: Activates
Reached after the page's main content; the focus ring sits outside the float shadow

mobile.base: Pressable over a StyleSheet from useTheme(), scaling to 0.94 while pressed; GlassSurface on iOS 26 for ink and raised; with `wiggle` the glyph wiggles with Animated (0.8 s) and onPress fires when it ends, one pending open at a time, at once under Reduce Motion. The bottom-bar squeeze and the haptic are the caller's
notes: ink: 56pt ink disc (surface.inverse, ink-on-inverse 20pt pen), right on the 12pt gutter, 12pt above the bottom bar. Coral until the V2 Figma of 2026-10-16 (ADR-9406).
A tap wiggles the pen (0.8 s) and opens New message when the wiggle ENDS, because the sheet covers the button. Reduce Motion plays nothing and opens at once.
tint: 56pt disc in brand.tint (#FDE8E8 / #382525) holding the 32pt AntFabric mark, 8pt right of the bottom bar. A light impact haptic, then the assistant is pushed as a stack screen.
No shadow on either phone disc — the V2 Figma draws them flat.

iOS 26+: Liquid Glass — the surface is drawn through expo-glass-effect's GlassView (gated on its availability check; the material itself follows the device's Clear / Tinted, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast settings). iOS 18 and earlier keep today's blur/opaque look. Compose and Help become glass discs with ink glyphs; the Fabric disc stays tinted, because it is the one prominent action.

gestures.action: Activates; scales to 0.94 while pressed
Ignored — one New message sheet, never two
