edgeCases.title: Long title or subtitle
edgeCases.handling: Web and desktop truncate each line to one with an ellipsis and show the full title as the tooltip; mobile wraps to two lines and then truncates. Trailing detail, count and chevron never shrink — the title gives way first.

edgeCases.title: Huge unread count
edgeCases.handling: The Badge caps at 99+; the accessible name still says the real number ("142 mentions").

edgeCases.title: Disabled with a reason
edgeCases.handling: Dimmed to 45% and inert, but still focusable in a menu and on a phone so the reason is reachable: the subtitle says why ("Only an owner can delete a channel"). Never hide an action someone can see a colleague use.

edgeCases.title: Hover-only affordances
edgeCases.handling: The desktop ⋮ appears on hover and on keyboard focus of the row. On mobile there is no hover: the same actions are a swipe and a long-press away, and are exposed as accessibilityActions. On a touch laptop (pointer: coarse) the ⋮ is always visible.

edgeCases.title: Read on another device
edgeCases.handling: One read-state event clears the bold title and the count on every device, live; the row does not re-sort or jump while you are looking at the list — it re-sorts the next time the list is opened.

edgeCases.title: Offline and stale rows
edgeCases.handling: Rows draw from the desktop's SQLite cache and the phone's snapshot. A channel you were removed from on another device disappears on the next resync rather than staying with a stale count; opening a cached row while offline shows its cached messages with the pane's offline banner.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: Min-heights are minimums: the row grows with the type, the tile stays 36, and the title wraps to its two lines before anything truncates.

edgeCases.title: Double press
edgeCases.handling: Opening is idempotent — a second press while the conversation loads does nothing new. A destructive menu row closes the menu on the first press, so a second press cannot fire it twice.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: Leading and trailing swap; the chevron mirrors to point left; the shortcut stays in its OS order.

web.base: One <button data-af-press> carrying the row's role (link, menuitem, option, checkbox, button) with aria-current / aria-checked / aria-selected, and aria-disabled so a disabled row stays focusable; `selected` through useControllable; the kit's Avatar, Badge and Kbd; inline styles over `t`
notes: A row that opens a conversation is an <a href>, so middle-click and ⌘-click open it in a new tab; the open one carries aria-current="page".
Hover reveals the row's ⋯ menu and its mark-as-read affordance; the same actions are on the row's context menu and in the keyboard map, so hover is never the only way in.
pointer: coarse raises min-height to 44px on touch laptops.

Pressing toggles `selected` (through useControllable, so the catalogue preview is interactive): a link or button row's grey fill fades in, an option row's check pops in. Opening the conversation is the caller's.
A checkbox row is one <button role="checkbox" aria-checked>: the box is drawn inside it, not a second control, so a click anywhere on the row ticks it.

keyboard.action: Moves between rows (roving tabindex — the list is one tab stop)
Opens the row or runs the menu item
First / last row
Opens the row's context menu

desktop.base: The same <button> as web, at desktop density (30px rows)
notes: Sidebar rows are 30px with a 7px radius fill; the ⋮ is hover-revealed and the unread count slides beside it (2026-10-06).

FileRow is the two-line, tiled case: a 36px chip, the name in semibold, middot-joined provenance ("Figma · Nuthan · yesterday · 4.2 MB"), and the channel trailing. Today's chip is coral-soft; this spec draws it grey because coral is reserved for "needs you" — owner to confirm.
Right-click opens the same menu as the ⋮ (native-feeling context menu, drawn in-app).
Pressing toggles `selected`: the surface.selected fill fades in over 120ms, or the option's check pops in.
A checkbox row (ForwardMessage, CreateChannel's invite list) is a <button role="checkbox"> with the box drawn inside, as CreateChannel does (ADR-0527).

Previous / next conversation from anywhere (sidebar rows)
Previous / next UNREAD conversation
Opens it

mobile.base: Pressable (Animated) with the row's accessibilityRole and state; the 0.6 press dim eases back with Animated.timing; `selected` through useControllable; every glyph in a tile; the kit's Avatar and Badge
notes: 12pt on all four sides and a 12pt gap (owner, 2026-09-09); a row inside a sheet passes its own horizontal inset.
Every glyph sits in a tile: 36 by default, 32 on Settings. The tile is surface.muted so it reads on both a white card and the page (ADR-8910).
Title and subtitle wrap to two lines rather than truncating to one — a phone row has the height.

What desktop reveals on hover is on a swipe (Mark read, Mute) and on long-press; both are also accessibilityActions so VoiceOver and TalkBack users can reach them (ADR-9418). The kit's `onLongPress` is the long press, and it adds the accessibility action itself.
Tapping toggles `selected`: the trailing check pops in (a picker's chosen row); the 0.6 press dim eases back.
A checkbox row is one Pressable with the kit's tick box trailing: the 20pt brand box fills and its tick pops in, and the whole row is the 44pt target.

menu.name: Menu
menu.description: The dropdown a ⋮ or a ▾ opens: a floating card of rows with an optional icon, a trailing count or word, a second line saying what the row will do, a shortcut on web and desktop, and a check for toggles. Destructive rows are danger-coloured text, never a pill.

label.description: The menu's accessible name.

items.description: Rows in order. An entry is a row by default; { type: 'separator' } draws a hairline and { type: 'label', label } a section heading. A row takes label, icon, sublabel (second line), count (trailing number or word), shortcut (Mod+F; web and desktop only), webShortcut (what the web draws instead when the browser owns the desktop shortcut; '' draws nothing), checked (true / false makes it a toggle; leave it out for an ordinary row), radio (with checked: a one-of-many row, role menuitemradio; web and desktop), href (the row navigates: an <a href role=menuitem>; web and desktop), tone ('danger'), disabled. A row's submenu is read by AppMenuBar and TrayMenu; Menu does not open one.

width.description: Panel width on web and desktop. The phone's menu is always 256pt (Figma Mobile / Menu), narrower only when the screen is.

showTrigger.description: Draws the ⋮ that opened the menu, so the catalogue shows where the panel hangs from.

triggerLabel.description: The ⋮ trigger's accessible name. Left out, it reads the `moreActions` string.

placement.description: below is the normal case. above is what the menu does by itself when there is no room under the trigger — the ⋮ on the last row of a list.

bare.description: Rows only, no card — for a sheet or another surface that lists the same rows (the long-press message sheet uses the menu's own rows this way).

toggled.description: The key (else the label) of the checkable row just pressed: its check is drawn flipped from what items says, and pressing it again flips it back. Preview state for the catalogue (one row at a time); in the kits the caller owns checked and hears onSelect.

onSelect.description: A row was chosen. The caller acts on it; for a toggle row it also flips the row's checked.

autoFocus.description: Focus moves to the first enabled row when the menu mounts (from a click as well as from the keyboard) and back to what had it when it unmounts. Turn it off for rows listed on a surface that already took focus. A tree under autoFocus={false} never moves focus in.

a11y.label: {label}
notes: Rows are menuitem; a toggle is menuitemcheckbox (menuitemradio with `radio`) with aria-checked. Disabled rows stay focusable by arrow keys on web and desktop (aria-disabled) so a screen reader can hear why. A row that draws a shortcut sets aria-keyshortcuts.
A row's accessible name joins label, count and sublabel: "Files, None", "Mute channel, No badges unless someone @mentions you".
Section labels are not focusable and are role=presentation: they are drawn headings, not a named group.

Web: focus moves to the first enabled row whenever the menu mounts, ↑ ↓ Home End and type-ahead move between rows, Esc closes (and stops there), and focus returns to what had it when the menu unmounts.
The ⋮ trigger the catalogue draws is an icon button with a label and a pressed look; the kit does not set aria-haspopup or aria-expanded on it: the product's own trigger does.

examples.name: Channel menu
examples.description: The ⋮ on a channel header: shortcut, trailing word, two-line row, a disabled row that says why, and a destructive row last.

examples.name: Toggles with sections
examples.description: The task filter popover: checked rows stay open on press so several can be chosen at once.

examples.name: Message actions
examples.description: The kebab on a message row, 168 wide on desktop.

examples.name: Conversation menu (phone)
examples.description: Mobile / Menu with a two-line row: the icon sits level with the first line.

edgeCases.title: Trigger near the bottom of the window or screen
edgeCases.handling: The panel measures itself before it is shown (visibility hidden for the first frame, never a jump from 0,0) and flips above the trigger when the space below is smaller than its height and smaller than the space above. On the phone the same rule uses the 12pt gutter as the edge.

edgeCases.title: A row that has nothing behind it
edgeCases.handling: Disabled, not hidden, and it says why: "None" in the count, or the reason as the sublabel. A delete past the 12-hour window is a disabled Delete reading "Messages can only be deleted within 12 hours of sending." An option that vanishes teaches nothing.

edgeCases.title: Label longer than the panel
edgeCases.handling: One line with an ellipsis; the panel never widens past its set width. The full label stays the accessible name and, on web and desktop, the tooltip.

edgeCases.title: More rows than the window has room for
edgeCases.handling: The panel caps at the space between the trigger and the window edge minus 8px and scrolls inside, keeping its shadow and corners. On a phone, a list longer than about eight rows is a sheet, not a dropdown.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard only
edgeCases.handling: Opening from the keyboard focuses the first enabled row (focusFirstItem); ↑/↓ wrap, Home/End jump, a letter type-aheads. Esc closes only this menu and gives focus back to the trigger. Focus is never left on <body>.

edgeCases.title: Window scrolls or resizes while open
edgeCases.handling: The panel re-places on every scroll (capture phase, so an inner scroller counts) and resize. If the trigger scrolls out of view the menu closes rather than floating over unrelated content.

edgeCases.title: The action is refused by the server
edgeCases.handling: Rows are gated by what the client knows (abilitiesFor), but the server stays the control: a permission changed on another device makes the write fail, the menu has already closed, and a toast says what happened in the server's own words. Rows are never re-gated optimistically.

edgeCases.title: Touch screen on a laptop
edgeCases.handling: With pointer: coarse rows grow to 40px and the panel to the phone's 6px padding, so a finger can hit them; the hover wash does not stick after a tap.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left languages
edgeCases.handling: The panel anchors to the trigger's end edge in the reading direction; icons lead and counts, shortcuts and checks trail on the mirrored side. Directional icons (arrow-up-right) mirror.

web.base: A <div role="menu"> of <button role="menuitem"> / "menuitemcheckbox" rows (aria-disabled rows stay reachable), inline styles over `t`; hover, press and focus from useInteraction; ↑ ↓ Home End and type-ahead through the shared roving keys, Esc and Tab handled in the panel; the panel scrolls past 80vh; Kbd for the shortcut column; pops in with enter("pop"). Placing and portalling the panel are the app's
notes: Portalling and placing the panel are the app's (it takes a `placement` of below or above and does not flip at the viewport's edge); the panel scrolls inside 80vh when it has many rows.
A row with `href` is a link item (<a href role="menuitem">), so ⌘-click and middle-click open a new tab; a plain click calls onSelect.
Shortcut hints are drawn only for shortcuts the page actually owns; a browser-reserved one (⌘W, ⌘T, ⌘N, ⌘L) is replaced by the web alternative, never shown as a promise the browser will break.
Right-click is not this component — see Context menu.
In the catalogue the panel pops in, and pressing a checkable row flips its check (one row at a time, through `toggled`); the menu stays open, as a checkbox row does.

keyboard.action: On the trigger: opens and focuses the first enabled row
On the trigger: opens and focuses the last enabled row
Moves between enabled rows, wrapping at either end; disabled rows are skipped
First / last row
Type-ahead to the next row starting with that letter
Runs the row and closes; a checkbox row toggles and stays open
Closes and returns focus to the trigger
Closes and moves focus on from the trigger

desktop.base: The same <div role="menu"> as web at desktop density (30px rows), drawing the desktop shortcut rather than webShortcut. The scrim and the z layers stay the app's
notes: The transparent scrim belongs to the menu, not the caller: every menu that forgot one stayed open after a click elsewhere. A click on the scrim dismisses and stops there — nothing behind it hears the click.
A row of sibling triggers sharing one open state (the task filter bar) raises them to z 62, so clicking the next filter opens it in one click instead of first closing this one.

Today's MenuRow has icon, danger, disabled and checked only, opens with focusFirstItem, and handles ↑/↓ in each caller. This spec adds section labels, sublabels, trailing counts, the shortcut column, type-ahead, Home/End and wrap-around in the component itself.
Desktop rows are 12px semibold at 30px; the panel radius is 13 today and moves to the 14 rail radius here.
Danger rows hover to a subtle danger wash — never grey, never the brand colour.

Runs the row
Closes this menu only (the Escape ladder peels one layer) and returns focus to the trigger

mobile.base: <Enter motion="pop"> (accessibilityRole menu) of Pressable rows (menuitem, or checkbox for a toggle row), StyleSheet over useTheme(). Anchoring with measureInWindow and the Modal stay the app's
notes: A dropdown, not a sheet, and no scrim: right edge on the 12pt gutter, 4pt under the ⋮ that opened it, 256pt wide, 6pt padding, 44pt rows and 60pt for a row with a sublabel.
It flips above the ⋮ when it would run off the bottom of the screen.
A row with nothing behind it is disabled at 45% and says why in its count ("None") — the menu explains itself rather than changing shape.
No shortcut column on a phone. Hover rules are not emitted here; pressed is the only feedback, with a selection haptic on press-in.
A row that opens a sheet waits for the menu's onDismiss on iOS before presenting, because iOS drops a modal presented while another is still going (hooks/useSheetHandoff).

Closes without running anything
Closes the menu

message.name: Message
message.description: One message in a channel, thread or DM: the author's face and name, the time, the words, and whatever it carries — attachments, reactions, a thread. It also says when it is still sending, did not send, is waiting for the network, or was deleted, and it marks an agent's messages as AI.

author.description: Display name. For an agent, the agent's name.

identity.description: The author's fallback avatar colour, chosen from their id.

time.description: The sent time in the reader's locale and clock (10:42 AM, 10:42).

gutterTime.description: The compact row's hover time, without AM/PM, so it fits the 36px gutter on one line in every locale (desktop gutterTime(), ADR-5041). The full time is the title.

body.description: The rendered message text (markdown, mentions and channel links are drawn by the kit's RichText; the catalogue shows plain text).
body.sample: Staging is green again. I'll cut the release branch at 4 and post the checklist in #release-train.

status.description: sending: dimmed with a clock until the server acknowledges. failed: "Couldn't send · Retry · Delete". queued: desktop only — held in the offline cache and sent on reconnect. deleted: the tombstone.

agent.description: Sent by an AI agent: agent avatar with the sparkle, the name in brand ink, and an AI tag, so nobody mistakes it for a colleague.

compact.description: A continuation: same author, within 5 minutes, same day, not after a thread summary and not the first unread. No avatar and no name; the time shows in the gutter on hover (web/desktop) and not at all on mobile.

unread.description: Past your read mark and not yet scrolled past: the soft coral unread wash, which fades once half the row has been on screen.

mentionsYou.description: Mentions you directly (or @here / @channel you are in): a soft coral wash with a soft coral edge on the leading side.

highlighted.description: The keyboard message cursor, or the row a notification or search result just brought you to: coral bar and wash.

hovered.description: Draws the hover state: wash, the gutter time on a compact row, and the message actions bar.

reactions.description: Reaction { emoji, count, mine, reactors } in first-reacted order. A reaction at 0 is removed, never drawn.

sample.reactors: You, Marcus Chen and Aisha Bello reacted

thread.description: { count, lastReply, participants, unread, following } — drawn as a thread summary when count > 0.

attachments.description: Attachment { key, kind, name, fileType, badge, typeLabel, size, status, progress, src, title, domain, description, url, duration } per item, drawn as an attachment card each.

addReaction.description: The add pill after the reactions (web and desktop: while the row is hot) and, on web and desktop, the smile-plus on the actions bar.

quickReactions.description: The actions bar's one-press reactions, as emoji. Empty draws none.

replyInThread.description: The actions bar's Reply in thread. It calls `onOpenThread`.

actions.description: The product's own actions on the bar: IconActionItem { key, label, icon, badge?, disabled? }, icon buttons after Forward. The icon is required: a product's action cannot draw a blank button.

more.description: The actions bar's ⋯. A bar with nothing on it is not drawn.

menuOpen.description: The ⋯ menu is open: its button on the bar stays pressed.

onStatusChange.description: Retry on a failed message: called with `status` as the press leaves it (sending). Given this too, the row is controlled; otherwise it goes back to sending itself.

onRetry.description: Retry was pressed on a failed message: the app posts it again.

onDelete.description: Delete on a failed or queued message: removes only the unsent copy.

onOpenThread.description: The thread summary, or Reply in thread on the actions bar (web and desktop).

onReact.description: A quick reaction on the bar or a reaction pill was pressed: toggle yours with this emoji. The server owns the counts, so this is a request: pass the new `reactions` when the server answers.

onAddReaction.description: The add pill or the bar's smile-plus was pressed: open the emoji picker.

onAction.description: A product action on the bar was pressed. Called with the whole item, so the product switches on `action.key`.

onAttachmentOpen.description: An attachment's card was pressed: the app opens its preview (the lightbox or file viewer; on the phone the MediaViewer, or Share / Save to device).

onAttachmentCancel.description: An attachment's cancel was pressed: an upload in progress, or a link preview the sender removes (web and desktop).

onAttachmentRetry.description: A failed attachment's Retry was pressed: the app starts its upload again. Given this, the card is controlled by the attachment's own `status`.

onMenuOpenChange.description: Called with `menuOpen` as the press on the bar's ⋯ leaves it: the caller opens or closes the menu.

a11y.label: {author}, {time}
notes: Web and desktop: the row is a tab stop (tabIndex 0), so a text-only message can be reached by Tab; focus anywhere in the row shows the actions bar, and Tab then moves into it. Shift+F10 or the Menu key and a long press on touch open the bar too; Escape closes it and returns focus to the row. The row's name is who, when, the state and the flags.

Phone: the message's own words are one stop ("Priya Raman, 10:42 AM, Staging is green again…, edited, 1 attachment: plan.pdf, 2 reactions"), with its actions on the rotor (Message actions, Retry, Delete, Open thread). Each reaction, the add pill, each attachment and the thread summary are stops of their own after it, so each can be used.
Status is said in words ("sending", "not sent", "not sent, you are offline"); a failure is an alert, announced once.
"AI" is part of the name for an agent, so it is never read out as a person.
The unread wash, mention edge and cursor bar are never the only signal: unread and mentions are in the label.

edgeCases.title: One enormous token
edgeCases.handling: A pasted URL, hash or model dump with no spaces breaks anywhere (overflow-wrap: anywhere, which also counts for min-content), so the row never pushes past the scroller and the timeline never scrolls sideways.

edgeCases.title: A very long name
edgeCases.handling: The name truncates; the time, the AI tag and the pin never do. The hover card and the accessible name carry the full name.

edgeCases.title: Retry, and a double press on Retry
edgeCases.handling: Retry turns the row back to sending in place and reuses the message's client id, so a send that actually reached the server before the timeout is not posted twice. A second press while it is sending does nothing. Delete removes only the unsent copy — nothing reached anybody.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: The desktop reads history from its SQLite cache and holds new sends as queued, in order, until the socket returns — even across a restart. Web and mobile refuse sends while offline and keep the draft in the composer ("You're offline, so this hasn't been sent. It's still here."); a send already in flight when the connection drops becomes failed.

edgeCases.title: Edited or deleted on another device
edgeCases.handling: The edit lands live with "(edited)"; a message being read is replaced in place without moving the scroll. Deletion is a hard delete today (ADR-0161): the row leaves the timeline for everyone, unless it has thread replies, in which case the tombstone stays so the thread is reachable.

edgeCases.title: Your own message from your other device
edgeCases.handling: A message you sent from the phone arrives on the desktop as sent, with no local echo and no unread wash — your own messages are never unread, and never counted in the badge.

edgeCases.title: Suspended or deactivated author
edgeCases.handling: History stays exactly where it was. The name dims to text.muted, the face falls back to the ink colour, and the hover card says the account is suspended. A DM with them shows the suspended notice instead of a composer.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: Name, time and body grow to the 1.3× cap; the header wraps the time under the name rather than truncating it, and the avatar column stays 40pt wide so continuations still line up.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: The gutter moves to the right and the actions bar to the left; the mention edge and the cursor bar sit on the inline-start side. Mixed-direction messages are isolated per paragraph (dir=auto).

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: The unread wash is 5% coral on dark (3% on light) so it survives the darker surface; the mention and cursor bars keep full-strength coral edges.

web.base: A <div role="article"> row with inline styles over `t`; the hover wash, gutter time and actions bar follow pointer hover (useInteraction), keyboard focus inside the row, or `hovered`. Children are the kit's Avatar, AttachmentCard, ReactionPill, ThreadSummary and MessageActions. The virtualised timeline is the app's.
notes: The hover wash is a CSS :hover on the row — never an inline background, which would beat it — and the unread wash is painted off a data-unread attribute for the same reason.
Every message has a permalink (…/c/platform-eng/p/<id>); Copy link in ⋯ copies it, and opening it scrolls to and highlights the row.
A background tab still receives messages; the tab title count and favicon dot change, the row does not animate in until the tab is visible.

Pressing a reaction toggles yours (each pill keeps its own state), and Retry on a failed message moves it back to sending. The row itself does not toggle `hovered` on a press: in an app that would leave a bar behind on a row the pointer has left, so hover, focus inside the row, or the prop draw it.

Not in the kit yet: Message has no events for the bar's quick reactions, Add a reaction, Forward or ⋯, nor for a reaction pill's toggle (the spec defines none), so those are inert or local inside Message; the body is plain text, not RichText.

keyboard.action: Moves the message cursor (bar + wash)
Edit / React / Reply in thread / Forward the message you are on
Opens the message's actions menu
Leaves the message

desktop.base: The same file as web (one component, desktop density): Avatar + text in the row, the kit's MessageActions floating at top 2 / right 14 on hover. Reply in thread on the bar calls onOpenThread.
notes: Row padding 8 18 2 (1 18 2 when compact), 10 between a 36px face and the text column. The face sits with the name, never in the middle of a long message.
The grouped row's gutter time is opacity-hidden, not display-hidden, and never wraps ("03:02 PM" in 32px of width once grew every row from 24 to 39px).
The unread wash today is brand/soft (ADR-9989); this spec paints surface.unread, the lighter coral both apps share — confirm with design.

queued exists only here: an unacknowledged send is kept in the SQLite cache and resent in order on reconnect, surviving an app restart. Today's desktop refuses offline sends outright (ADR-0704); this spec is the outbox (#317).
Not in the kit yet: events for the bar's reactions, Forward and ⋯, and for a reaction pill's toggle (the spec defines none on Message); right-click opening the ⋯ menu is the app's.

keyboard.action: Moves the message cursor
Edit / React / Reply in thread / Forward
Opens the ⋯ menu
Opens the ⋯ menu at the pointer

mobile.base: Pressable (onLongPress, delayLongPress 300; none while sending) over Views, StyleSheet over useTheme() tokens, Avatar 40. One screen-reader stop whose label carries the words, reactions and replies, with Retry, Delete, Open thread and Message actions as accessibility actions.
notes: V2: 12pt gutters, 8 above a header row and 0 above a continuation, 8 below every row; 16 Bold name, 12 Medium faint time.
A compact row shows no time at all — there is no hover to reveal it. Long-press shows the full timestamp at the top of the actions sheet.
A local echo (sending) is drawn at 55% and ignores long-press; reactions on it ignore taps.
The phone refuses sends while offline and keeps the draft, so queued never occurs here; a send that loses the network in flight becomes failed with Retry.

gestures.action: Opens the message actions sheet (quick reactions, Copy text, Reply in thread, Forward, Edit, Pin, Delete)
Opens the person's profile sheet
Nothing — reserved, so a quick double tap on a link never reacts by accident

A send that doesn't go through

message-actions.name: Message actions
message-actions.description: The small toolbar that appears at the top-right of a message on hover or keyboard focus: three quick reactions, add a reaction, reply in thread, forward, and ⋯ for the rest. It floats over the row, so appearing never moves the text.

quickReactions.description: One-press reactions, as emoji: your three most-used, falling back to 👍 ✅ 👀. Empty draws none, and no rule after them (a narrow pane, or an archived channel).

addReaction.description: The smile-plus that opens the emoji picker. Off in an archived channel.

replyInThread.description: Off on a reply (a reply cannot have a thread) and on the thread root inside its own thread panel — opening it again would wipe the half-typed reply below. Absent, not disabled.

actions.description: The product's own actions: IconActionItem { key, label, icon, badge?, disabled? }, drawn as square icon buttons after Forward and before ⋯. The icon is required: a product's action cannot draw a blank button.

more.description: Whether the ⋯ menu has anything in it (Edit, Copy text, Copy link, Pin to channel, Mark unread, Delete…). A menu with no rows is never drawn.

menuOpen.description: The ⋯ menu is open; the bar stays visible while it is, even after the pointer leaves the row.

onAction.description: A product action was pressed. Called with the whole item, so the product switches on `action.key`.

onMenuOpenChange.description: Called with `menuOpen` as the press on ⋯ leaves it: the caller opens or closes the menu.

a11y.label: Message actions
notes: Every control is a real button with a name ("React with 👍", "Reply in thread").

Arrow keys, Home and End move between the buttons; left and right follow the tree's direction, so in right-to-left they turn round. Every button is still its own Tab stop: a single roving stop needs IconButton to take a tabIndex, which it does not yet.
Inside a Message, the bar shows on hover, on focus in the row, and after a long press or Shift+F10 / the Menu key; Escape closes it back to the row.

edgeCases.title: Message at the very top of the scroller
edgeCases.handling: The bar sits inside the row (top 2), not above it, so the sticky day pill never covers it and the first message of the day is as reachable as any other.

edgeCases.title: Sending, failed or queued message
edgeCases.handling: No bar: a message without a server id cannot be reacted to, threaded or forwarded. The row shows its own Retry / Delete instead (see message).

edgeCases.title: Narrow pane
edgeCases.handling: Below 420px of message width the quick reactions go and the bar is Add a reaction, Reply in thread and ⋯; Forward moves into ⋯. It never wraps onto two lines.

edgeCases.title: Touch laptop (pointer: coarse)
edgeCases.handling: A tap stands on the message (the message cursor) and shows the bar at 40px targets; a long-press opens the ⋯ menu. Hover never has to happen.

edgeCases.title: Two copies of the same message
edgeCases.handling: With a thread open, the root is drawn in the timeline and as the panel's first row. Each bar keys its picker to its own surface, so one press opens one picker, not two.

edgeCases.title: Read-only channel
edgeCases.handling: Reactions stay ("You can still read it and react to messages"); Reply in thread follows the channel's reply setting; Forward is always allowed for people who can read.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: The bar appears without its 120 ms fade and the quick reactions do not grow on hover.

web.base: A role="toolbar" box with inline styles over `t`: quick reactions are <button>s with hover and press from useInteraction, the rest the kit's IconButton (square); ⋯ is a toggle IconButton that holds `menuOpen`. ← / → move focus along the bar. Tooltips are each button's title.
notes: Shown on row hover and on :focus-within, positioned absolute at top 2 / right 14 of the row so it costs the message no height and no reflow.
Right-click on a message opens the same actions as a context menu, except on a link, an image or selected text, where the browser's own menu is kept (Copy link address, Save image, Look Up).
Bare-letter shortcuts (E, R, T, F) are safe in a browser because they only fire while a message, not a text field, has focus.

keyboard.action: Moves the message cursor; ↑ in an empty composer edits your last message
React (opens the emoji picker)
Reply in thread
Forward
Edit your message
Opens the ⋯ menu for the message you are on
Closes the menu, or leaves the message

desktop.base: The same toolbar as web (one file): the kit's IconButton ×n in a floating card (surface.raised, shadow raise), fading in on mount; the caller opens its menu from onMenuOpenChange.
notes: Today's bar is Add a reaction, Reply in thread, Copy text and ⋯ (Edit, Forward, Pin to channel, Delete). This spec adds three quick reactions and moves Forward onto the bar; Copy text moves into ⋯.
Hidden while another message's picker or menu is open, so two bars never stack; kept visible while its own popover is open.
Right-click anywhere on the message body opens the ⋯ menu (ADR-6120); inside the message editor the system text menu (Cut, Copy, Paste, Look Up) stays.
The bar fades in (120 ms) when the row is hovered; pressing ⋯ toggles `menuOpen`, which holds the button pressed while the menu is open.

React
Reply in thread

Edit your message

Closes the menu, then leaves the message

mobile.alternative: A phone has no hover. Long-press a message (300 ms, light haptic) opens the message actions sheet (see context-menu): a row of quick reactions with "React with another emoji", then Copy text, Reply in thread, Forward, Edit message, Pin to channel and Delete message (danger). Swipe right on a message to reply in thread is not used: the screen's swipe-back owns that edge.

message-divider.name: Message divider
message-divider.description: A rule across the timeline: the day a run of messages was sent ("Today", "Yesterday", "Monday", "Monday, 27 October") or the coral "New messages" line where your unread starts. While scrolling, the current day rides at the top as a sticky pill.

kind.description: date marks a day boundary; new marks the first message you have not read.

label.description: For date: "Today", "Yesterday", a weekday within the last 6 days ("Monday"), else "Monday, 27 October" — with the year only when it is not this year ("Friday, 13 December 2024"). Formatted in the reader's locale and time zone. Ignored for new.

sticky.description: The floating day pill pinned to the top of the scroller. On web and desktop it is a button that opens the jump-to-day menu (Today, Yesterday, Last week, a calendar).

onJump.description: The sticky pill was pressed: open the jump-to-day menu.

expanded.description: The jump-to-day menu the sticky pill opens is open: the pill reports it through aria-expanded. Left out, the pill says nothing about the menu's state.

level.description: The heading level of a day divider, so a timeline fits the page's outline.

notes: Date dividers are exposed as headings (level 3 by default, `level` sets it) in the timeline, so screen-reader users can jump day by day with the heading rotor or H.
The sticky pill's name says what it shows and what it does: "Showing Yesterday. Jump to another day". It reports `aria-expanded` from the `expanded` prop when the product gives it.

edgeCases.title: Midnight passes while the channel is open
edgeCases.handling: Labels are recomputed at local midnight (one timer, not per row) and when the window or app regains focus: "Today" becomes "Yesterday", and the next message gets a new "Today" divider. Two dividers saying the same thing are impossible because a boundary is a change of label, not of the raw date string.

edgeCases.title: Travelling across time zones
edgeCases.handling: Days are the reader's local calendar days. A message sent at 23:30 in Bengaluru appears under "Yesterday" for a reader in San Francisco. Each row's time keeps its own value; only grouping follows the reader.

edgeCases.title: New messages and a new day on the same message
edgeCases.handling: The date divider comes first and the coral line second, directly above the message: "Tuesday, and this is where you got to".

edgeCases.title: Unread run read on another device
edgeCases.handling: If you read the channel on your phone, an open desktop pane keeps its "New messages" line until you leave the channel (removing it mid-read would move the text you are looking at); on the next open it is gone. A closed or backgrounded pane updates on return.

edgeCases.title: Only your own messages are new
edgeCases.handling: No line. Your own messages and thread replies never count as unread, so the line is placed at the first message somebody else sent past your read mark, or not at all.

edgeCases.title: Long localised label
edgeCases.handling: The label never wraps or truncates; the rules on either side shrink to nothing first. German and Tamil weekday-and-month strings fit at 320 wide.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: The date divider is symmetrical. "New messages" puts its label at the inline end, which is the left in Arabic and Hebrew.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: Jumping to a day scrolls instantly instead of smoothly; the mobile scroll pill appears and disappears without a fade.

web.base: A row with role="heading" (level 3) for a day or role="separator" for New messages, inline styles over `t`; the sticky pill is a <button> (aria-haspopup="menu") with hover, press and focus from useInteraction, and onJump opens the app's jump-to-day menu
notes: The sticky pill is a position: sticky band the messages scroll under; only the pill takes pointer events. Its label is the day of the topmost visible row, measured from data-day-start anchors, not per message.
The first day draws no in-list divider: the sticky pill is already showing that label in the same place, and two pills on top of each other read as a glitch.

keyboard.action: On the sticky pill: opens Jump to day (Today, Yesterday, Last week, a calendar)
Closes the menu and returns focus to the pill

desktop.base: The same row as web at desktop density, inline styles over `t`; the sticky pill's onJump opens the app's jump-to-day menu (MenuSurface, 244 wide)
notes: "New messages" is a coral rule at 50% with the label at its end, and it sits above the first unread message so that message lands directly under the sticky day pill when the channel opens (data-first-unread).
Today the desktop writes the year on every date past the 6-day window; this spec drops it within the current year.

keyboard.action: On the sticky pill: opens Jump to day

mobile.base: View (accessibilityRole header for a day, role separator for New messages) with hairline Views either side of the Text, StyleSheet over useTheme(); the sticky pill is a translucent View, not a button
notes: Today's TimelineDivider: a hairline either side of a 12pt SemiBold faint label; "New messages" is the same shape in coral and is a header for VoiceOver.

Gap: the phone has no sticky day pill yet. Spec: while the list is scrolling, a translucent pill shows the topmost day and fades out 1.5 s after scrolling stops (no fade under Reduce Motion — it simply hides). It is not a button on mobile; the jump-to-day menu is desktop and web only.

meter.name: Meter
meter.description: One value against a capacity or a target, as a bar that changes colour at its thresholds. `usage` is for what runs out (seats, storage, a quota) and turns to the caution colour and then the loss colour as it fills; `score` is for what you want high (a goal, a rating) and turns as it falls.

value.description: What there is, in the same unit as `max`. A value past `max` fills the bar and says the real share (112%).

max.description: The capacity or target the value is measured against: 1 when the value is already a share (0.42 is 42%).

label.description: What is measured, and the meter's accessible name.

kind.description: usage is fine while low and worse as it fills; its fill is the data accent while it is fine. score is fine while high; its fill is the data gain colour while it is fine. Both turn to the caution colour and then the loss colour at the thresholds.

format.description: A format name, its options or a function, as core's `fmt` takes. "percent" prints the share (42%); any other prints the value of the max in it (9.4 GB of 10 GB, 455 of 600).

thresholds.description: { warning, danger }: the shares of `max` where the fill turns to the caution colour and then the loss colour. Usage turns at or above them (default 0.75 and 0.9); a score turns at or below them (default 0.6 and 0.4).

showState.description: An icon beside the value in the caution (triangle) and critical (circle) states, so the state is not the fill's colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1). On by default; `false` leaves the colour and the spoken value to say it ("78%, caution"), for a product that prints the state beside the meter itself.

compact.description: Just a short track with the value beside it, for a table row or a list item that already names what it is. The label stays the track's accessible name.

a11y.role: meter (web); img while the value is not a number. progressbar with a value on the phone, where there is no meter role
a11y.label: The `label` prop, with the printed value as its text ("42%", "9.4 GB of 10 GB")
notes: The colour is never the only signal: the value is printed beside the label (or beside the track, compact) and is the meter's text, so a person who cannot tell the hues apart still has the number.

aria-valuemin is 0, aria-valuemax the max and aria-valuenow the value held to 0 to max; the spoken value is the printed one, and in the caution and critical states it says so ("78%, caution", "93%, critical"), so the state is not the fill's colour alone. `showState` also draws an icon for it.
A value that is not a number is not a meter: the track is a named image reading the label and an en dash, with no value attributes.

examples.name: Seats used, near the limit
examples.description: 78% of seats is over the 75% caution line.

examples.name: Storage, nearly full
examples.description: Over 90%: the loss colour.

examples.name: Q4 goal, a score
examples.description: 455 of 600 tickets resolved by Fabric: high is good.

props.label: Q4 goal: tickets resolved by Fabric

examples.name: A score that fell
examples.description: A score turns as it falls: 34% is under the 40% line.

Open tickets against the team's limit of 200

edgeCases.title: Empty
edgeCases.handling: Zero draws the empty track and no fill. A usage meter at zero is fine; a score at zero is in the loss colour, because a score of nothing is bad.

edgeCases.title: Over capacity
edgeCases.handling: A value past the max fills the track and stops there, and the text says the real share (112%). The fill is the loss colour for usage.

edgeCases.title: No capacity
edgeCases.handling: A max of zero, or a value or max that is not a number, draws the empty track and an en dash. It never divides by zero or draws a full bar.

edgeCases.title: A long label
edgeCases.handling: The label wraps and the value stays on its line at the end; it is never cut, since it is the meter's name.

web.base: A <div role="meter"> track over a fill, drawn from its recipe; the fill slides to a new value on a transform (never its width). The fill is picked from the data tokens by the value against its thresholds. No chart library
notes: Shipped from the data subpath, not the root entry: an app that never imports it carries none of the chart code.

desktop.base: The same <div role="meter"> as web, at desktop density

mobile.base: A View (accessibilityRole progressbar, with accessibilityValue min, max, now and the printed text) over a track View and a fill View, drawn from the same recipe
notes: React Native has no meter role: progressbar is the closest a screen reader announces as a value out of a range.

metric-tabs.name: MetricTabs
metric-tabs.description: Several metrics over the same period, each one's total as a tab. The chosen tab is marked with its colour and its metric draws as bars underneath; choosing another moves the same bars to the new heights and eases their colour, so the eye follows what changed. A metric keeps its colour whichever is chosen. "View as table" shows every metric's rows in Table.

data.description: Rows, one per point, in order: [{ date: 1791763200000, fabric: 58, people: 49, escalated: 6 }, …]. The same rows can feed a table and a bar chart. A value that is not a number is a bar of 0, and counts as 0 in a total.

x.description: The field of each row that is the category: a date or a word.

metrics.description: The metrics, one tab each, in order: [{ field, label, format?, total? }]. `field` is the row's field and the tab's id, `label` its name, `format` its own number format (a count, a rate and a sum can sit together), `total` the number on the tab when it is not the sum of its field (a rate, an average). The first eight are tabs: the palette has eight colours, and a ninth would wrap onto the first.

title.description: The card's title. It names the figure on the page, and is the first words of what a screen reader hears.

subtitle.description: One line under the title: what it covers. Empty draws none.
subtitle.sample: Oct 12 to 25, a day at a time

format.description: A format name, its options or a function: what core's `fmt` takes, for a metric that names none. The total on each tab, the axis, the tooltip, the summary and "View as table" print through it.

xFormat.description: The category's format, for a date: "month", "day", or options such as { type: "month", timeZone: "UTC" }. A timestamp under a date format is read as a point in time, so the summary reads as a trend. Left out, the category prints as it is.

value.description: The field of the metric that is chosen. Left out, the chart keeps its own, starting with the first metric. Controlled when the app passes it with `onValueChange`. A field that is none of the metrics' chooses the first.

onValueChange.description: A tab was pressed, or an arrow key moved to one. Called with its field. Choosing the tab that is already chosen calls nothing.

height.description: The plot's height, in px (points on the phone). The card is as wide as the space it is given.

empty.description: The title of the empty state when there are no rows. Say why: nothing yet and nothing matching a filter are different sentences.

emptyLine.description: One sentence under it: what to do about it.

loading.description: A grey line where the tabs go and grey bars in place of the plot, from the kit's Skeleton, and no "View as table". The header stays, so the card does not jump when the data arrives. Screen readers hear it once.

a11y.role: tablist with a tab panel and a figure (web), a tablist and one image (phone)
a11y.label: The tab list is named by the title; the panel by the chosen tab (aria-labelledby); the figure by the summary: "Resolved tickets, By Fabric: By Fabric fell from 58 to 34, highest in Oct 22…"
notes: The strip is a tablist and each tab a tab, selected while it is the chosen one. Only the chosen tab is in the Tab order; the arrow keys (they follow the reading direction, so they turn round in right-to-left text), Home and End move between tabs and choose as they go, so a tab and its metric are never out of step. Each tab names the panel it controls (aria-controls). Each tab's name includes its total ("By Fabric, 412"), which a screen reader hears with it.

The figure is named by the sentence core's `summarize` writes from the rows of the chosen metric: dates read as a trend, and where it peaked. It is heard, not printed: in the light theme the series colours sit under 3:1 against the card, so the tab's colour is never the only way to know which metric is drawn: its name is on the tab, and the tooltip and "View as table" give the numbers.
A tab's rule and fill say which tab is chosen with more than a colour: the fill and the rule are both there, and `aria-selected` says it to everything else.
"View as table" is the other way in: every metric, day by day, in Table with real headers, each in its own format. The tabs are hidden while it shows, since the table has every metric at once.

edgeCases.title: No rows
edgeCases.handling: An empty `data` draws the kit's EmptyState in the plot's place and says why (the title and line are props); the card keeps its header, and has no tabs and no "View as table", since there is nothing to total or show. The figure's label says there is no data.

edgeCases.title: One metric
edgeCases.handling: One tab is not a choice, but it still names what is drawn and totals it: the strip has one tab, always chosen, and the arrow keys have nowhere to go.

edgeCases.title: A value that is not a metric
edgeCases.handling: A `value` that names none of the metrics' fields chooses the first one, so the card is never without a chosen tab. The same holds when the metrics change under a chosen field that is no longer there.

edgeCases.title: More than eight metrics
edgeCases.handling: The palette has eight colours, and a ninth would wrap onto the first, so the first eight metrics are tabs and the rest are left out. A strip wider than the card scrolls sideways on the web and the desktop; on the phone the eight share the width and are narrow, so a card with that many is a table's job.

edgeCases.title: Loading
edgeCases.handling: One grey line the size of a total stands where the tabs go and grey bars of uneven heights fill the plot; the card keeps its header. There is no table button and no summary yet. A screen reader hears "Loading metrics" and "Loading chart" once each.

web.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a <section>: the title and "View as table" (Button); a strip of <button role="tab"> (a swatch, a name and a MetricValue each) pulled out to the card's edges, and a tab panel holding a ChartFrame with recharts' BarChart, one Bar under one data key
notes: Shipped from the data subpath: recharts is reached only from there. The plot is BarChart's own (the kit's `RechartsBars`): the same grid, axes, tooltip, lit category and motion.

The chosen metric is always drawn under one data key, `__metric`, whichever it is. recharts then tweens the same bars to their new heights over 600ms on the kit's ease-out, and each bar's fill eases to the new metric's colour, instead of drawing a new series from zero. The value axis re-fits to the new metric. Reduced motion turns the tween off and the colour change stays a plain swap.
The chosen tab has a recessed fill and a 2px rule in its series colour along its foot; the rule fades in over the kit's base duration. A tab's colour is the same whichever tab is chosen.
Tabs share the strip's width and keep a least width (`chart.tabMinW`); a strip with more tabs than the card is wide scrolls sideways.
A long daily series keeps every bar and the tooltip has every day; recharts leaves out the axis labels that would run together.

keyboard.action: Moves to the chosen tab (the other tabs are not stops), then into the plot and on to "View as table"
On a tab: chooses the next tab, wrapping, and moves focus to it
On a tab: chooses the previous tab, wrapping, and moves focus to it
On a tab: chooses the first tab
On a tab: chooses the last tab
On a tab: chooses it

desktop.base: The same Card, tab strip and recharts' BarChart as web, at desktop density
notes: The same chart as the web's. Hover is the pointer's, so a tab lights under it and the tooltip follows it.

keyboard.action: Moves to the chosen tab (the other tabs are not stops), then into the plot and on to "View as table"
On a tab: chooses the next tab, wrapping, and moves focus to it
On a tab: chooses the previous tab, wrapping, and moves focus to it
On a tab: chooses the first tab
On a tab: chooses the last tab

mobile.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a View: the same header and Button, a row of Pressable tabs (accessibilityRole tab) that share the card's width, and a ChartFrame holding react-native-gifted-charts' BarChart (`data`, one bar per day) under one data key
notes: Shipped from the data subpath: gifted-charts and react-native-svg are reached only from there. The plot is BarChart's own (the kit's `GiftedBars`), with the same scale as the web's.

A long series cannot label every bar on a phone: core's `sparseLabels` keeps one label in every few (a fortnight of days is one in four), and the tooltip has every day. The tabs share the width, so three fit on a phone, each at least 44pt tall.
The chosen tab has a recessed fill and a 2px rule in its series colour; a tab is lit while it is pressed, as the web's is while it is pointed at.
The bars draw in unless the person reduces motion. Under react-native-web (the catalogue, `pnpm check`) gifted-charts' animation is off, because the values it animates with reach the DOM as text.

gestures.action: Chooses it: its metric draws as bars
Lights that day's bar and shows its tooltip; the others step back

metric-value.name: MetricValue
metric-value.description: A number as a headline: the digits large and strong, the symbol and unit around them ($, K, %, m) smaller and fainter, so $184,200 reads as 184,200 first. It prints through the same formats as an axis and a table cell, and eases to a new value when it changes.

value.description: The number. When it changes the digits ease to the new one over 300ms; the first value, and any value under reduced motion, appears at once.

format.description: A format name ("percent"), its options ({ type: "currency", compact: true }) or a function: what core's `fmt` takes, so a headline, an axis and a table cell print one value the same way. Whatever surrounds the digits in the printed text is drawn as the symbol or unit.

size.description: The kit's type scale: sm is the lead size, md is h2, lg is h1, xl is display. md, lg and xl are one step smaller on the phone, where a 38px figure does not fit.

a11y.label: The plain formatted value, "$184,200", once
notes: The split into digits and units is drawing, not meaning: a screen reader gets the whole value from one place (a hidden copy on the web, the label on the phone) and the drawn pieces are hidden from it, so it never hears "$", "184,200" as separate things.
While the digits ease to a new value a screen reader already has the new one; it does not hear the numbers in between.
Reduced motion turns the easing off: the value changes at once.

examples.name: MRR
examples.description: Monthly recurring revenue: the dollar sign is the unit.

examples.name: Compact
examples.description: K and M are units too.

examples.name: Median first reply
examples.description: A duration has two units, m and s.

edgeCases.title: No value
edgeCases.handling: NaN (a number that has not loaded) draws an en dash at the digits' size, never a unit-sized dash and never 0. A screen reader hears "–".

edgeCases.title: Negative
edgeCases.handling: The sign stays with the digits and the currency symbol is the unit: −$4,200 draws a full-size minus, a small $, and 4,200.

edgeCases.title: A function format
edgeCases.handling: Whatever the function returns is split the same way: the digits are strong and the text around them is the unit. A result with no digit in it is drawn whole at the digits' size.

edgeCases.title: A long value
edgeCases.handling: It never wraps: the figure keeps one line, and the parent decides what to do with the width (compact the format before a card clips it).

web.base: A <span> drawn from its recipe: the digits and, for each symbol or unit, a smaller span in the faint ink; proportional figures. A visually hidden copy carries the plain value for screen readers. No chart library
notes: Shipped from the data subpath with the rest of the KPI pieces, though it draws no chart.

desktop.base: The same <span> as web, at desktop density

mobile.base: One Text (accessibilityLabel the plain value) with a nested Text for each symbol or unit, which inherits the digits' baseline and overrides the size, ink and weight
notes: md, lg and xl are one type step smaller than on the web and desktop; sm is the same.

mobile-header.name: Mobile header
mobile-header.description: The top of every phone screen, under the status bar. A tab screen carries its name as a 28pt large title with the bell and your photo on the right; a pushed screen carries a back control, a 16pt title with an optional subtitle, and its own actions. iOS centres a pushed title and uses a chevron; Android starts it at the left with an arrow.

variant.description: main: a tab's large title + bell + photo. pushed: back + title + actions, for anything opened on top of a tab.

subtitle.description: Pushed only — '7 members', '#design-crit'. One line, faint.

titleGlyph.description: Pushed only — a channel's # or lock, 4pt before the title.

userName.description: Names the photo on the main header's right, and its initials. Empty draws no photo.

identity.description: The colour of the photo's initials when there is no `avatarSrc`.

actions.description: IconActionItem: { key, icon, label, badge?, disabled? } for each 40pt control: before the photo on a main header, after the title on a pushed one. A badge is a coral count (9+ at most). Two at most on a pushed header; more go behind ⋮.

titleAlign.description: platform centres a pushed title on iOS and starts it on Android. V2 today draws start on both.

statusBar.description: Draws a picture of the OS status bar above, to show the safe area the header sits under. A real app has the system's own bar: leave it off and pad the header by the device's top inset.

connection.description: A one-line status under the header while the socket is not connected.

notes: The title is the screen's heading (accessibilityRole header) and the first thing VoiceOver reads after the back control.
The bell's name carries the count: 'Notifications, 3 unread'. The connection line is a polite live region on Android and is also announced once when it appears, since iOS has no live regions.
Header titles grow with Dynamic Type up to 1.3x so they stay on one line; the rows and buttons are not fixed-height.

The status bar and its clock are a picture, hidden from the accessibility tree and off by default: the system draws the real one. The header does not read the device's safe-area insets itself; the app pads it by the top inset.

edgeCases.title: The bell has no count today
edgeCases.handling: The spec adds the coral badge on the bell, capped at 9+, from the same server count as the desktop rail's Notifications. Reading a notification on any device lowers it; it is never cleared just by opening the inbox screen.

edgeCases.title: A long title
edgeCases.handling: Large titles and pushed titles stay on one line with an ellipsis, and never push the bell, photo or actions off screen. The full name is what VoiceOver reads; tapping a channel's title opens its details.

edgeCases.title: Connecting and offline
edgeCases.handling: After 2 s without a socket the header says 'Connecting…' with a spinner; once the OS reports no network it says 'Offline — showing what's on this phone'. Sends are refused while offline. The line disappears the moment the socket is back, with no 'Connected' flash.

edgeCases.title: Text at 130%
edgeCases.handling: Font scale is capped at 1.3× (maxFontSizeMultiplier). The header's height is a minimum, so the row grows; the 28pt title truncates before the controls move, and the 40pt controls do not scale.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: The row mirrors: the back control moves to the right and its glyph points right; bell and photo move to the left. A start-aligned title aligns right.

edgeCases.title: Notch, Dynamic Island, landscape
edgeCases.handling: The header pads by the safe-area top inset, never a constant: 47pt under the Dynamic Island, 24–32dp on Android, 0 in iPhone landscape where the status bar hides. Landscape adds the side insets so the back control clears the notch.

edgeCases.title: Notifications turned off for AntFabric
edgeCases.handling: The bell still works — the inbox is in-app and the count comes from the server. The Notifications screen opens with 'Notifications are off for AntFabric' and a button to the system settings.

edgeCases.title: Photo fails to load
edgeCases.handling: The avatar shows initials first and fades the photo in when it decodes; a 404 keeps the initials for the session. The button is never an empty circle.

web.alternative: web-top-bar. In a browser the browser draws the status of the device and the back button; the app's top bar carries search, Help and the ⋯ menu.

desktop.alternative: title-bar. A desktop window has a title bar with window controls, history buttons and search; notifications and the profile live in the nav rail.

mobile.base: Views and Text in StyleSheet over useTheme() tokens (fonts by file; the status bar's clock in the system face), IconButton for bell, back and actions, a Pressable around the Avatar, the kit's Spinner for Connecting…; title as accessibilityRole header. The drawn status bar is a stand-in: in the app the header sits in SafeAreaView edges={['top']} with expo-status-bar
notes: main is MainHeader today: the 28pt title is Figtree, not the Heading face; the bell and photo are 40pt boxes 8pt apart, 12pt under the status bar on the 12pt gutter.

The bell pushes /notifications onto the root stack (ADR-9417) and rings on the tap; the photo pushes /profile (ADR-9419), named 'Settings' to VoiceOver. The unread badge on the bell is new in this spec — today the bell has no count.

pushed is Screen's header: 16 SemiBold title, 12 Medium faint subtitle, the row centred on the 40pt controls, and a 12pt gap under it (V2, 2026-10-15). A title somebody else named (a channel, a person) is held to one line.
iOS/Android: V2 today starts the title and uses Ionicons chevron-back on both. titleAlign 'platform' gives iOS's centred title and Android's left title with an arrow — the owner to choose.

Status-bar ink follows the theme (dark ink on light, light ink in dark mode) via expo-status-bar. Android 15 is edge-to-edge by force, so the header always pads by the top inset rather than trusting a translucent bar.

gestures.action: Rings, and pushes Notifications
Pushes Settings (profile)
Opens the workspace switcher sheet when more than one workspace is signed in

gestures.gesture: Swipe from the left edge (iOS) / system back (Android)
gestures.action: Same as the back control; Android 14+ shows the predictive-back peek
Scrolls the screen's list to the top

flows.title: The bell rings and opens Notifications
Back from #release-train to Messages

nav-rail.name: Nav rail
nav-rail.description: The app's one persistent navigation column, at the left edge on desktop and web: 64px of icons collapsed, 248px with labels open, opened and closed by the sidebar button in the title bar or the web top bar. It reads top to bottom as identity, search, the places to be, what is waiting, then you — and the place you are is one soft coral pill that slides between rows. Two variants: flat (variant 1) lists the destinations; drill-in (variant 2), which the web and desktop screens use, opens a destination's sections in the rail itself, its icon taking the logo's place at the top.

variant.description: flat (variant 1): one list of destinations. drill-in (variant 2): pressing a destination moves its icon into the logo's place and lists its sections under it; the top icon, the Main menu chip or Esc go back.

expanded.description: 248px with labels, or 64px of icons. The rail has no toggle of its own: the sidebar button in the title bar (title-bar) or the web top bar (web-top-bar) sets it. Remembered per device.

logo.description: The mark in the lockup tile. A string is drawn as the tile's glyph; an element is drawn bare in the tile. Leave it out for no tile.

title.description: The wordmark beside the tile while expanded. With no `logo` and no `title`, the lockup is not drawn at the menu level.

home.description: The key of the destination the lockup opens; its name is that destination's label, else the key itself. Empty opens the first destination.

workspace.description: The signed-in workspace, drawn under the lockup when expanded. It opens the workspace switcher. Empty draws no chip.

active.description: The key of the row that carries the pill. A key no destination has ("none" while the profile screen covers the workspace) marks none.

level.description: drill-in: the active destination's sections with its icon at the top (sections), where the rail rests, or the destinations (menu), where you go to change destination. A destination without sections always shows the menu. Variant 1 ignores it.

section.description: drill-in: the current section of the active destination, by key. "none" lights no section (a page of that destination that is in none of them); any other key that names none of them makes the first current.

destinations.description: { key, label, icon, badge, max?, sections? } in rail order. max defaults to 9 (9+); the Inbox opts up to 999 because a mail backlog is measured in hundreds. Meetings and My tasks never badge: a schedule is not a backlog. sections, for the drill-in variant, are { key, label, icon, badge?, max? }: the Inbox's are the desktop app's mail folders without Unread (state/mail.ts, MAIL_FOLDERS), Channels' the workspace sidebar's sections (WorkspaceSidebar), and Meetings' Day and Week and My tasks' Due today and Done those panes' views; the rest are placeholders until the product names them.

search.description: Draws the Search row (its field while expanded).

utilities.description: NavItem: { key, label, icon, badge?, max?, badgeLabel? }. The rows above the profile: notifications, a bug report. Collapsed, a badge is a corner count (9+ by default) read as `badgeLabel`; expanded the row reads "{label} · {count}" with no pill.

userName.description: The person's name, in the profile button at the foot. Empty draws no profile button.

identity.description: The colour of the profile's initials when there is no `avatarSrc`.

notice.description: A card above the bottom rows, such as the over-the-air update card (UpdateNotice). Draws nothing when empty.

onLevelChange.description: drill-in: a destination with sections was pressed (sections), or the top icon, the Main menu chip or Esc took the rail back (menu).

onSectionChange.description: drill-in: a section was pressed, or a destination opened on one: the section last open there, or its first.

onAction.description: A utility row was pressed: its item, whole.

workspaceMenuOpen.description: The menu the workspace chip opens is open: the chip's aria-expanded. The app opens it from `onWorkspace`.

profileMenuOpen.description: The menu the profile button opens is open: the button's aria-expanded. The app opens it from `onProfile`.

notes: The current row has aria-current="page"; the pill itself is aria-hidden and carries no text, so the place is announced once.
Labels are built from the UNCAPPED number — 'Inbox, 390 unread' — even when the eye sees 9+ or 1k+.
Collapsed, every row keeps its accessible name and gets a tooltip; nothing is icon-only to a screen reader.

Drill-in: the list is a <nav> named for where it is ('Mode', or 'Channels sections'). The top tile is a button named 'Channels. Back to the main menu', so the destination is announced where the logo was.
Drill-in: opening a destination or going back replaces the pressed row, so focus moves to the row that is now current instead of falling to the page. Escape in a destination's sections goes back.
The workspace chip and the profile button are menu buttons (aria-haspopup="menu"); their aria-expanded follows `workspaceMenuOpen` and `profileMenuOpen`, which the app sets while its menu is open.
The destination list scrolls when it does not fit, so the utilities and the profile stay in view. Every row, the utilities and the profile draw a focus ring.

examples.name: Variant 1 · flat, collapsed
examples.description: The destinations in one list. The sidebar button that widens it is in the title bar or the web top bar.

examples.name: Variant 2 · drill-in, inside Channels
examples.description: Channels' icon has taken the logo's place and its sections are listed under it. The tile goes back to the destinations.

examples.name: Variant 2 · drill-in, the destinations
examples.description: The menu level: the same rows as variant 1, but pressing one opens its sections. Expanded, a chevron on hover says so.

props.notice: UpdateNotice — Update available · Restart to update

edgeCases.title: Big counts in a 64px column
edgeCases.handling: Channels and Recordings print 9+. The Inbox prints its real number up to 999 and then 1k+ — never 999+, which is four glyphs and hangs nine pixels past the rail's hairline. The accessible name keeps the exact count.

edgeCases.title: No row is current
edgeCases.handling: The profile screen draws over the workspace and lights no row; the pill is not parked anywhere arbitrary — it is simply absent until a destination is chosen.

edgeCases.title: Long workspace, name or email
edgeCases.handling: The workspace pill hugs its text and ellipsises at the rail's width; the profile's name and email truncate on one line each. Full values are in the tooltips.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: The pill jumps to the new row instead of sliding, and the rail's width change is instant. Drill-in: the sections and the destinations swap in place, without sliding, and the tile appears without popping. Hover washes keep their 120ms fade, which is not motion.

edgeCases.title: Drill-in: a destination with no sections
edgeCases.handling: It opens directly, as in variant 1: the pill moves to it and the rail stays on the destinations, with no chevron on hover. Only a destination with sections gets a second level.

edgeCases.title: Drill-in: a section the destination does not have
edgeCases.handling: When `section` names none of the active destination's sections (an old link, a folder that was removed), the first section is current rather than none, so the rail always says where you are.

edgeCases.title: Read on another device
edgeCases.handling: Counts are server-owned: reading #design-crit on the phone lowers the Channels badge here, the Dock or taskbar badge and the tab title in one read-state event.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Desktop draws the rail from its SQLite cache with the last known counts; the web keeps what it has in memory. The profile's presence dot is hidden — this device cannot know anyone's presence — and Report a bug queues the report until reconnect.

edgeCases.title: Short window
edgeCases.handling: At 720px tall the rail still fits: the spacer shrinks to its 12px minimum first. Below that (web at high zoom) the destinations scroll inside the rail while identity, notifications and the profile stay pinned.

edgeCases.title: Touch laptop
edgeCases.handling: pointer: coarse keeps the 40px rows (already above the 24px minimum) and opens tooltips on long-press instead of hover; the collapsed rail never relies on hover to reveal a label.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: The rail is --surface-chrome on the darker page; the pill becomes --brand-soft dark (#382525) with the light coral label, and the hairline on the right edge stays the only seam.

web.base: A <nav aria-label="Main"> with a nested <nav aria-label="Mode">: every row a <button data-af-press> (aria-current="page" on the current one, a title as its tooltip) with Badge, Kbd and Avatar; inline styles over t, hover and focus from useInteraction. active, level and section are useControllable with onActiveChange, onLevelChange and onSectionChange; expanded is the app's, set by the web top bar's sidebar button (onSidebarExpandedChange). The pill is painted on the current row (no shared sliding indicator yet), and rows are buttons, not router links, since there is no href prop
notes: The same rail as desktop, under the web top bar rather than beside traffic lights. Every row is a real link — /assistant, /projects, /channels — so ⌘-click and middle-click open a destination in a new tab.
The active row comes from the route, not from state: Back in the browser moves the pill.

Desktop's jump chords mostly collide in a browser (⌘⇧T reopens a closed tab, ⌘⇧C is the inspector, ⌘⇧P a private window in Firefox, ⌘⇧M Chrome's profile menu). The web uses two-key sequences instead: G then A, P, C, M, T, R, I.
Report a bug on the web opens the same report flow without the native screenshot; it asks to capture the tab with getDisplayMedia and works without it.
The rail's width is opened and closed from the web top bar, by the sidebar button before Back, as shadcn's sidebar puts its trigger outside the sidebar. The rail holds only navigation.

The web screens draw the drill-in variant (variant 2) inside Channels. With routes, the destination, the level and the section are all in the URL (/channels/dms), so Back in the browser also steps back out of a destination.

keyboard.action: Opens the command palette
Drill-in: from a destination's sections back to the destinations, focus on the destination

keyboard.keys: G then A / P / C / M / T / R / I
keyboard.action: Assistant, Projects, Channels, Meetings, My tasks, Recordings, Inbox (not while typing)
Moves between rows inside the rail

desktop.base: The same @antfabric/ui-react component as the web: <button> rows over t with Badge, Kbd and Avatar, states from useInteraction; the width animates by a CSS transition and the labels fade in with enter("fade"). Drill-in: the sections slide in with enter("slide-left") and the destinations back with enter("slide-right"), the tile pops in with enter("pop"). The coral pill is drawn on the current row; the sliding indicator (useSlidingIndicator) and the destination icon's flight to the top are not in the kit yet
notes: Every row is 40px — a circle collapsed, a pill expanded (ADR-0300: the rail stays round; only the search field is squared).

The active pill is ONE element that slides between rows with a leading edge faster than its trailing edge, so it stretches toward the destination and settles (ADR-0517/0518). Rows paint nothing; the catalogue draws the pill on the active row because it cannot animate.
Colour: --brand-soft fill. Today's label is --brand, 3.11:1 on that fill, which fails AA; this spec uses --brand-active (the 'brand-strong' repair NavRail names, 5.40:1). Owner to confirm.
Badge caps come from the destination: 9+ for Channels and Recordings; the Inbox prints up to 999 and then '1k+', because the collapsed rail fits three glyphs and a fourth hangs over the seam.
UpdateNotice mounts here and renders nothing unless a release is waiting (it was once mounted nowhere, and an offered update drew nothing).

Pressing a destination sets `active` and the pill moves to it. The rail keeps it itself until the app passes it back (useControllable), and reports it through onActiveChange, so the catalogue preview is interactive.

The rail has no collapse control of its own: the sidebar button sits in the title bar, after the traffic lights (or ☰) and before Back, as shadcn's sidebar puts its trigger outside the sidebar. Its onSidebarToggle gives the app the width to pass as `expanded`, and the rail's width animates between 64px and 248px while the labels fade in. Today's desktop draws the button under the lockup (NavRail.tsx, a.toggleNav); this spec moves it.

Drill-in (variant 2), which the desktop screens draw: pressing a destination that has sections moves its icon onto the coral tile where the logo was and lists its sections under it (`level` 'sections'); expanded, the wordmark becomes the destination's name and the workspace pill a Main menu chip. The tile (an arrow on hover or focus), the chip and Esc go back to the destinations (`level` 'menu'). Each destination reopens on the section last open there. A destination without sections opens directly, as in variant 1.
Drill-in on desktop is new in this spec: today's desktop rail is flat, and each destination's sections live in the pane beside it (WorkspaceSidebar for Channels, the Inbox's folder column).
The workspace pill opens the workspace switcher (desktop-onboarding, ADR-5553). Collapsed, the pill is hidden, so the profile menu carries 'Switch workspace'.
Window chrome: under the macOS traffic lights the rail starts below the 44px title bar (title-bar).

notification-item.name: Notification item
notification-item.description: One row of the notification feed — the desktop NotificationRail and the phone's Notifications screen. Who, what, where and when on two lines; unread rows wear the warm tint, a coral tile and a dot; an agent asking for approval can be answered right in the row.

title.description: "Who · #channel", or just "Who" for a DM, rendered from ids so it reads right before the channel list has loaded.

sender.description: Who did it — the face on the row.

identity.description: The colour of the sender's initials when there is no `avatarSrc`. An agent is always drawn as one.

body.description: The server's bounded snippet. Two lines at most.
body.sample: @Arjun can you sanity-check the rollout plan before the 3pm train?

time.description: "just now", "4m ago", "3h ago", "2d ago" — the apps' agoLabel.

leading.description: avatar: the sender's face with a small badge. tile: a 32px glyph squircle, for an event that has no one to show (a meeting, a recording).

icon.description: The badge on the face, or the tile's glyph. Left out, the face has no badge. The icon only: behaviour reads the server's `data.kind`, never the category.

agent.description: The sender is an agent: its face, and no badge.

lead.description: Words before the body: "Replied in a thread".

revealed.description: The row's own actions are showing: on hover or keyboard focus (web, desktop), or swiped left (mobile).

approval.description: "" is not a request. pending shows Approve / Decline in the row; the rest are its outcomes.

decidedOn.description: Set when the approval was answered on another device, e.g. "your phone".

notes: The row is a role=listitem and needs a role=list around it (a `<ul>` or `<div role="list">` holding the rows): the kit draws one row, and a lone row has no list. A product that draws one row on its own wraps it.

When an approval is answered, Approve and Decline go: the outcome is spoken (through the page's announcer on the web, the screen reader's announcement call on the phone) and on the web focus moves to the outcome line, so a keyboard user is not dropped on the page.
The row's actions on the web are 11px buttons about 21px high; WCAG 2.2's 24px minimum needs the neutral theme's override, which raises them.
One accessible name per row: "Unread. Priya Raman · #platform-eng. @Arjun can you…. 4m ago". The dot and tile colour are never the only sign of unread.
Mobile exposes Mark read and Clear as accessibilityActions, so VoiceOver's rotor and TalkBack's actions menu reach what a sighted person swipes for.
