edgeCases.title: Nothing chosen yet
edgeCases.handling: An unanswered invitation lights nothing; pre-selecting an option would show a decision nobody made. Tab lands on the first option and Space or an arrow chooses. A required group with no answer says so under it on submit.

edgeCases.title: Arrow keys choose as they move
edgeCases.handling: WAI-ARIA radios select on arrow, so walking from Every message to Nothing passes through Mentions only. Writes are debounced 400 ms: that walk sends one request, not two, and the dot shows each step immediately.

edgeCases.title: A write in flight, or refused
edgeCases.handling: The dot moves at once. If the server refuses, it moves back with a toast: "Couldn't change notifications for #release-train. Try again." A group whose write must finish first (an RSVP to Google Calendar) is disabled while it runs, with a real disabled attribute so Space cannot fire either.

edgeCases.title: An option that cannot be chosen
edgeCases.handling: A disabled option stays visible, dimmed, with its reason as its description; arrow keys skip it. If the current value is itself not settable here (a channel posting policy set to specific roles in the admin console), the group is replaced by a sentence saying where it can be changed.

edgeCases.title: Long labels and narrow columns
edgeCases.handling: List labels wrap and the ring stays on the first line. Pills never wrap their own text; the row wraps instead, so a pill moves to the next line whole.

edgeCases.title: Changed on another device
edgeCases.handling: The per-channel level is an account setting: choosing Nothing on the phone moves the desktop's dot live, even with the menu open. A DM has no level on the server, so the control is never offered on a DM rather than offered and ignored.

edgeCases.title: Ring contrast
edgeCases.handling: The unchosen ring is border.default on desktop and border.muted (#DEDEDE) on the phone — 1.6:1 and 1.3:1 on white, under WCAG 2.2's 3:1 for a control boundary. The label identifies each option, but the gap is recorded rather than hidden; proposed fix for the owner: text.placeholder (3.3:1) for the unchosen ring on both.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: Rows grow past 44pt with the text and the ring stays aligned with the first line; descriptions wrap without limit.

edgeCases.title: Cards in a narrow column
edgeCases.handling: Cards take as many columns of at least `radioGroup.cardMinW` (220) as fit and wrap; narrower than one, a card is the column's full width. A long label wraps and its tags move under it whole. The phone always stacks the cards one per row.

web.base: role="radiogroup" over <button role="radio"> options (or pills), inline styles over `t`; roving tabindex and arrow keys that move and select, skipping disabled options; hover, press and focus from useInteraction; `value` through useControllable
notes: Pressing an option sets `value` (an `on.press` action, so the catalogue preview is interactive): the new dot grows from the ring's centre as the old one shrinks away, and a pill's ink fill cross-fades. Disabled options set nothing.

appearance="cards": each card is the <button role="radio">, in a CSS grid of as many columns of at least `radioGroup.cardMinW` as fit. Hover takes the edge to border.default; the chosen card's edge is the strong ink at 2px (a hairline plus an inset ring, so nothing moves), never the brand. The preview is aria-hidden; the card is named by its label and its tags (aria-labelledby), and its description is its aria-describedby.

keyboard.action: Enters the group at the chosen option (or the first, if none), and leaves it
Moves to and selects the previous / next option, skipping disabled ones
Selects the focused option when nothing is chosen yet

desktop.base: The same radiogroup as web; appearance="pills" draws the ChoicePills look (36px ink pills)
notes: pills: 36px, 14px padding, caption semibold. The chosen pill goes INK (surface.inverse), the design's one deliberate exception to coral selection — a wizard screen already has a coral primary button, and two corals cannot both mean "commit".
Only unchosen pills take the hover fill; hovering the pill you already chose would be feedback for an action that does nothing.
Disabled is a real disabled attribute, never pointer-events:none — a row that looks inert but still fires on Space only protects the mouse user.

Inside a menu the same choice is three menuitemradio rows with an 8px dot (ChannelPane's Notify me about), and the menu stays open after a choice — the dot moving is the confirmation. That is Menu's job; this component is the form version.
Pressing an option or pill sets `value`: the dot scales in from the ring's centre over 180ms as the old one shrinks out, and the chosen pill's ink fades in.

keyboard.action: Move to and select the next option
Enters and leaves the group

mobile.base: A View (accessibilityRole radiogroup) of Pressable rows (radio), StyleSheet over useTheme(); the dot scales in and out with Animated.timing; `value` through useControllable. Always the list — pills are web and desktop only
notes: Each option is a 44pt row: a 20pt ring with a 1.5pt stroke, a 10pt dot when chosen, 12pt gap, a 16pt medium label. The chosen ring is primary; the rest are borderStrong (#DEDEDE).
Radio buttons, not tabs (owner, 2026-10-15: "Tab isn't a right way to take the input").
Disabled dims the whole group to 45% and answers nothing; the person still reads the value.
The ring scales to 0.9 while pressed — the phone's press feedback on every target. Selection haptic on change.
Tapping a row sets `value`: the dot scales in from the centre while the previous one shrinks out.
appearance="cards" stacks the cards one per row, each a Pressable radio; `pills` is drawn as the list.

gestures.action: Chooses it; tapping the chosen row does nothing

reaction-pill.name: Reaction pill
reaction-pill.description: One emoji reaction under a message: the emoji and how many people chose it. Yours wears the soft coral fill and edge, and pressing the pill toggles yours. The add variant opens the emoji picker.

count.description: How many people reacted with this emoji. Server-owned; a pill at 0 is removed, never drawn.

mine.description: You are one of the reactors. Soft coral fill and edge; sets aria-pressed.

reactors.description: Who reacted, as one sentence: up to 50 names, then "and N others". You are "You". It is the hover card on web and desktop and part of the accessible name everywhere.
reactors.sample: Priya Raman, Marcus Chen and Aisha Bello reacted

variant.description: add is the smile-plus pill at the end of a reaction row that opens the emoji picker.

showReactors.description: Draws the who-reacted hover card open, above the pill. The catalogue cannot hover, so this is how the card is shown.

disabled.description: The message is still sending or failed, so it has no server id to react to.

onMineChange.description: Called with `mine` as the press leaves it: flipped, for a reaction (the add pill never calls it). Given `mine` too, the pill is controlled and the caller's count is the truth; otherwise it flips itself and moves its count by one.

onPress.description: The pill was pressed: a reaction toggles your reaction (through `onMineChange`), add opens the emoji picker.

onLongPress.description: Opens the Reactions sheet: who reacted, per emoji.

a11y.label: {emoji} {count}. {reactors}
notes: The pill is a toggle: aria-pressed / accessibilityState.selected says whether you reacted.
The name always carries the count: "👍 3. Priya Raman, Marcus Chen and You reacted"; the sentence is added when `reactors` is given.
Web and desktop: the who-reacted card opens on a resting pointer or on focus, is linked to the pill with aria-describedby, stays open while the pointer is over it, and Escape dismisses it.
On mobile the name ends with the hidden gesture: "Double tap and hold to see who reacted".

props.reactors: Marcus Chen and Aisha Bello reacted
You, Priya Raman, Kenji Watanabe, Sofia Herrera and Daniel Okafor reacted
You, Priya Raman and Marcus Chen reacted

edgeCases.title: Hundreds of reactors
edgeCases.handling: The sentence names up to 50 people and then "and 112 others", so the card is capped by content as well as by its 420px width. A name that will not wrap breaks anywhere rather than widening the card.

edgeCases.title: A count above 999
edgeCases.handling: The pill reads 999+ so a company-wide announcement does not grow a pill wider than the emoji row; the accessible name keeps the exact count.

edgeCases.title: Pressed twice quickly
edgeCases.handling: Each press flips the pill at once (optimistic) and the toggles are sent in order; if the server answers with a different count, its number wins and the pill settles without flashing. A press while the previous toggle is in flight is not dropped.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: A press while offline is refused with the offline toast and the pill does not change. A reaction that quietly never arrives would tell the author nothing while telling you they had seen it.

edgeCases.title: Reacted from another device
edgeCases.handling: The reaction event updates count and mine on every open client. Reacting on the phone turns the desktop pill coral without a refresh; removing it there removes it here, and a pill that reaches 0 leaves the row.

edgeCases.title: An emoji this device cannot draw
edgeCases.handling: A newer Unicode emoji on an older OS, or a custom workspace emoji whose image failed, shows its :shortcode: in the pill instead of a tofu box. The accessible name uses the emoji's name either way.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: The pill's 32pt height is a minimum; the run grows with Dynamic Type up to the app's 1.3× cap and the reaction row wraps onto another line rather than clipping.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard and screen reader
edgeCases.handling: Every pill is a real toggle button in the tab order; focus shows the who-reacted card immediately, without the hover delay, and the card's sentence is also the accessible name.

web.base: A <button aria-pressed> with inline styles over `t`; hover, press and focus from useInteraction. The who-reacted card is a role="tooltip" box: in flow above the pill with showReactors, floating above it after a 500 ms hover or at once on keyboard focus.
notes: The who-reacted card opens on hover after the app's tooltip delay and on keyboard focus with none, flips below the pill when it would leave the top of the timeline (96px margin), and is capped at 420px wide.
pointer: coarse (a touch laptop or tablet browser): no hover card; press and hold for 500 ms opens it instead, and the pill grows to 32px.
Not in the kit yet: flipping the card below the pill near the top of the timeline, the 420px cap (the card is 240 wide), and the coarse-pointer hold and 32px pill.

keyboard.action: Toggles your reaction
Moves through the reaction row; the add pill is last

desktop.base: The same <button aria-pressed> as web (one file, usePlatform), 22px from the desktop density tokens; the who-reacted card opens on a 500 ms hover or keyboard focus, or with showReactors.
notes: 22px tall, 9 radius, 11/12px SemiBold — today's ReactionChip. Yours is brand/soft with the brand/soft edge.
The hover card is an inverse card with the emoji above the sentence, exactly as the desktop draws it today; the add pill is new in this spec.
Pressing the pill toggles `mine` and moves `count` by one (optimistic): the coral fill fades in or out, and a pill that reaches 0 leaves the row. The pill pops in when it arrives.

keyboard.action: Toggles your reaction
On a focused message (the message cursor), opens the emoji picker — the add pill's job

mobile.base: Pressable with onLongPress, StyleSheet over useTheme() tokens (32pt pill, 1pt edge); usePress for the pressed fill; pops in with <Enter motion="pop">.
notes: A 32pt pill: "👍 3" as one 14pt SemiBold run in the text colour whoever reacted; yours is primarySoft with the borderBrand edge (V2 Figma).
No hover exists, so who reacted is the Reactions sheet on long-press, and the accessible name says so.
Light haptic on toggle, played by the app's onPress (the kit has no haptics dependency). A pending (local echo) message ignores the tap rather than dimming the pill a second time.
