search-field.name: Search field
search-field.description: The app's one search box: a recessed field with the glass at the start and one trailing slot that is either a clear button or a keyboard hint, never both. A slow search turns the glass into a spinner so the clear button stays put. The desktop rail's search is this field drawn as a button that opens the command palette.

value.description: Controlled when the caller passes onValueChange: the field shows `value` and asks for every change, and clearing is the caller's job (the ✕ reports onValueChange("") then onClear()). Given no onValueChange, the field keeps its own text.

placeholder.description: Say what is searched, not "Search" — the field is the only hint of what a screen holds.

label.description: Accessible name when it should differ from the placeholder. Falls back to the placeholder.

shortcut.description: A key that focuses or opens this search, written once as Mod+K or /. Drawn as a key in the trailing slot, hidden at rest and while there is text to clear.

busy.description: A search is in flight: the glass becomes a spinner. Off for instant filtering — a spinner that flickers on every keystroke is worse than none.

accent.description: Mark the edge while the field holds text — for a box narrowing a list you can see, where "why is this list short" is a real question.

launcher.description: Draw the field as a button that opens the command palette, like the desktop nav rail. A real input there would have to duplicate the palette's filtering or throw its first keystroke away.

focused.description: Draws the focused look (edge and shortcut hint) without real focus — for the catalogue and screenshots.

onClear.description: The ✕ was pressed (or Escape with text in the box), after onValueChange("").

onSubmit.description: Enter on web and desktop; the keyboard's Search key on the phone.

onPress.description: launcher only — opens the command palette.

a11y.label: {label || placeholder}
notes: The glass is decoration. While busy it becomes a progressbar named by strings.search-field.loading ("Loading"; a product that wants "Searching" sets it).
Enter submits and Escape clears the text, then blurs on the second press. When the clear button goes away with the text, focus moves to the field.

Inside a FormField with no label or placeholder of its own, the field's label names it, and it takes the field's description, error, aria-invalid and aria-required. Result counts are the product's to announce.

examples.name: Filtering a list
examples.description: accent marks the edge while the box narrows a visible list.

edgeCases.title: A slow search
edgeCases.handling: busy is set only for searches that go to the server, after 300 ms, and held at least 400 ms. The GLASS becomes the spinner, not the trailing slot, so the ✕ stays where it is — a search taking eleven seconds is exactly the one somebody wants to cancel. Still busy after 8 s, the results area says "Still searching…"; a failure says "Search didn't finish. Try again." with a Retry.

edgeCases.title: Two clear buttons
edgeCases.handling: The input is type="text" with role="searchbox". type="search" makes WebKit draw its own ✕ next to ours; appearance:none does not remove it. Do not tidy the type back.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Desktop searches its local SQLite cache and labels the results "Showing results on this device." The phone filters what is already loaded and says so in the same words. The web has no cache and says "You're offline. Search needs a connection." The field itself never disables — what was typed runs when the connection returns.

edgeCases.title: IME composition
edgeCases.handling: Searching waits for compositionend: while a Japanese, Chinese or Korean IME is composing, no query is sent and Enter confirms the candidate instead of submitting.

edgeCases.title: A long query
edgeCases.handling: The text scrolls inside the field; the ✕ stays visible at the end. Queries are trimmed and capped at 256 characters before they are sent.

edgeCases.title: / and ⌘K while typing elsewhere
edgeCases.handling: / focuses search only when no editable element has focus, so typing a / in the composer stays a slash. Mod+K works everywhere, including from the composer, because it has no meaning in text.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: 44pt is a minimum; the field grows with the text and the glass stays centred on the first line. The placeholder truncates rather than wrapping.

edgeCases.title: Screen reader result counts
edgeCases.handling: The count is announced once typing pauses, never per keystroke. Clearing returns focus to the field and announces "Search cleared".

web.base: <input type="text" role="searchbox" data-af-input> in a drawn box, inline styles over `t`; hover and focus-within from useInteraction; the ✕ is IconButton and the hint is Kbd, faded in on hover and focus while it holds its box; Escape clears then blurs, Enter calls onSubmit; launcher is a <button aria-haspopup="dialog"> laid over the whole field; `value` through useControllable
notes: type="text" with role="searchbox", NOT type="search": WebKit draws its own cancel ✕ beside ours as a shadow pseudo-element the kit cannot style (the owner: "I see two close icons").
Mod+K is not browser-reserved — a page may claim it, as Slack, GitHub and Linear do — so the web keeps ⌘K/Ctrl+K. It only works while the page has focus; from the address bar the browser keeps it.
Offline, the web has no local index: the results area says "You're offline. Search needs a connection." and the field stays usable for when it returns.

Pressing the field sets `focused` (the edge fades in, and the shortcut hint shows when there is one); pressing the ✕ sets `value` to "". Both are `on.press` actions, so the catalogue preview is interactive.

keyboard.action: Opens the command palette (launcher) from anywhere in the app
Focuses the page's own search, only when no editable element has focus
First press clears the query; second press blurs the field
Runs the search when results are not instant; otherwise opens the highlighted result
Moves into the results list

desktop.base: The same field as web, one geometry (36px, --radius-control); the rail launcher is the same <button> drawn as this field
notes: ONE geometry since 2026-09-25 (owner: "All the search field should have same height and same bg fill"): 36px, --radius-control, 16px glass inset 12px, 13px medium text. The old sm/lg sizes resolve to it.

Rest is --hover-surface and hover LIFTS to --surface-raised (the owner swapped them the same day). Focus is a 2px border.active edge and no halo; the hairline shadow is under every state, so the field never appears to lift on focus.
The ⌘K hint is hidden at rest and fades in (opacity, 120ms) on hover or focus, holding its box so the placeholder never stretches into the space. The catalogue draws it when focused is set.
accent + text gives a 1px border.active edge — one step under focus's 2px. Width is the only thing separating the two now the halo is gone; do not give accent the thick edge.
Offline, desktop searches its SQLite cache and the results header says "Showing results on this device."
The nav rail's Search is launcher: a button titled "Search people, channels, projects (⌘K)" opening the palette. Collapsed, the rail shows it as a bare glass icon button.
Pressing the field sets `focused` and the border.active edge fades in over 150ms; the ✕ clears `value`. The launcher has no catalogue action: it opens the palette.

keyboard.action: Opens the command palette
Clears the query, then blurs
Moves into the results list

mobile.base: TextInput with returnKeyType="search" (onSubmitEditing → onSubmit) in a View over a StyleSheet from useTheme(); focus is a 1pt inset boxShadow ring over the 1pt edge; the ✕ is IconButton; `value` through useControllable. No shortcut hint or launcher on the phone
notes: V2's search box: 44pt, 12pt corners, a hairline Rim and NO shadow, filled surface.hover; a 20pt glass in text.faint; 16pt medium text. Focus is the same 2pt border.active edge.
This spec adds the clear ✕ on the phone (32pt box with hitSlop to 44pt) — today's SearchInput has none.

Used as a screen subheader through SearchBar: outside the scroll view, so it stays put while the list moves under it. A filter button sits BESIDE the field, never inside — inside reads as a clear button.
No shortcut hint on the phone. On iPad with a keyboard, ⌘F focuses it through a UIKeyCommand.
Tapping the field sets `focused` (the 2pt edge fades in); tapping the ✕ clears `value` and keeps the keyboard up.

gestures.action: Focuses and raises the keyboard with a Search return key
Dismisses the keyboard (keyboardDismissMode on-drag); the query and filter stay

flows.title: Type to narrow a list, ✕ to clear
The rail's Search opens ⌘K

segmented-control.name: Segmented control
segmented-control.description: A pill track that switches the view of one pane: one raised card marks the chosen segment, and a segment may carry a count of how many are in it. Desktop slides that one card between segments; the phone fills the chosen segment in place.

items.description: [{ key, label, count? }]. count is how many are in there, never how many need you, so it is a quiet bordered chip and never the brand colour. 0 or missing draws no chip.

value.description: The chosen item's key. A value that matches no item is allowed and draws no card — for a strip whose panel can be closed.

size.description: md tabs are 32px tall and sm tabs 28px; the strip adds its 4px padding and hairline edge around them (42px and 38px). The phone has one size.

full.description: Stretch the track to its column. Segments share the SPARE width (flex 1 1 auto), so a long label keeps its words. Usual on phones.

scrollable.description: The track scrolls sideways instead of squeezing, for labels that cannot fit (localised copy, 130% text).

label.description: The strip's accessible name.

a11y.label: {label}
notes: Each segment is role=tab with aria-selected / accessibilityState.selected. The count chip is hidden and joins the tab's name instead: "Mentions, 3".

The strip is one tab stop; the arrow keys move to the neighbouring segment and choose it, and Home and End go to the first and last. In a right-to-left tree ArrowRight goes to the previous segment. There is no live region: the panel change is the feedback.
On the phone each segment's touch area is grown to 44pt without drawing more.

edgeCases.title: Labels that do not fit
edgeCases.handling: A label never wraps and never truncates first: a two-line tab changes the strip's height and moves everything under it. With full, short labels lend their spare width to long ones (Recordings needed 74 of 76px at the rail's 360px minimum). If the words still do not fit, the strip becomes scrollable rather than clipping a label.

edgeCases.title: A huge count
edgeCases.handling: The chip caps at 99+ so a segment cannot outgrow its neighbours; the exact number stays in the tab's accessible name. A count from a capped read (a 100-row page) is drawn 100+ — at least this many — never as a bare 100 that reads as a fact.

edgeCases.title: Nothing chosen
edgeCases.handling: A value that matches no segment draws no card at all. Never default to the first segment: a card under Files with no Files panel open is the control telling a lie. Tab then lands on the first segment.

edgeCases.title: Count still loading
edgeCases.handling: No chip until the count is known — never 0, never a skeleton. When it arrives the segment widens and the desktop indicator re-measures in the same frame, so the card never sits short of its segment.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: Segments grow taller with the text (font scale capped at 1.3×). A fixed three-way strip that no longer fits at 393pt switches to scrollable instead of wrapping.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: The desktop card jumps to the chosen segment instead of sliding; the label inks still cross-fade, since a colour change is not motion.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left languages
edgeCases.handling: Segments run right to left, ArrowRight moves toward the end of the reading order, and the desktop card slides leftward to the next segment.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard-only and screen readers
edgeCases.handling: Only the chosen segment is tabbable; arrows move and select. The focus ring is drawn on the segment, outside the card, so it is visible whether or not the card is under it.

web.base: role="tablist" of <button role="tab"> segments, inline styles over `t`; ONE card, measured after mount (and on resize), slides by transform to the chosen segment — on the server and the first paint the chosen segment draws its own card in the same place; roving tabindex with ArrowLeft / ArrowRight / Home / End (automatic activation); hover and focus from useInteraction; `value` through useControllable
notes: Web values are the desktop's (32px tabs inside a 42px strip). The web profile's taller controls do not apply: a tab strip is not a press target on its own row.
When the strip switches a routed view, each tab is a link (Tabs.Tab render={<Link>}) so the URL holds the choice and back/forward and a shared link land on the same tab.
Pressing a segment sets `value`, and the one card slides to it, 250ms ease-out.

keyboard.action: Moves to and selects the previous / next segment (automatic activation); wraps at the ends
Selects the first / last segment
Leaves the strip for the panel; only the chosen segment is in the tab order

desktop.base: The same tablist as web, at desktop density: the one card slides 250ms ease-out between segments
notes: The chosen card is ONE absolutely-positioned element that travels (ADR-0518); the segments paint no fill of their own.
Labels are semibold in both states so nothing changes width while the card is in flight; only the ink changes (text.strong chosen, text.faint not).
Today's desktop Tabs are plain buttons with no arrow-key handling; this spec adds the roving focus Radix Tabs gives for free.
This spec adds a label-ink hover for unchosen segments (text.muted). The desktop has none today; there is still no hover fill, because the card is the only fill in the strip.
A strip inside a segmented strip must be the underline Tabs instead — two grooves nested read as two peers.
Pressing a segment sets `value` and the single card slides to it. Until the strip has been measured (on the server, and the first paint) the chosen segment draws its own card in the same place.

keyboard.action: Moves to and selects the previous / next segment
Selects the first / last segment

mobile.base: A View (tablist) of Pressable segments, in a horizontal ScrollView when scrollable; StyleSheet over useTheme(); the chosen segment fills itself at once; on iOS 26 a PanResponder drives the selection lens (a clear GlassSurface at 1.15 scale that follows a horizontal drag and settles on the nearest segment); `value` through useControllable
notes: The fill does not travel on the phone: the chosen segment fills itself on the render after the tap, matching V2's FilterChips decision ("No smooth motion").
One size: 36pt tall (8 + 20 line + 8) with a 1pt edge on every segment, transparent when unchosen, so nothing moves when the choice does.
Today the phone draws a count chip even for 0; this spec hides it, as the desktop does — a chip reading 0 is a worse answer than no chip.
With scrollable, choosing a segment scrolls it fully into view.
Tapping a segment sets `value`. On the phone the card appears at once, with no transition, keeping the "No smooth motion" decision; only the label inks cross-fade.

iOS 26+: the selection lens, as on the tab bar — touching the control lifts the selected card into a clear-glass lens that can be dragged across the segments and settles on release, selecting that segment. iOS 18 and Android keep the plain tap.

gestures.action: Chooses the segment; an unchosen segment washes surface.hover while pressed
Scrolls the strip when scrollable

flows.title: Choose a segment and the list below follows

select.name: Select
select.description: Pick one value from a list. On web and desktop a trigger opens a panel drawn by this design — never the OS's own popup — the trigger's width, with the chosen row marked by a brand-coloured dot. On the phone the same trigger opens a bottom sheet of 52pt rows instead of a dropdown.

items.description: [{ key, label, supportingText?, icon?, color?, avatar?, identity?, agent?, disabled? }]. supportingText sits muted on the SAME line. One leading slot: icon (tinted by color, a token) or avatar (a photo URL; "" draws initials).

value.description: The chosen item's key. Controlled when the caller passes onValueChange.

label.description: Visible label above the trigger, and its accessible name. Required as a name even when not drawn.

size.description: sm 32px toolbar · md 36px · lg 44px dialog field. The phone has one 48pt trigger.

variant.description: field is the bordered box every dialog uses. chip is the ticket table's 26px recessed Status control — squared, not a pill. link has no box at all: the value and a caret, sized to the value, for a record's detail rail.

name.description: The name a form posts the chosen key under: the select writes a hidden field with it. On a phone-sized browser the native picker takes it.

open.description: Draws the panel (or the phone's sheet) inline under the trigger. On in the catalogue so the panel is visible; the kits own open state at runtime: the trigger toggles it, choosing a row, Escape, Tab or a press outside closes it.

placement.description: Where the panel opened. The kit measures the viewport — rows plus the search box — and flips above when it would not fit below.

activeKey.description: The key of the row under the keyboard / pointer cursor. Empty means the chosen row, which is where the panel opens.

searchable.description: A filter box pinned at the top of the panel. Off by default: a search box over five options asks you to type where pointing was faster.

query.description: What is in the filter box. items should already be the filtered list.

title.description: Why a disabled select is disabled — the one case a native tooltip is the right control.

onOpenChange.description: The panel (the phone: the sheet) opened or closed: by the trigger, a choice, Escape, a press outside, focus leaving, the sheet's close button or Android's back button.

onQueryChange.description: The filter box's text changed. Filter `items` to match: the select shows what it is given.

a11y.label: {label || placeholder}
notes: Web and desktop: the trigger is role=combobox with aria-haspopup=listbox, aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant; rows are role=option with aria-selected. Arrow keys, Home, End, Enter, Space and typing a letter work from the trigger; Escape closes and keeps focus on the trigger; Tab closes.

A searchable select moves focus into the filter when it opens. The filter names the list it drives (aria-controls) and the row under the cursor (aria-activedescendant); the arrow keys and Enter work from it, Escape clears the text and then closes, and Tab moves on and closes the panel.

Phone: the trigger is a button that opens a modal sheet (accessibilityViewIsModal). The sheet closes by its close button, the screen reader's escape gesture and Android's back button, as well as by choosing a row; its rows are radios.

Inside a FormField with no label of its own, the field's label names the select, and it takes the field's description, error, aria-invalid and aria-required. A disabled row is skipped by the arrow keys.

items.label: AF-1182 Auth token refresh loops on wake
AF-1204 SSO callback drops the deep link
AF-1219 Rotate the OAuth signing keys

examples.name: Opens above
examples.description: Near the bottom of the window the panel flips above the trigger.

props.label: Project
props.title: A channel filed under a project stays in it. Move it from the project.

edgeCases.title: Near the bottom of the window
edgeCases.handling: Before first paint the kit measures the space below the trigger against what the panel will need — rows × 40 + padding + the search box and any offer row — and flips above when it does not fit and there is more room above. An estimate that forgets the search box flips the wrong way near an edge.

edgeCases.title: Inside a scrolling list
edgeCases.handling: The panel is portalled to the document and positioned fixed, so the ticket table's scroller cannot clip a dropdown on its last visible row. If the trigger scrolls away while open, the panel closes — a panel left floating over the wrong row is worse than one that closed.

edgeCases.title: Long option labels
edgeCases.handling: Rows and the trigger ellipsize on one line; the panel never grows wider than its trigger. The full label is the row's tooltip on desktop and its accessible name everywhere. On the phone the label truncates and supportingText takes a second line.

edgeCases.title: No match, or nothing to choose
edgeCases.handling: A filter with no result says "Nothing matches “zzz”." in the panel, and the filter box keeps focus so the person can fix the typo. An empty list says "Nothing to choose from." — the trigger is still focusable so the reason can be read.

edgeCases.title: Many options
edgeCases.handling: The panel caps at 320px and scrolls, opening centred on the chosen row; type-ahead jumps by label. Past roughly fifteen options, or whenever scanning fails (every ticket in a project), turn on searchable. On the phone the sheet scrolls up to 90% of the screen.

edgeCases.title: The chosen value is gone
edgeCases.handling: A value that matches no item (a project deleted on another device) shows the placeholder rather than a stale label, and the form's save is refused with a reason until a new value is chosen. Changes arriving from another device while the panel is open update the rows in place and keep the active row.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Options that come from the server (people, projects) are read from the desktop's local cache with "Showing people on this device." under the search box; the web says "You're offline. Showing what was already loaded." A choice that needs the server to save is refused on the phone while offline, as every send is.

edgeCases.title: Screen reader and text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: The sheet is modal: focus moves to its title, the screen behind is hidden from VoiceOver and TalkBack, and choosing returns focus to the trigger. Rows grow past 52pt with the text and labels wrap to two lines before truncating.

web.base: A <button role="combobox"> trigger over a role="listbox" panel drawn in flow under it (column-reverse above), inline styles over `t`; the active row is aria-activedescendant, moved by the arrow keys, Home / End, type-ahead and pointer hover; searchable pins a SearchField; `value`, `open`, `activeKey` and `query` through useControllable. A phone-sized browser gets a native <select>
notes: The panel is drawn in flow under the trigger, exactly its width, and flips above a trigger on screen when its rows would not fit below. It is not portalled: a select inside a clipping container (a scrolling table) needs room for it.
On a phone-sized browser (pointer: coarse and under 600px wide) the web kit renders a native <select>, so the phone's own picker opens — the custom listbox is a desktop-pointer answer.
Never advertise a typed shortcut inside the panel that the browser owns; type-ahead letters are fine because the panel has focus.
Pressing the trigger toggles `open` and the panel pops in; pressing a row sets `value` and closes it. Disabled rows set nothing.

keyboard.action: Opens the panel on the chosen row
Moves the active row, skipping disabled rows
Jumps to the first / last row
Chooses the active row and closes
Closes and returns focus to the trigger
Type-ahead onto the labels
Closes without changing the value and moves on

desktop.base: The same combobox trigger and listbox panel as web — the kit's own, never a native <select>; Escape is captured (stopPropagation) so it does not also close the pane behind
notes: A native <select> cannot be styled: the OS draws its popup outside the page — a dark translucent menu on macOS, a flat white list on Windows. The owner: "I want the dropdown to be like this."

The panel is EXACTLY the trigger's width, left-aligned to it ("MAKE THE DROPDOWN ALIGNED WITH THE SELECTOR WITH SAME WIDTH AS THE SELECTOR"). Long options ellipsize. link gets a 200px floor; an icon-only trigger passes a panel width.
The chosen row gets a coral DOT, not a tick ("instead of the tick icon, let's have a dot"): a tick is the checkbox alphabet of the multi-select filter menu; one-of-many is a dot.
The ACTIVE row carries the wash, and pointer hover moves the same cursor as the arrow keys, so two rows can never be highlighted at once.
Hover is the fill (and the ink), focus is the 2px border.active edge; open does not change the border. Invalid beats focus. chip focuses with a 1px edge.
The panel opens centred on the chosen row (a 96-row time list opens at 4:00 PM, not at midnight), and flips above the trigger when the measured rows plus the search box would not fit below.
sm 32 / md 36 / lg 44 are the desktop's --control-h-sm / -lg / -input, which the shared token profile does not carry yet, so they are written as numbers.
Pressing the trigger toggles `open`; the panel pops in (fade and a 0.94 → 1 scale from its top edge, 220ms). Choosing a row sets `value` and closes.

keyboard.action: Moves the active row, skipping disabled rows
First / last row
Chooses and closes
Closes and returns focus to the trigger — captured so it does not also close the pane behind
Type-ahead

mobile.base: A Pressable trigger (the text field's 48pt box) and a sheet drawn under it that slides up through <Enter motion="slide-up">: grabber, title, an optional SearchField, then Pressable radio rows in a ScrollView capped at 90% of the screen; `value`, `open` and `query` through useControllable. The sheet is not a Modal: the screen places the Select where its sheet should appear, and the backdrop and focus return are the screen's
notes: No dropdown on the phone: a 48pt trigger (the text field's box) opens a bottom sheet. A popover anchored to a field is too small to tap reliably and lands under the keyboard.
The sheet: a grabber, the label as its title, then 52pt rows with the leading icon or avatar, the label, supportingText as a second line, and the same coral dot on the chosen row.
Choosing a row closes the sheet at once and returns VoiceOver / TalkBack focus to the trigger. There is no Done button — a single choice is its own confirmation.
searchable opens the sheet at full height with the search field focused and the keyboard up; otherwise the sheet is as tall as its rows, up to 90% of the screen, and scrolls.
For two to five options that should stay visible, use RadioGroup on the screen instead of a sheet.
The phone has no Select today; screens push a list or use RadioGroup. This spec is new on mobile.
Tapping the trigger toggles `open` and the sheet slides up from the bottom edge; tapping a row sets `value` and closes it.

gestures.action: Opens the sheet with a light haptic
Chooses it and closes

gestures.gesture: Swipe the sheet down / tap the backdrop
gestures.action: Closes without changing the value
Closes the sheet, not the screen

flows.title: Change a ticket's status from the table
Pick a project from the sheet

session-state.name: Session state
session-state.description: What a person sees when their session ends or needs them: expired, signing in through the browser (SSO), the phone's biometric lock, a suspended account, and the plain signed-out welcome — one compact card per state, with each platform's way back in.

state.description: waiting = the SSO hand-off is in the browser. locked = the phone's app lock.

returnTo.description: Where the web sends the person after sign-in — the URL they were on.

biometric.description: "Face ID", "Touch ID", "Fingerprint" or "Face unlock" — the OS's own name.

unlocked.description: The lock was just passed: the tile turns to an open lock in success green, the buttons go, and the app comes forward. What the Unlock button does in the catalogue; in the app onUnlock fires and the lock screen leaves.

error.description: Why the last attempt did not sign anyone in — the platform layer's sentence, verbatim.

offline.description: No backend answering: Sign in would do nothing, so the card says so.

notes: The reason and any error are spoken when they arrive, politely: on the web through the page's own announcer, on the phone through the screen reader's announcement call (the note is also role=status there). A change of state says the new title.

Focus does not move when the card appears: it would steal it from wherever the person was. When Sign in turns the card to waiting, the button that had focus goes, so on the web focus moves to the waiting status (and that is read instead of the title); the phone's sign-in sheet takes it from there.
The waiting spinner is hidden from assistive technology; the words beside it say what is happening.

edgeCases.title: One 401 is not a dead session
edgeCases.handling: A route can answer 401 for its own reasons. The client asks GET /api/v1/auth/session once and shows this card only when the gateway itself refuses the handle (ADR-0210); otherwise the failing request reports its own error and the person stays signed in.

edgeCases.title: The browser never comes back
edgeCases.handling: The waiting card stays with Open the browser again and Cancel. A hand-off that times out, a refused browser open, or a callback with the wrong state shows the platform's own sentence verbatim, so it can be reported accurately.

edgeCases.title: Offline when the session ends
edgeCases.handling: Signing in cannot work with no backend answering, so the button is disabled and the card says "You're currently offline." with the backend named. It never falls back to a demo or cached session.

edgeCases.title: Suspended or removed accounts
edgeCases.handling: A suspended person is not sent round a sign-in loop that can only fail: no Sign in again, just who can fix it. A removed account reads "This account has been removed. Contact your administrator if you think this is a mistake."

edgeCases.title: Expired in the middle of something
edgeCases.handling: Drafts stay where they are and come back after sign-in. A recording keeps recording on the device; its upload waits until the person is signed in again. Nothing is discarded by the session ending.

edgeCases.title: Biometrics fail or change
edgeCases.handling: A failed Face ID shows the OS's reason under the button and the person can retry or use the passcode. If biometrics are removed or re-enrolled in Settings, the lock falls back to the passcode; Sign out is always one tap away.

edgeCases.title: Signed out on another device
edgeCases.handling: Signing out of one device ends only that device's session. An administrator revoking every session ends them all; each app shows Your session expired the next time the gateway refuses its handle, including on the socket's 4401.

web.base: A role="region" card named by its title, inline styles over `t`, popping in with enter("pop"), with the kit's Button; Sign in again turns it to waiting (`state` through useControllable) while the route's same-tab OIDC redirect runs (TanStack Start beforeLoad → /sign-in?next=…)
notes: Sign in again keeps the URL: the current path rides in next= and the router sends the person back to it. Only a same-origin path is accepted, never an absolute URL, so the parameter cannot become an open redirect.
Drafts are kept in IndexedDB per user and restored only when the same person signs back in.

keyboard.action: Activates Sign in again

desktop.base: The same card as web at desktop density, with the kit's Button (lg, full); Login with AntFabric turns it to waiting while the system browser handles SSO and returns through antfabric://auth/callback (tauri-plugin-deep-link); Escape inside the card calls onCancel
notes: Staging builds register antfabric-staging:// (the committed default) and production passes VITE_DEEP_LINK_SCHEME=antfabric, so a staging and a production install on one Mac never steal each other's callbacks.
Only the hand-off id rides the custom-scheme URL — never a token. A callback whose state does not match the sign-in this window started is refused.
The reason line uses the gateway's refusal CODE, never its message: an ordinary expiry, account_suspended, or account_deleted.
"Open the browser again" and Cancel on the waiting card are new; today the Login screen says "Signing you in…" and waits.
In the catalogue the card pops in, and Login with AntFabric (Sign in again on the web) sets `state` to waiting, which is what the person sees while the browser has them.

keyboard.action: Activates the primary button
Cancels a waiting sign-in

mobile.base: <Enter motion="pop"> card, StyleSheet over useTheme(), with the kit's Button; `state` and `unlocked` through useControllable. The app runs expo-auth-session (ASWebAuthenticationSession / Custom Tabs) and expo-local-authentication around it
notes: The lock screen auto-prompts for Face ID / fingerprint when it opens, and falls back to the passcode when the hardware is missing or nothing is enrolled.
Signing in or out never draws a login screen at someone who is mid-sign-in: while the keychain read or the profile flush is outstanding, a loader shows instead.
Sign out unregisters this phone's push token first, or the next person would receive the previous person's notifications.
In the catalogue the card pops in; Login with AntFabric sets `state` to waiting, and Unlock (or Use passcode) sets `unlocked`, so the tile turns to an open lock and the buttons go.

gestures.action: Cancels; nothing is signed in

flows.title: The session expires, and you sign in again
The app is locked, and Face ID opens it

sheet.name: Sheet
sheet.description: A panel that slides in from the side of the window over a scrim: a record's details, a short form, a navigation drawer on a narrow window. Always modal: the page behind does not scroll and is out of reach until it closes. Not for a yes-or-no decision (Dialog) or a small panel that hangs from a control (Popover). The phone draws the BottomSheet.

open.description: The sheet is showing. ✕, Esc and a press on the scrim close it, unless `dismissible` is off.

side.description: Which edge it slides in from. end (the right in a left-to-right page) for details and forms; start for a navigation drawer.

width.description: The panel's width; 0 is the sheet.w token (480). A narrower window draws it full width.

title.description: The header's title. Empty draws none: a drawer names itself with `label`.

children.description: The body. It scrolls when it is taller than the window; the header and footer stay.

footer.description: The actions under the body, parted from it by a hairline, at the end of the row. Empty draws no footer.

label.description: The sheet's accessible name when it has no title (a navigation drawer: "Menu").

dismissible.description: ✕, Esc and a press on the scrim close it. Off while something must be finished first.

a11y.label: {title}
notes: Labelled by its title, else by `label`, else "Panel".
Modal: Tab wraps inside, the rest of the root is inert and hidden from assistive tech while it is open.

examples.name: Details with actions
examples.description: A person's details from a table row, with the footer's actions.

examples.name: Navigation drawer
examples.description: From the start edge, no title: it names itself.

edgeCases.title: Taller than the window
edgeCases.handling: Only the body scrolls; the header and the footer stay in view.

edgeCases.title: A window narrower than the sheet
edgeCases.handling: The panel is never wider than the window: on a phone-width browser it fills it.

edgeCases.title: Something must be finished first
edgeCases.handling: With `dismissible` off, Esc and the scrim do nothing and the ✕ is disabled; the footer's actions close it.

web.base: A role="dialog" aria-modal panel in the overlay layer of its AntFabricRoot, the window's height, sliding in from its side (enter("slide-left") from the end, "slide-right" from the start) over a scrim; header (title, subtitle, IconButton ✕), a body that scrolls, a footer. Tab wraps inside, Esc and a press on the scrim close it (the top overlay only), the page's scroll is locked and the rest of the root is inert while it is open; `open` through useControllable(open, onOpenChange)
notes: On the server, and in the catalogue's pictures, it is drawn in place in a 640 × 420 stage; in the browser it moves into the layer before the first paint.
Focus moves to the first control in the sheet when it opens and back to what opened it when it closes.

keyboard.action: Closes the sheet (when dismissible); focus goes back to the opener
Moves through the sheet and wraps inside it

desktop.base: The same panel as web at desktop density

mobile.base: The BottomSheet, with the title, the ✕, the subtitle at the top of the body and the footer under it; `side` and `width` are the web's. Drawn where it is mounted, as the BottomSheet is: the app presents it (a Modal or its navigator's sheet)

sidebar-item.name: Sidebar item
sidebar-item.description: One channel or conversation in the sidebar: a # or lock or a face, the name, and what it needs from you. Bold means unread, a coral count means someone asked for you, dimmed with a crossed bell means muted. Dense on desktop and web; on a phone it is a full-width row of one line, as V2 draws it today, with a second only while someone types.

name.description: The name. The row draws `glyph` before it.

glyph.description: A one-character text mark before the name, read with it ("#" for a channel). Empty draws none.

icon.description: A leading icon, not read ("lock", "users"). Empty draws none.

avatar.description: Draws the name's face, from `avatarSrc`, `identity`, `presence` and `agent`.

description.description: Read after the name, not drawn ("private channel").

agent.description: A conversation with an AI agent.

unread.description: Something new you have not read. Bold — unless muted.

mentions.description: Mentions, or every unread message in a DM. Shown even when muted.

draft.description: An unsent draft is waiting here.

active.description: This is the conversation on screen. Medium weight on a grey fill — never coral, which marks selection only in the nav rail.

selectedName.description: The row a surrounding list has selected — sidebar-section passes its `selected`. When set, this row is active exactly when it is the named one, whatever `active` says; empty leaves it to `active`.

typingText.description: What is read while someone types, and what the phone's second line says. Empty uses the `typing` string ("typing…"); a channel might say "Aisha is typing…".

actionsVisible.description: The row's ⋮ (Move to…, Mute, Leave), always shown when set. With `onMenu` alone it is there but transparent until the pointer is over the row or keyboard focus is in it; the room for it is reserved, so showing it never reflows the row.

onMenu.description: The row's options were asked for: its ⋮ was pressed, the context menu was opened on the row, or Shift+F10 or the Menu key was pressed on it. The app opens its menu (Move to…, Mute, Leave) from it.

notes: A button on every platform (there is no href prop): the row reports `onPress` and the app navigates. Middle-click and open-in-new-tab are the app's to add.
The whole row is one accessible name: '#design-crit, 3 mentions, muted, draft'. The glyph and the badge's own number are hidden so nothing is read twice.
The open conversation has aria-current="page" (selected on the phone); selection is never carried by colour alone. Pressing the open row leaves it open.

Web and desktop: with `onMenu` the row's ⋮ appears while the row has pointer hover or keyboard focus and stays in the tab order; the context menu and Shift+F10 or the Menu key on the row also call `onMenu`.
Phone: `onLongPress` is also an accessibility action, 'Options for #design-crit', so a screen reader, Voice Control or Switch Control user can run it.
Typing is announced only when the row is focused — a live region on every row would be noise.

edgeCases.title: Name longer than the sidebar
edgeCases.handling: One line, ellipsis at the end; the badge, draft and muted glyphs never shrink. The full name is the tooltip on web and desktop and the accessible name everywhere.

edgeCases.title: A huge count
edgeCases.handling: The count caps at 99+ — past that the exact number has stopped changing what anyone does.

edgeCases.title: Muted, with a mention
edgeCases.handling: Muting stops the bold and the sound for ordinary messages, never for someone asking for you: the coral count still shows on a dimmed row.

edgeCases.title: Unread in the channel you have open
edgeCases.handling: When the window is in the background or a pane covers the conversation, new messages still count. The row is bold and selected at once until the conversation is on screen again.

edgeCases.title: Read on another device
edgeCases.handling: Unread is server state. Reading on the phone sends one read-state event, and the desktop row loses its bold and count within a second — along with the Dock badge and the tab title.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left names
edgeCases.handling: The row mirrors: the # or face sits at the right, the count at the left. A name in Arabic or Hebrew inside an English sidebar keeps its own direction (dir=auto on the name).

edgeCases.title: Someone who no longer exists
edgeCases.handling: A deactivated colleague keeps their DM row in the neutral ink colour with no presence; a peer that never resolved reads 'Unknown user'. Neither can be typed to, and the row says so on open, not in the sidebar.

edgeCases.title: Typing, motion and offline
edgeCases.handling: Typing clears 6 s after the last heartbeat and is never shown while this device is offline (it would be stale). With reduced motion the dots stay still. Offline, rows draw from the on-device cache and presence dots are hidden rather than shown stale.

edgeCases.title: Hover-only ⋮ on touch
edgeCases.handling: On a phone the ⋮ does not exist: long-press opens the action sheet and swipe reveals Mark as read and Mute. On a touch laptop (pointer: coarse) the ⋮ is always visible on the open row and the row grows to 40px.

edgeCases.title: Text at 130% on a phone
edgeCases.handling: The row's height is a minimum: the name (and the typing line) grow and the row grows with them. Each stays on one line with an ellipsis; the glyphs and the badge keep their size and never wrap.

web.base: A <button data-af-press> row (aria-current="page" when open, one aria-label for the whole row) with Avatar and Badge, and the ⋮ IconButton laid over its right end as a sibling; inline styles over t, hover, press and focus from useInteraction. There is no href prop yet, so the kit's row is a button, not a link; the ⋮ reports `onMenu`, from which the app opens its Base UI <Menu>
notes: Right-click opens the same menu as the ⋮; the browser's own context menu is still one Shift+right-click away.

keyboard.action: Opens the conversation
Opens the row's ⋮ menu
Previous / next conversation in sidebar order (not while typing)

desktop.base: The same @antfabric/ui-react component as the web: a <button> row (6/10 padding, radius.row) + Avatar, Badge and the ⋮ IconButton as a sibling; inline styles over t, states from useInteraction. active is kept by the row (useControllable) and toggled by a press; a surrounding section decides through selectedName
notes: Unread is asked first: a channel you have open can still gather unread (window in the background) and then it is bold AND selected.

The ⋮ is a sibling button laid over the row's right end, never a button inside a button; the row reserves its room only while it is shown, so it never covers the count. The catalogue draws it with actionsVisible.
Muted and typing are new in this spec — today's sidebar has neither. Draft (pencil, fg.faint at 5.33:1, never an opacity) and the # / lock / face rules are today's.
The external-organisation glyph is new; it stays on even when the row is muted, because who can read the channel is not a notification preference.

Pressing the row makes it `active` (the grey selected fill fades in) and leaves it active if pressed again: the current page is not a toggle. Inside a sidebar-section the section's `selected` decides instead, through `selectedName`, so only one row is ever open.

keyboard.action: Opens the conversation
Previous / next conversation in sidebar order
Opens the row's ⋮ menu

mobile.base: A full-bleed Pressable (accessibilityRole button, accessibilityState.selected, onLongPress) with inset content: Avatar, Badge, Icon and Text in StyleSheet over useTheme() tokens, fonts by file. Swipe actions are not in the kit; the list wraps rows in swipe-row
notes: V2 today (owner, 2026-10-06) draws the name only — 44pt for a channel, 56pt for a DM — with no last message and no time, and so does the kit (2026-11-11): the last message and its time would need a backend change, so the row leaves them out. It grows to 64pt with a second line only while someone types.
A draft is the desktop's pencil at the end of the name line, since there is no preview line to begin with 'Draft:'.
There is no hover, so the ⋮ does not exist on a phone: long-press opens the row's action sheet and a swipe reveals the two commonest actions.
Light haptic on press-in; selection haptic when the swipe crosses its threshold.

gestures.action: Opens the conversation
Action sheet: Mark as read, Mute, Star, Move to…, Leave
Reveals Mark as read and Mute
Marks as read in one move, with an Undo toast

flows.title: Open #design-crit from the sidebar

sidebar-section.name: Sidebar section
sidebar-section.description: A group in the sidebar — Starred, Channels, Direct messages, or one someone made — with a header that collapses it. Collapsed, the header carries the section's unread total, because the rows that would have said so are gone; the conversation you have open stays visible underneath so you never lose your place.

icon.description: Drawn before the label, in the section's accent (a star for Starred). Empty draws none.

expanded.description: Whether the rows are shown. Collapsed (false), the header carries the section's unread total and only the open row stays.

selected.description: The key of the row that is open. Empty falls back to each item's own `active`, so a section built from data keeps working; pressing a row sets it.

unread.description: Unread across the section's rows, muted rows excluded unless they hold a mention. Drawn only while collapsed.

addLabel.description: The + action's name: 'Add channels', 'New message', 'Add to this section'. Empty uses the `add` string ("Add").

actionsVisible.description: Draws + and ⋯. On web and desktop the kit reveals them on header hover or focus-within (opacity, so revealing never reflows); on a phone they are always there.

divided.description: A hairline above the header, parting it from the section before. Off for the first section.

emptyText.description: Shown when the section has no rows, e.g. Starred before anything is starred.

items.description: SidebarItem props, one object per row, without `selectedName`, `actionsVisible` and the events: { key, name, glyph?, icon?, avatar?, description?, unread?, mentions?, muted?, draft?, active?, typing?, typingText?, external?, avatarSrc?, identity?, presence?, agent? }. The row that was opened is `onSelectedChange`'s.

onItemLongPress.description: A row was long-pressed: its key. The app opens the row's action sheet (Mark as read, Mute, Star, Move to…, Leave) from it.

notes: The header toggle carries aria-expanded; collapsed with unread, its name is 'Channels, 12 unread'.
The badge's own number is hidden; the toggle's name already says it.
Phone: `onMenu` (the long press on the header) is also an accessibility action, 'Channels options', and `onItemLongPress` is one on each row.
The + and ⋯ buttons are revealed while the header has hover or focus-within, by opacity, so they stay in the tab order. The list is a role=list of the rows.

props.label: Starred
props.emptyText: Star a channel or person to keep them here

edgeCases.title: Collapsed, with somewhere you are
edgeCases.handling: The open conversation stays as the one row under a collapsed header, so collapsing a section never hides where you are. Leaving it lets the row go.

edgeCases.title: The collapsed total
edgeCases.handling: Only drawn while collapsed — open, every row already says it. It counts unread conversations' messages, not muted rows, except that a mention in a muted row still counts: muting never hides someone asking for you. It caps at 99+.

edgeCases.title: Empty section
edgeCases.handling: Starred with nothing starred says how to fill it instead of drawing an empty header. A custom section emptied by moving its last channel out stays until deleted, with the same hint.

edgeCases.title: A very long section
edgeCases.handling: 200 channels render through a virtualised list; the header stays sticky while its rows scroll under it, so the collapse control is always reachable.

edgeCases.title: A long section name
edgeCases.handling: The label truncates; the chevron, the total and the actions never shrink. The full name is the tooltip and the group's accessible name.

edgeCases.title: Reordering
edgeCases.handling: Drag a header to move a section and a row to move a channel between sections. Every drag has a non-drag path: ⋯ › Move up / Move down for sections and the row's 'Move to…' menu for channels. On a phone, long-press the header.

edgeCases.title: Collapsed on one device
edgeCases.handling: Web and desktop share the account's layout, so a collapse on one shows on the other at the next sync. The phone keeps its own. A layout saved while offline wins over the server only if it is newer.

web.base: A role=group <div>: a header row holding the toggle <button> (aria-expanded) and the + / ⋯ IconButtons as siblings, then a role=list of SidebarItem rows; inline styles over t. Hover, focus and the actions' reveal (header hover or focus-within, by opacity) come from useInteraction and pointer/focus events, never :hover. expanded is useControllable with onExpandedChange; selected is kept by the section (onSelectedChange) and set by a row press
notes: Collapse state belongs to the account, not the browser: collapsing Channels on the web collapses it on the desktop app too. It is saved with the sidebar layout, the same record that holds section order and which channel lives where.
+ and ⋯ fade in on header hover or focus-within; they are in the layout at rest (opacity 0), so revealing them never moves the label.

keyboard.action: On the header: collapses or expands the section
On the header: collapses / expands, the tree convention
Header toggle, +, ⋯, then the rows

desktop.base: The same @antfabric/ui-react component as the web: a header row holding the toggle <button> and sibling + / ⋯ IconButtons (never a button inside a button), then SidebarItem rows; inline styles over t, states from useInteraction
notes: One component for all six kinds today — Starred, Channels, Projects, Direct messages, each project inside Projects, and custom sections.
The label is --text-body (14) semibold in fg.subtle, level with the rows under it (ADR-0670). The chevron matches the label's size and turns rather than swapping glyphs.
A hairline above each section (ADR-0689) with 12px of air above the rule (ADR-0691).
New in this spec: the open conversation stays visible under a collapsed header (Slack does this). Today a collapsed section hides every row.
Pressing the header toggles `expanded` (the chevron turns, rows fade back in); pressing a row sets `selected`, which moves the grey open-row fill to it and is the row kept under a collapsed header.

keyboard.action: Collapses or expands
Moves through conversations across sections, skipping collapsed ones except the open row

mobile.base: A View (role group): a Pressable header (accessibilityState.expanded, long press → onMenu) with an Animated chevron and the + IconButton, then SidebarItem rows in a list View; StyleSheet over useTheme() tokens. A long list virtualises in the app's own FlashList around it
notes: Today the Messages tab groups Channels and Direct messages with plain headings and no collapse; collapsing, Starred and custom sections are new on the phone.
No hover: + is always visible; ⋯ is replaced by long-pressing the header.
Collapse state on the phone is its own — a short screen wants different sections open than a 1440px window.

gestures.action: Collapses or expands, with a light haptic
Section actions: Rename, Sort, Move up, Move down, Delete (custom sections only)

flows.title: Collapse Channels and keep your place

skeleton.name: Skeleton
skeleton.description: A grey shape where data is about to appear — never invented content. It waits 300 ms before showing, stays at least 400 ms once shown, sweeps slowly unless reduced motion is on, and says what is loading to a screen reader exactly once.

shape.description: line a line of text (a pill), block an icon tile or thumbnail, circle a face, tag a tag or chip, panel a card or picture. row is the ListRowSkeleton preset: a lead, a title and a subtitle per row.

width.description: Shapes only. A length or a percentage; size it to what is coming.

label.description: What a screen reader hears, once — "Loading messages", not "Loading".

visible.description: Pass useSlowFlag(loading): false for the first 300 ms (laid out but invisible, so nothing jumps when it fades in), then true for at least 400 ms.

lead.description: Row preset: a face (circle), an icon tile (rounded square) or text only.

lines.description: Row preset: 1 a name-only row, 2 name and subtitle, 3 name and a two-line subtitle.

trailing.description: Row preset: a short line at the trailing edge — a notification's age, a message's time.

rows.description: Row preset: one entry per row, with its title and subtitle bar widths. The kit cycles 148/96/132/112/160/104 so a column of rows never reads as one stamp.

a11y.label: Loading messages
notes: One element, aria-busy and named by `label`, says what is loading; every shape inside is aria-hidden. A sighted reader sees shapes, a screen-reader user hears the sentence — nobody gets both or neither.

The sentence is spoken once, when the placeholder appears (visible turns true), through the page's own announcer on the web and the screen reader's announcement call on the phone. The element is not a live region, so a page of placeholders is not a page of them.
When the data lands, the element goes away; focus is not moved.

edgeCases.title: The data comes back fast
edgeCases.handling: Under 300 ms nothing shows — the group is laid out but invisible (visible=false), so a fast load never flashes grey. Once shown, it stays at least 400 ms so it never blinks.

edgeCases.title: Still loading after 8 seconds
edgeCases.handling: The shapes stay, and the pane adds one muted line under them: "Still loading. Check your connection." No spinner on top, no second skeleton.

edgeCases.title: The load fails
edgeCases.handling: The skeleton is replaced by the pane's error state ("Couldn't load conversations" with Try again). A skeleton never runs forever — a 30 s ceiling turns it into that error.

edgeCases.title: Data is already on screen
edgeCases.handling: A refresh, a revalidation or a reconnect never swaps visible rows for a skeleton. The cached rows stay; a quiet refresh indicator or the pull-to-refresh spinner says work is happening.

edgeCases.title: Offline with nothing cached
edgeCases.handling: A skeleton would never resolve, so it is not shown. The pane says "You're offline. This will load when you reconnect." and loads by itself on reconnect.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: The sweep stops and the shapes are still grey, exactly as Figma draws them. The fade-in (160 ms opacity) stays — it is not motion across the screen.

edgeCases.title: Screen reader
edgeCases.handling: Hears "Loading conversations" once, from the group; the shapes are hidden. A list of forty rows is still one announcement.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: Each bar sits in a line box of fontSize × 1.4 at the current scale, so the skeleton row is as tall as the real row it stands in for and nothing jumps when the text arrives.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: The fill is one step above the card in each theme (#2c2c2f on #222124) and the sheen one step above that, so the shape reads without glowing.

web.base: A role="status" aria-busy <div> fading in with enter("fade"), its shapes aria-hidden; the sweep is the af-sheen keyframes moving a linear-gradient band; inline styles over `t`
notes: Every shape starts at the same phase of the 1.4 s sweep (negative animation-delay from performance.now()), so a list sweeps as one surface rather than forty out-of-step bars.
A background tab pauses CSS animation for free; nothing to do.
Route loaders in TanStack Start resolve before paint where they can — a skeleton is for the waits that remain, not a substitute for prefetching.

desktop.base: The same <div> as web, at desktop density
notes: Today's desktop kit: a 120px band of skeleton.sheen crosses each shape every 1.4 s; under prefers-reduced-motion the keyframes end on their last frame, which parks the band off the shape — a still grey shape.
Never drawn over data already on screen: the SQLite cache paints first, and a refresh is a quiet indicator, not a skeleton.

mobile.base: A View (role status, busy) with hidden shapes; one shared Animated.loop moves a sheen band (sliced, since React Native draws no gradient) across every shape on screen, and is off under Reduce Motion
notes: One Animated loop drives every shape on screen, started by the first and stopped by the last — forty rows cost one animation. An invisible group does not run it.
Reduce Motion is read once (AccessibilityInfo) and shared: the shapes stop and stay grey.
SkeletonText sits each bar in the same line box the real Text takes (fontSize × 1.4), so nothing moves when the words land.

flows.title: A slow first read: nothing, then the skeleton, then the rows

spark-bars.name: SparkBars
spark-bars.description: A few bars with no axes, small enough to sit beside a number. The latest period is in full colour and the ones before it are quieter, so it reads as the number beside it, with the shape of what came before. Use it where each period is its own amount; a Sparkline is for a trend.

data.description: Rows, one per period, in order: [{ hour: 0, runs: 620 }, …]. The same rows can feed a chart, a table and a stat.

y.description: The field of each row that is the value. A value that is not a number is left out.

width.description: Px (points on the phone). The bars share it, so more periods are thinner bars.

animate.description: Draws in once when it mounts, unless the person reduces motion. Off by default: a page holds many, and a list of them would all move at once.

tone.description: default is the first series colour. positive and negative are the data palette's gain and loss, for bars that are good or bad whatever their height (cancellations are negative).

format.description: A format name, its options or a function, as core's `fmt` takes: how the default label prints the latest value, in the provider's locale. It is not drawn.

label.description: What a screen reader hears. Empty says how many periods there are and the latest value ("12 periods, latest 790"); say more where the number beside it does not ("Fabric runs by two hours, last 24h").

a11y.label: The `label` prop, or "12 periods, latest 790" (the value in `format`, in the provider's locale)
notes: The bars are a picture of numbers, so they are one image with a label, not a set of bars to tab through. The value beside them is what a screen reader reads.
An empty SparkBars is hidden from screen readers: it has nothing to say.

examples.name: Fabric runs, last 24h
examples.description: Two-hour blocks: the latest is the one in full colour.

props.label: Fabric runs by two hours, last 24h

examples.name: Tickets resolved by Fabric, by week

props.label: Tickets resolved by Fabric, last six months

examples.name: Wide
examples.description: More room, fatter bars.

edgeCases.title: No data
edgeCases.handling: An empty array draws an empty box of the same size, hidden from screen readers, so the number beside it does not jump.

edgeCases.title: One period
edgeCases.handling: One bar is the latest, so it is in full colour. It is no wider than a chart's widest bar (36px on the web, 26pt on the phone), not the whole frame.

edgeCases.title: Negative values
edgeCases.handling: Bars start from zero, so a loss hangs below the line. The scale is widened to hold both, and the latest is still the one in full colour.

edgeCases.title: All zero
edgeCases.handling: Nothing to draw: the bars have no height, and the box stays so the layout holds. Say so in the label ("No runs yet today") rather than rely on the picture.

edgeCases.title: Many periods
edgeCases.handling: The gap between bars closes up before the bars get narrower than 2px, so thirty bars in 96px are 2px bars with a gap of about 1px. Past about fifty at that width they get thinner than that: use a chart, since this is the shape of a few periods, not a series.

web.base: recharts' BarChart with no axes at an explicit width and height (never a responsive container), inside a <span role="img">; the earlier bars are Cells at a reduced opacity, never animated unless `animate`
notes: Shipped from the data subpath: recharts is a dependency of the React kit and is reached only from there.

desktop.base: The same recharts BarChart as web, at desktop density

mobile.base: react-native-gifted-charts' BarChart with its axes, rules and labels hidden and `disablePress`, in a View (accessibilityRole image); the earlier bars are the colour at a reduced opacity, never animated unless `animate` and the person has not reduced motion
notes: gifted-charts needs react-native-svg and expo-linear-gradient (or react-native-linear-gradient) in the app; the kit declares them as peers.
In the catalogue (React Native Web) it never animates: its Animated values do not reach the DOM.

sparkline.name: Sparkline
sparkline.description: A trend with no axes: a line, an optional flat fill and a dot on the last point, small enough to sit beside a number. It says which way something is heading, not what each point was; a chart does that.

data.description: Rows, one per point, in order: [{ week: "W35", mrr: 38200 }, …]. The same rows can feed a chart, a table and a stat.

y.description: The field of each row that is the value. A value that is not a number is left out.

area.description: A flat fill under the line: the line's colour at one opacity, never a gradient.

marker.description: A dot on the last point, ringed in the card's colour so it reads on any ground.

flush.description: Edge to edge, the fill running to the bottom: a trend bled into the foot of a card. Size it to the card's width.

animate.description: Draws in once when it mounts, unless the person reduces motion. Off by default: a page holds many, and a table of them would all move at once.

tone.description: default is the first series colour. positive and negative are the data palette's gain and loss, for a trend that is good or bad whichever way it points (a falling ticket count is positive).

format.description: A format name, its options or a function, as core's `fmt` takes: how the default label prints the first and last value, in the provider's locale. It is not drawn.

label.description: What a screen reader hears. Empty says where the trend starts and ends, in `format` ("Trend from 38,200 to 46,800"); say more where the number beside it does not ("MRR, last twelve weeks").

a11y.label: The `label` prop, or "Trend from 38,200 to 46,800" (the values in `format`, in the provider's locale)
notes: The line is a picture of numbers, so it is one image with a label, not a set of points to tab through. The value beside it is what a screen reader reads.
An empty sparkline is hidden from screen readers: it has nothing to say.

examples.name: Open tickets in #platform-eng
examples.description: Falling is good, so the tone is positive.

props.label: Open tickets in #platform-eng, last twelve days

examples.name: Bled into a card
examples.description: Flush: no margin, the fill to the bottom.

edgeCases.title: No data
edgeCases.handling: An empty array draws an empty box of the same size, hidden from screen readers, so the number beside it does not jump. It never draws a flat line: no data is not zero.

edgeCases.title: One point
edgeCases.handling: One value has no line, so it is a dot. It is the last point, so it takes the marker's look whether or not `marker` is on.

edgeCases.title: All equal
edgeCases.handling: A flat series draws a flat line in the middle of the frame, not along its bottom edge: the scale is widened around the one value.

edgeCases.title: Negative values
edgeCases.handling: A series that crosses zero draws as it is: there is no zero line, since a sparkline shows direction and not level. Say so in the label if the sign matters ("Net revenue, down to a loss").

web.base: recharts' AreaChart with no axes at an explicit width and height (never a responsive container), inside a <span role="img">; a flat fill, never animated unless `animate`
notes: Shipped from the data subpath: recharts is a dependency of the React kit and is reached only from there.

desktop.base: The same recharts AreaChart as web, at desktop density

mobile.base: react-native-gifted-charts' LineChart with its axes, rules and labels hidden, in a View (accessibilityRole image); a flat fill, never animated unless `animate` and the person has not reduced motion
notes: gifted-charts needs react-native-svg and expo-linear-gradient (or react-native-linear-gradient) in the app; the kit declares them as peers.
In the catalogue (React Native Web) it never animates: its Animated values do not reach the DOM.

stat-tile.name: StatTile
stat-tile.description: The compact KPI: an optional icon, a label and a period on top; the value with its change under it; and at most one visual, a sparkline or bars at the end, or a ring at the start. A dashboard holds many of them; the one headline number that leads a page is a KpiCard.

label.description: What is counted: "Open tickets", "Orders shipped". One line; a long one is cut with an ellipsis and is still the tile's accessible name.

icon.description: A lucide icon name, in a soft chip before the label. Empty draws no chip.

aside.description: A word at the end of the top row: the period the number covers ("24h"), or "Now".

value.description: The number, drawn by MetricValue. It eases to a new value.

format.description: A format name, its options or a function: what core's `fmt` takes. The symbol and unit of the printed value are drawn smaller and fainter than the digits.

delta.description: The change, as a number the delta format prints: -0.101 is −10.1%. Left out, the tile has no Delta and no period.

deltaFormat.description: The Delta's format (default a signed percent), for a change in points ("points") or a multiple.

inverse.description: Down is good (open tickets, response time): the Delta's colours swap. The arrow still points the way the number went.

period.description: What the change is against, after the Delta: "vs September", "since Monday".

trend.description: Rows for the visual at the end of the tile, one per period: [{ month: 4, mrr: 152400 }, …]. Used with `trendY`. On the phone it sits under the value and takes the tile's width.

trendY.description: The field of each row that is the value.

trendKind.description: line is a Sparkline with its fill and a dot on the last point, for a trend; bars is SparkBars with the latest period in full colour, for amounts per period.

progress.description: A share of a goal, 0 to 1: a ProgressRing at the start of the tile with the share in its middle, in place of a trend.

loading.description: Grey lines the size of the label, the value and the change, from the kit's Skeleton, in place of the numbers. Screen readers hear "Loading Open tickets" once.

a11y.label: The label; on the phone, "Open tickets, 142, Down 10.1% vs September"
notes: On the web the tile is a labelled group (not a landmark) and its parts read in order: the label, the value (once, plain), the Delta ("Down 10.1%, good"), the period. On the phone the whole tile is one element with that sentence, so one swipe reads a tile.
The visual is a labelled image ("Fabric runs, by period") and the value beside it is what carries the number.
Loading is a status named "Loading Open tickets", announced once; the extra grey lines are hidden from screen readers.

examples.name: Approvals waiting on Fabric
examples.description: Fewer waiting is good, so the Delta is inverse.

examples.name: Fabric runs, bars
examples.description: Bars: each two hours is its own amount.

examples.name: Q4 goal
examples.description: A ring at the start: 455 of 600 is 76%.

edgeCases.title: No comparison yet
edgeCases.handling: Without a `delta` the tile is a label and a value: no Delta, no period. It never shows 0%: a first period has nothing to be compared with.

edgeCases.title: A long label
edgeCases.handling: The label keeps one line and is cut with an ellipsis; the icon and the aside stay put. The full text is the tile's accessible name.

edgeCases.title: A trend with no rows
edgeCases.handling: An empty `trend`, or a trend with no `trendY`, draws no visual and the tile keeps its size. A ring (`progress`) takes the place of a trend: give one or the other.

edgeCases.title: Not loaded yet
edgeCases.handling: A value that is not a number draws an en dash at the value's size, and a Delta that is not a number reads "Change unavailable". Use `loading` while the request is in flight.

web.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a <section> drawn from the recipe: the Icon in a soft chip, MetricValue, Delta (badge, sm), and one of Sparkline, SparkBars or ProgressRing; Skeleton while loading
notes: Shipped from the data subpath. The visual at the end is a fixed size (92px for a line, 84px for bars); the tile around it takes whatever width its parent gives.

desktop.base: The same Card and <section> as web, at desktop density

mobile.base: The kit's Card (pad none) around a View: the Icon in a soft chip, MetricValue, Delta, and the visual stacked under the value at the tile's measured width, or a ProgressRing beside it
notes: The phone stacks a sparkline or bars under the value and stretches them to the tile; a ring stays beside it.
The Card is flat on the phone: the hairline border separates it, and `elevate` does not apply.
On the phone a dashboard lays two tiles to a row.

swipe-row.name: Swipe row
swipe-row.description: A phone list row that swipes left to reveal its actions: Mark read and Clear on a notification, Rename and Delete in chat history. The buttons slide in attached to the row's edge, and a closed row ignores rightward drags so the screen's swipe-back keeps working.

open.description: Draws the row swiped open, resting at the buttons' width. A row with no actions to show never opens.

unread.description: The row is tinted (unless `dense`), and the actions marked `unreadOnly` are shown. A read row offers one button fewer, so its tray is 96 narrower.

dense.description: One 44pt line, the title only, never tinted: a list of conversations rather than of notifications.

body.sample: @Aisha can you sanity-check the Android build before Priya cuts the branch?

icon.description: The glyph on the row's tile (mention, reply, DM, reaction…). Left out, there is no tile.

actions.description: The buttons, in order: SwipeRowAction { key, label, text?, tone?, unreadOnly? }. `label` is each button's accessible name and may hold `{title}`, filled with the row's title; `text` is what it draws. `tone: "danger"` is the destructive fill, and a press on it leaves the row open behind the product's confirm. `unreadOnly` shows it only while the row is unread. The tray is 96 wide per button shown and 12 more (108 for one, 204 for two); with none, the row does not swipe.

onOpenChange.description: A swipe or a tap opened or closed the row. The list closes whichever row was open before (one open at a time).

onPress.description: The row itself was tapped, or activated by a screen reader: open the notification. Given it, a tap on a row with its tray open closes the tray; without it a tap toggles the tray.

onAction.description: A button was pressed. The row closes first, unless the action's tone is danger. Called with the whole item, so the product switches on `action.key`: Mark read sets `unread` false, Clear deletes the notification on the server (no confirm: the source message is untouched), Delete asks to confirm first.

notes: The row is named by its whole line, "<title>, <preview>, <time>"; a double tap runs `onPress` (open the notification), or toggles the tray when there is none.

A swipe is invisible to VoiceOver and TalkBack, so every action is also an accessibility action on the row (the Actions rotor, TalkBack's actions menu), and so is the tray itself ("Show actions" / "Hide actions") when the row has an `onPress`.
Each button names its row, not just the verb: "Clear Marcus Chen mentioned you in #release-train".
Destructive buttons are crimson with a white label and are never the only cue: the word says what happens.
In a right-to-left layout the row swipes toward the right and the tray sits on the left.

edgeCases.title: Android's edge back gesture
edgeCases.handling: With gesture navigation, a swipe that starts at the right screen edge is the system back. Drags starting inside the system gesture inset (about 24dp) are left to the OS; start the swipe on the row's body to reveal actions.

edgeCases.title: Screen reader
edgeCases.handling: The row never needs a swipe: the actions are on the rotor / actions menu, and choosing one runs it directly without opening the row.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: Button labels stay one line up to the 1.3× cap ("Mark read" fits 88pt at 20.8pt); past that they shrink to fit rather than wrap. The notification row grows taller; the 44pt buttons stay centred in it.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Clear and Delete need the server, so offline they are refused with "You're offline. Try again when you're back." and the row closes unchanged. Mark read is queued locally and synced on reconnect, so the badge clears at once.

edgeCases.title: Changed on another device
edgeCases.handling: A notification read or cleared on the desktop updates this list live: an open row closes and drops its Mark read (sliding to 108), or leaves the list if it was cleared.

edgeCases.title: Scrolling while a row is open
edgeCases.handling: A vertical scroll that starts on a row scrolls the list, never half-opens the row (the pan activates on horizontal movement only); the open row stays open until another opens or it is tapped closed.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: The row still follows the finger — direct manipulation is not decorative motion — but snapping open or shut after release is instant.

edgeCases.title: Right-to-left
edgeCases.handling: Mirrored: swipe right to reveal actions on the left, and the back gesture comes from the right edge, so the closed-row rule applies to leftward drags instead.

web.alternative: Hover actions on the row, as the desktop notification rail does: hovering (or focusing) a notification reveals Mark as read and Clear as small buttons at its trailing edge, with Mark all as read and Clear all in the panel header; a chat-history row reveals a ⋯ with Rename and Delete. Touch-screen browsers get the same buttons always visible, since a horizontal swipe in a browser is the back gesture.

desktop.alternative: Hover actions, as today's notification rail: Mark as read and Clear appear on hover or keyboard focus at the row's trailing edge (Clear deletes on the server), with Mark all as read and Clear all in the header; chat history uses a ⋯ menu with Rename and Delete. Trackpad two-finger swipes are left to the OS and the app's history navigation.

mobile.base: PanResponder + Animated translateX over a Pressable row, StyleSheet over useTheme(); the buttons ride the row's trailing edge, `open` through useControllable, every action also an accessibility action
notes: Opens past 40pt at half drag speed (friction 2, a flick adding 0.05 s of its velocity, as gesture-handler's Swipeable does) and stops exactly at the buttons' width: 8 after the row, 88 per button, 8 between, 12 to the edge — 204 for two, 108 for one.
The buttons ride the row's trailing edge (translateX = width + translation), so they slide in with it instead of fading in behind it, as iOS Mail's do.

A tap on the row toggles `open` too (and closes an open row, as iOS Mail does), so the catalogue's previews stay pressable. Every action closes the row, except one with tone danger (Clear, Delete), which leaves it open behind the app's confirm. Mark read is the app's to apply: it sets `unread` false.

A closed row never takes a rightward drag, so a back swipe that starts on a row still goes back (ADR-9414); once open, 10pt to the right drags it shut. On Android a drag that starts in the 24dp system-gesture strip at the right edge is left to the OS.
One row open at a time: onOpenChange(true) is where the list closes the previous one. Give the row a solid background — the unread tint is see-through and is laid on top of the solid fill.

gestures.action: Opens and rests at the actions' width

gestures.gesture: Swipe right on a closed row
gestures.action: Ignored by the row — the screen's swipe-back takes it

gestures.gesture: Swipe right on an open row
gestures.action: Closes it
Runs it and closes the row (Delete in history asks to confirm first)
Opens the notification or conversation as usual
