Back returns to where you just were

toast.name: Toast
toast.description: A short sentence about something that just happened, on an ink pill that leaves by itself. One at a time. The mark agrees with the sentence — a tick for done, an exclamation for a refusal — and an optional action (Undo) lets you take it back.

message.description: Past tense for a confirmation, imperative for a fixable refusal, "what failed + whether to retry" for a failure. Never an identifier, a status code, a path or a service name.

tone.description: success: a tick on the brand disc. error: an exclamation on the danger disc, announced assertively. info: a neutral mark, for state (offline, refreshing).

actionLabel.description: One verb, usually Undo. With an action Dismiss shrinks to a ×; give `duration` a longer value for it than for a plain toast.

dismissed.description: Gone: the pill has left (faded and slid back the way it came). What Dismiss, the ×, Undo and, on the phone, a tap on the toast do in the catalogue; in the app the toast unmounts and onDismiss fires.

dismissible.description: Draws Dismiss. On mobile the whole toast is the dismiss target (tap it).

duration.description: How long the toast stays, in milliseconds, before it dismisses itself and fires onDismiss. 0 keeps it until it is dismissed. The clock stops while the pointer is on the toast or focus is inside it (web and desktop) and runs twice as long while a screen reader is on (phone).

onPauseChange.description: The pointer or focus entered the toast (true) or both left (false): for an app that keeps its own timer.

notes: The message is spoken when the toast appears or its text changes, through the page's own announcer on the web (success and info politely, error assertively) and through the screen reader's announcement call on the phone, where iOS has no live regions. The toast itself is not a live region: one that arrives holding its text is not read.

A toast never takes focus. On the web its action and × are buttons in the tab order; once dismissed the toast is inert, so they leave the tab order and the accessibility tree. On the phone Undo is also an accessibility action on the toast and its touch area is 44pt.

`duration` (0 by default, so no timer) pauses while the pointer is on the toast or focus is inside it (WCAG 2.2.1) and, on the phone, doubles while a screen reader is on. F6, Mod+Z and Esc are not built in: an app that wants them binds them to onAction and onDismiss.

props.message: Your message did not send. Try again.
Couldn't open the conversation. Try again.
You're offline. Showing what's on this device.

edgeCases.title: Several toasts at once
edgeCases.handling: Never a stack. Web and desktop show the newest and drop the older — except that a success never replaces an error still in its first 2 s; it waits behind it. Mobile queues oldest-first, 4 s each. Identical messages raised within the window collapse into one ("Link copied" three times shows once).

edgeCases.title: Screen reader
edgeCases.handling: Announced once, politely for success and info, assertively for errors, without moving focus. With `duration` set, the clock pauses while the toast is focused and, on the phone, doubles while a screen reader is on. Undo is also an accessibility action on mobile (VoiceOver rotor / TalkBack actions menu).

edgeCases.title: Undo, and the time to use it
edgeCases.handling: An Undo toast should be given a long `duration` (8 s is the product's); the clock pauses on hover and focus (WCAG 2.2.1). The action happens immediately and Undo reverses it — the toast is never a confirmation dialog in disguise. After it leaves, the action is final; Undo never appears for something that cannot be reversed (sending a message).

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Connectivity is said once by the connection banner, not by a toast per failed request. Desktop sends while offline go to the outbox without a toast. The phone refuses a send while offline and says so once, as info: "You're offline. Showing what's on this device." A burst of failures on reconnect is collapsed to one sentence.

edgeCases.title: Window hidden in the tray
edgeCases.handling: Do not show it. A toast nobody can see is not saved for later either — five stale toasts on reopen are noise. If the event matters to someone who is away (a message failed to send, a mention), it goes out as an OS notification through the notification settings; otherwise nothing. Same while the window is minimised or on another Space.

edgeCases.title: Tab in the background
edgeCases.handling: The toast is queued and its timer starts only when the tab becomes visible, so a 5 s message is not gone before anyone looks. Anything that must reach a person who left the tab is a browser notification (if granted) or the tab title count — never a toast.

edgeCases.title: Mobile app backgrounded or killed
edgeCases.handling: Toasts are not drawn while the app is in the background, and anything older than 10 s is dropped from the queue on return. A failed send becomes a local notification only if the app is backgrounded when it fails; a killed app shows nothing — the message itself is marked "Not sent" in the conversation.

edgeCases.title: Long or technical text
edgeCases.handling: Two lines at most, then an ellipsis. Names inside are cut to 32 characters on a word boundary; an upstream error that reads like a log line (a path, a uuid, an HTTP status, "the chat service") is replaced by the caller's plain sentence and sent to the console.

edgeCases.title: Over the composer
edgeCases.handling: Web and desktop sit bottom-centre but only the pill takes pointer events. Mobile sits at the top for exactly this reason; with the keyboard open it stays at the top rather than riding the keyboard.

edgeCases.title: Dark mode
edgeCases.handling: The inverse surface turns LIGHT in the dark themes, so the pill becomes light with dark text. The chips are mixed from the toast's own ink rather than white, so Dismiss never disappears. The marks sit on solid brand and danger discs, which keep their contrast on either pill; the phone's bare error glyph must take the light-theme danger ink on that light pill, not the dark theme's pale red.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: No slide: the toast fades in and out (150 ms). Timers are unchanged.

web.base: The ink pill: a role=status / alert <div> with aria-live, rising in with enter("rise"); Undo, Dismiss and the × are <button>s with hover and focus from useInteraction. Pressing one keeps `dismissed` inside and fades it back down; placement and the timer are the app's
notes: Bottom-centre, 24px up, one at a time. The fixed viewport is pointer-events: none and only the pill takes clicks, so the strip never eats the composer's clicks.

`duration` is the kit's timer: it pauses while the pointer is on the toast or focus is inside it and resumes with the time that was left. Starting it when the tab is visible, and queuing, are the app's.
Browser notifications are a separate, permission-gated channel; a toast is never used to say something the person must see after leaving the tab.
It rises into place from the bottom; Dismiss, the × and Undo set `dismissed`, and it fades back down.

keyboard.action: Reaches Undo and the × while the toast is up (the app can bind F6 or Mod+Z to onAction)

desktop.base: The same pill as web, at desktop density
notes: Today: one ink pill, bottom-centred, 5.2 s, Dismiss on the right. A second toast REPLACES the first (one timer).
The mark follows toastTone (ADR-4734): a failure no longer wears a tick. aria-live follows it too — polite for success, assertive for a refusal.
A progress toast ("Refreshing…", ADR-0783) has no timer and a 700 ms floor; finishing never wipes a different toast raised meanwhile.
Dismiss's fill is derived from the toast's own ink, so it survives the inverse surface turning light in the dark themes.
Copy rules live in toast-copy.ts: names cut to 32 characters on a word boundary, refusal codes mapped to plain sentences, log-line-shaped upstream messages never shown.
It rises into place from the bottom; Dismiss, the × and Undo set `dismissed`, and it fades back down.

keyboard.action: Reaches Undo and the × while the toast is up (the app can bind F6 or Mod+Z to onAction)

mobile.base: A Pressable pill (the whole toast dismisses) that drops in with <Enter motion="drop"> and fades back up with Animated.timing; Undo is its own Pressable and an accessibility action; placement, the queue and the timer are the app's
notes: At the TOP, at the safe-area inset + 8pt, 12pt from each side: at the bottom it sat over the channel composer and swallowed the tap meant for Send.
A FIFO queue, one at a time, 4 s each; tapping the toast dismisses it. Mounted under the auth overlay, so a toast never covers sign-in.
No Dismiss button and no hover; the action chip (Undo) takes its own tap and does not dismiss-then-act twice.
Before ToastHost existed, every toast() call went into an array nothing drew — a failed DM open said nothing at all.
It drops in from the top; a tap anywhere on it (or on Undo) sets `dismissed`, and it fades back up.

gestures.action: Dismisses
Dismisses
Undoes and dismisses, with a light haptic

toast-region.name: Toast region
toast-region.description: Where the app's toasts appear: a stack at one edge of the window, the newest nearest it, above dialogs and sheets, letting presses through between the toasts. The app keeps one region per window and puts its Toasts in it; each Toast keeps its own timer, pause and dismissal.

side.description: Which edge of the window the toasts stack on.

align.description: Where along that edge. end with top suits notifications that arrive while the app is in front.

max.description: The most toasts shown at once; the newest are kept, the older ones wait out of sight.

a11y.label: Notifications
notes: A landmark a screen reader can jump to. Each Toast is announced when it appears, through the kit's announcer.

examples.name: Top end
examples.description: Where notifications that arrive while the app is open are shown.

edgeCases.title: More toasts than max
edgeCases.handling: Only the newest `max` are drawn; when one is dismissed, the next older one comes back into view.

edgeCases.title: A toast over an open dialog
edgeCases.handling: The region is above the dialog's layer, and a press on a toast does not cancel the dialog.

web.base: A <section> landmark (named "Notifications") in the overlay layer of its AntFabricRoot at z.toast, above modal dialogs and sheets; a column at the chosen edge with pointer-events only on the toasts; a press on it is not a press outside an open overlay. In place, in a 560 × 240 stage, on the server and in the catalogue's pictures
notes: Toasts announce themselves through the kit's one announcer; the region does not add a second live region.

desktop.base: The same region as web at desktop density

mobile.base: A View stacking the toasts at its edge, pointerEvents box-none; drawn where it is mounted: the app lays it over its screen inside the safe area

tooltip.name: Tooltip
tooltip.description: The name of an icon-only control, in a small ink bubble, after a 320 ms rest on hover and at once on keyboard focus. It wraps the control it belongs to: the control is described by the bubble, and Esc, blur, a press and leaving close it.

label.description: The words the bubble says: the same as the control's accessible name when it has no visible text.

shortcut.description: A shortcut drawn inside the bubble after the label, written once as Mod+Shift+M. The trigger also gets it as aria-keyshortcuts.

side.description: Which side of its control the bubble hangs on. The kit does not flip it at the window's edge: a product that needs that passes the side it computed.

showTrigger.description: With no children: draws the icon button the tooltip belongs to, with the bubble in flow beside it, as the catalogue shows it.

children.description: The control the tooltip belongs to. The bubble floats beside it, opens on its hover (after a short rest) and keyboard focus, and the control is aria-describedby it.

open.description: The bubble is showing. Hover and keyboard focus change it; set it to draw the bubble open (the catalogue does).

notes: The bubble is role=tooltip and the control is aria-describedby it. When the control's own name already says the label, the bubble's label text is hidden from the description, so only what is more (the shortcut, in words) is read: a screen reader does not say everything twice.

WCAG 1.4.13: dismissible (Esc, without moving focus), hoverable (the bubble sits flush with the control and is inside the same host, so moving onto it does not close it), persistent until the pointer or focus leaves or Esc.
A disabled control should use aria-disabled rather than disabled, so it still receives pointer events and its tooltip can say why.

edgeCases.title: Long label
edgeCases.handling: Over 34 characters the bubble wraps at 260px instead of growing across the window. Most labels are two or three words; a sentence belongs in data-tip only when the accessible name must be long and the tooltip short.

edgeCases.title: Near the edge of the window
edgeCases.handling: If the preferred side does not fit, the opposite side is used; if neither fits, the preferred side stays. The bubble is then clamped 8px inside the window on the cross axis, so a control in the top-right corner gets a bubble below it that slides left.

edgeCases.title: Keyboard focus
edgeCases.handling: On :focus-visible the tooltip shows at once — the delay exists to stop a sweeping pointer from opening ten, which a Tab press cannot do. Esc hides it and keeps focus. Pressing the control hides it.

edgeCases.title: A control that draws its own hover card
edgeCases.handling: An avatar or @mention opens a hover card after 380 ms; a tooltip at 320 ms would arrive first and cover it. Such triggers carry data-tip="" — an empty string is a decision, not a missing value.

edgeCases.title: Disabled control
edgeCases.handling: Native disabled buttons stop receiving pointer events in some engines, which would hide the one tooltip that matters. Controls use aria-disabled, and the tooltip says why: "Only channel admins can archive #release-train".

edgeCases.title: Touch on a laptop or tablet
edgeCases.handling: A tap never shows a tooltip — it would flash under the finger. pointerType touch is ignored; a long-press on an icon-only control shows the label as on the phone.

edgeCases.title: Scroll, resize, switching windows
edgeCases.handling: Any scroll (capture phase, so an inner list counts), resize, pointerdown, keydown or window blur hides the bubble at once. A trigger that unmounts during the delay never shows one: the timer checks the element is still connected and has a size.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion and dark mode
edgeCases.handling: With reduced motion the 120 ms fade is dropped. In dark mode the ink bubble inverts to the light inverse surface with dark text, so it still reads as "not part of the page".

web.base: A <div> wrapping the control (`children`) with a role="tooltip" bubble that the control is aria-describedby; it opens after a 320 ms rest on hover and at once on :focus-visible, closes on Esc, blur, press and leave, and the bubble itself is hoverable; inline styles over `t`, Kbd (inverse) for the shortcut; fades in with enter("fade"); `open` through useControllable(open, onOpenChange). With no children it draws a built-in IconButton and the bubble in flow
notes: Hover opens it only where (hover: hover) holds and the pointer is not touch — a phone browser or a tap on a tablet never flashes one.
The kit does not remove a `title` the control carries: leave it off a control that has a Tooltip, or the browser draws a second bubble.
Shortcuts inside the bubble follow the web's alternatives, never a browser-reserved key.
The bubble floats flush to its control (no gap to cross, so it stays open while the pointer moves onto it) and does not flip at the window's edge.

keyboard.action: Shows the tooltip for the focused control at once, without the delay
Hides it without moving focus

desktop.base: The same bubble as web at desktop density, with ⌘ glyphs on macOS
notes: The trigger is the Tooltip's `children`: the first button, link, field or [role=button] in it takes aria-describedby and aria-keyshortcuts.
320 ms delay; labels wrap at the recipe's 260px max width with a 1.35 line height.
The bubble fades in (no slide or scale: a label should not travel); the catalogue's Replay plays it.
Hidden immediately on pointerdown, Esc and blur. The app's tooltip host (not built here) also hides on scroll, resize and window blur.
z-index is the top of the stack (above toasts), so a tooltip is never under a dialog that is open.

mobile.alternative: No hover on a phone. Every icon-only control already carries an accessibilityLabel, which VoiceOver and TalkBack read; an accessibilityHint adds what it does when the name alone is not enough. A long-press on an icon button shows its label as a callout above the finger (the iOS 17 / Android 14 pattern), with a light haptic — and only for icon-only controls, so long-press stays free for rows.

flows.title: Rest on an icon button to read its name

tray-menu.name: Tray menu
tray-menu.description: The desktop's menu-bar extra (macOS) and system-tray menu (Windows, Linux): what the recorder is doing, how much is unread, recording controls, pausing notifications, and the way back into the window. The macOS menu-bar title follows the recorder, so the timer is readable without opening anything.

appName.description: The app's name: the menu's accessible name.

items.description: Every row, in order: `{ key?, type?: "item" | "separator" | "label", label, icon?, text?, count?, filled?, tone?: "danger", disabled?, submenu? }`. A `label` row is a dimmed readout; `count` is the right-hand detail (read after the label); `filled` draws the glyph solid (`danger` is the record glyph); `text` is drawn when it differs from the accessible name; `submenu` opens a menu of its own.

tone.description: The tray icon: idle is the plain dot, live the red one, paused the amber, busy the blue.

statusText.description: Beside the macOS status item: "Recording 0:12". "" draws none.

date.description: The picture's date: the macOS menu bar draws "date clock".

clock.description: The picture's clock: the macOS menu bar draws "date clock", the taskbar "clock".

openMenu.description: The key of the row whose submenu is open. "" is none.

onSelect.description: A row was pressed (a row with a submenu opens it instead).

onOpenMenuChange.description: A submenu opened or closed: the key of the open row, or "".

notes: Disabled readout rows (status, unread, paused until) are how a native menu says "this is information"; screen readers read them as dimmed items.

The menu is one Tab stop: the arrows move inside it, and Tab leaves it. Each submenu is its own menu with the same keys, and focus returns to the row that opened it. Closing the whole menu is the OS's: the kit draws the picture of it, so Escape at the top level is the app's.
The tray icon and the status bar around the menu are a picture of the OS and are hidden from assistive technology; the tooltip text is the app's to set on the real tray icon.

edgeCases.title: The timer ticks
edgeCases.handling: The recorder pushes a snapshot every 250 ms. A state change rebuilds the menu; a tick only retexts the status line, the macOS title and the tooltip, and only when the text actually changed — so an open menu never flickers or closes under the pointer.

edgeCases.title: Saving after Stop
edgeCases.handling: Stopping reads "Saving…" in the menu and the menu bar until the file is written; Start stays disabled until then, so a second recording cannot start on top of a save.

edgeCases.title: The window is hidden in the tray, or on another Space
edgeCases.handling: Show / Hide AntFabric reveals with show → unminimize → focus (the order tao needs), including from a fullscreen Space; the same reveal a Dock click and a notification click use. Hiding never quits, and the socket stays connected so notifications still arrive.

edgeCases.title: No tray on this Linux desktop
edgeCases.handling: Stock GNOME shows no tray icons without the AppIndicator extension. Then the tray cannot be the way back: closing the window minimises instead of hiding, so AntFabric is never left running with nothing on screen to reach it.

edgeCases.title: Windows hides new tray icons
edgeCases.handling: Windows 11 puts a new app's icon in the ^ overflow. The first time the window is closed to the tray, a one-off toast says "AntFabric is still running. You'll find it in the system tray."

edgeCases.title: Quit while recording
edgeCases.handling: Quit stops the recording and waits for the save ("Saving…") before the process exits; audio is never discarded by quitting. If the save fails, the next launch's recovery reports "A partial recording was saved."

edgeCases.title: Pausing from the tray
edgeCases.handling: Pause notifications ▸ works with the window hidden: it writes the same server-side pause as the in-app menu, so every device goes quiet. While paused the item becomes a dimmed "Notifications paused until 9:00" and Resume notifications. Custom… opens the window at the picker.

edgeCases.title: Dark menus
edgeCases.handling: The menu is drawn by the OS in its own theme; the bar icon is a template image on macOS so it inverts with the menu bar, while the record, pause and stop glyphs are fixed colours chosen to read on both.

edgeCases.title: Liquid Glass and earlier macOS
edgeCases.handling: The tray menu is a native NSMenu, so macOS chooses its material: glass on 26+, vibrancy before. Nothing to build; the preview shows both.

edgeCases.title: The Mac's Liquid Glass settings
edgeCases.handling: A native NSMenu: macOS applies Clear or Tinted, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast to it by itself.

web.alternative: A browser has no tray. The tab title count and the favicon dot carry the unread count (App badge), Pause notifications lives in the notification rail's settings menu, and a recording runs only while its tab is open — the tab's own recording indicator is the status.

desktop.base: A drawing of the macOS menu-bar extra or the Windows / Linux tray and its menu, picked by usePlatform().os: a `role="menu"` of `<button role="menuitem">` rows, inline styles over `t`, the highlight from useInteraction, Up / Down / Right / Left handled on the menu, Liquid Glass through glass() on macOS 26, and a fade-in with enter("fade"). Presses move the recorder and the pause in local state. The app builds the real one with Tauri TrayIconBuilder + muda Menu (MenuItem, IconMenuItem, Submenu, PredefinedMenuItem::separator), rebuilt on a recorder state change and retexted in place on each 250 ms tick.
notes: Ships today: the status line, Start / Pause / Resume / Stop Recording, Open Recordings Folder, Show / Hide AntFabric, Quit AntFabric. New in this spec: the unread line and Pause notifications ▸.

macOS: the menu-bar title is set only while recording, paused or saving ("Recording 0:12") — menu-bar width is shared with every other app. Idle writes an empty string explicitly, because set_title(None) is a no-op on macOS and once left "Saving…" there for the life of the process.
The unread count goes in the menu, never in the menu-bar title; the Dock badge already carries it.
Transport glyphs are images, not emoji, painted mid-grey (record in red) because a muda menu-item image is not a template image and would vanish in one of the two menu themes.
Windows and Linux show the tooltip "AntFabric Recorder — 00:00:12" on hover instead of a title.
Windows: left-click on the tray icon shows or hides the window, right-click opens this menu. macOS: either click opens the menu.
macOS 26+ (Tahoe): the menu-bar extra sits on a transparent menu bar and its menu is Liquid Glass, drawn by macOS. macOS 15 and earlier: vibrancy. The Windows tray menu is unchanged.

In the catalogue the menu fades in; Pause notifications ▸ toggles `submenu`, a duration sets `notificationsPaused` (and an example `pausedUntil`, counted from 10:42), and Start / Pause / Resume / Stop move `recorder` through its states.

keyboard.action: Windows: focuses the notification area; Enter or Shift+F10 opens the menu
Moves through the enabled items, and wraps; a letter jumps to the next item that starts with it
Activates the item
Opens the submenu of the row that has one (and moves into it); Left or Escape closes it and gives focus back to its row. The keys swap in a right-to-left tree

mobile.alternative: A phone has no tray. The home-screen badge carries the count; a running recording is an iOS Live Activity (Lock Screen and Dynamic Island timer) and an Android ongoing foreground-service notification "Recording 0:12" with Pause and Stop; Pause notifications lives in Profile.

typing-indicator.name: Typing indicator
typing-indicator.description: The line between the timeline and the composer that says who is writing right now: one name, two names, or "Several people". Three dots pulse beside it; under reduced motion they hold still.

names.description: First names of the people typing in THIS conversation (or this thread, in the thread panel), oldest first. Never includes you — not even from your other device.

notes: Not a live region. Typing changes every few seconds and announcing it would talk over somebody reading or dictating; a screen reader finds it by moving to it.
The dots are hidden; the accessible text is the sentence without the ellipsis. The bounce stops when the person turns on Reduce Motion, on the phone as it is turned on.

edgeCases.title: A very long name
edgeCases.handling: The name truncates and the verb never does — "is typing…" is the part that carries the meaning. The accessible name keeps the full name.

edgeCases.title: You are typing on another device
edgeCases.handling: Your own participant id is filtered out, so typing on the phone never shows "Priya is typing…" to Priya on the desktop.

edgeCases.title: Someone stops without sending
edgeCases.handling: A "stopped" removes them at once; a lost "stopped" (closed laptop, dead socket) still lapses after 8 s, because the list is always read through the TTL, never straight off the last event.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: There are no typing events offline, so the slot shows the offline notice instead ("AntFabric is offline right now. Check your internet connection. Anything you type stays here until you're back online.") and the typing list is cleared. On reconnect the slot is empty until a fresh "started" arrives.

edgeCases.title: Reduced motion
edgeCases.handling: prefers-reduced-motion (and iOS Reduce Motion / Android Remove animations) holds the dots still at three fixed opacities — the drawing in this catalogue. The words already say what is happening.

edgeCases.title: Typing in a thread
edgeCases.handling: A reply being typed shows in that thread's panel or screen only. The channel's own slot is for top-level messages, so a busy thread does not make the channel look busy.

edgeCases.title: Text scaled to 130%
edgeCases.handling: The slot grows to fit one line at the larger size; it stays one line and the name truncates first.

web.base: Plain flex row, inline styles over `t`; the dots are the kit's af-bounce keyframes (1.2 s, 160 ms stagger) and rest at .35 / .65 / 1 under reduced motion; the sentence is read from a visually hidden span, the dots and ellipsis are hidden
notes: A background tab still receives typing events but sends none; the dots animate only while the tab is visible (no work for a hidden tab).
Two tabs on the same channel are one person: the server keys typing by participant, so you never appear twice to others.

desktop.base: The same row as web, inline styles over `t`, in the channel pane's status slot; dots on af-bounce
notes: Today the desktop draws a static coral "•••" and the sentence in italic faint caption text; this spec animates the dots.
A typer lapses 8 s after their last "started" (TYPING_TTL_MS); senders re-arm every 4 s and send "stopped" after 5 s idle, on send, or on blur.
When the window is hidden in the tray nothing is drawn or animated; the slot is recomputed from live typers when it shows again, so a stale "is typing…" never greets you.

mobile.base: View labelled with the sentence, Text, StyleSheet over useTheme(); the dots with Animated.loop on the native driver, staggered 160 ms, held still under Reduce Motion
notes: The phone app does not show typing today. It sits directly above the composer, under the timeline, and does not push the list: it occupies a fixed 28pt slot that is always reserved, so the last message never jumps.
The app only listens while the conversation screen is focused and in the foreground; backgrounding clears the list.

flows.title: Someone starts typing, then sends

update-banner.name: Update notice
update-banner.description: How each platform says a new version is ready, without interrupting: the desktop rail card that walks from Update available to Restart to update, the web's Reload line that never fires mid-typing, and the phone's over-the-air update card with its restart sheet — plus the case where only a store update will do.

stage.description: Desktop uses available → downloading → installing → ready (or failed). The phone adds checking, latest and store-required. The web only knows available and failed.

progress.description: Download percent; -1 when the server sent no length.

error.description: The updater's own sentence, verbatim. Left out, the card says the `errorDefault` string ("The update could not be installed.").

expanded.description: The notice is the card. Left (false) is the nav rail collapsed to 64 px: an icon with a dot.

confirm.description: The Restart to apply? sheet is open.

onStageChange.description: Called with `stage` as the press leaves it: downloading after Install or Retry (desktop), checking after Check again (phone). Given `stage` too, the notice is controlled and the updater's own events move it; otherwise it moves itself.

onApply.description: Desktop: install the waiting release, or retry a failed one. Phone: open the store for a store-required version.

onRestart.description: Desktop: Restart to update relaunches onto the installed release. Web: Reload. Phone: Restart now in the sheet.

notes: A change of stage is spoken when it happens, through the page's own announcer on the web and desktop (a failure assertively, with the updater's reason read out after the title) and through the screen reader's announcement call on the phone for a failure, the latest-version note and the store notice. Progress is not read out percent by percent. The card is not a live region itself: one that arrives holding its text is not read.

The card's button is named by the whole action ("Restart to update to version 0.43.0") and described by the title and the detail line, so reaching it reads the failure too. The web's reload line is announced the same way.
On the phone Android's back button puts the restart sheet away.
The detail line truncates for sighted readers only; the full error is in the DOM and in the tooltip.

props.error: The update signature could not be verified.

edgeCases.title: Never reload under someone's typing
edgeCases.handling: Reload happens only on the button. A composer with focus or text holds off even the out-of-date case until it is empty and blurred; drafts are persisted per conversation and come back after the reload.

edgeCases.title: Several tabs on the web
edgeCases.handling: Every open tab shows the line; reloading one does not reload the others. A service-worker update activates only once no tab is on the old build, so a tab in the background is never swapped out from under its owner.

edgeCases.title: Restart while recording
edgeCases.handling: Restart to update is held while a recording runs: the desktop card reads "Restart after recording" and does nothing until it stops; the phone's sheet already says to finish a recording first, and Later is always there.

edgeCases.title: The download has no length
edgeCases.handling: With no content length the detail reads "Downloading…" instead of a percentage; the card is not clickable while downloading or installing.

edgeCases.title: A long failure
edgeCases.handling: The updater's sentence is shown verbatim (so it can be reported accurately), truncated to one line in the rail with the whole of it in the tooltip and to screen readers. Clicking the card retries.

edgeCases.title: Offline, or no updater in this build
edgeCases.handling: A check that cannot reach the server leaves the notice hidden on desktop and web; on the phone, Check for updates reports the failure under the button. A build with no updater configured says nothing at all on desktop and "Updates are not enabled in this build." on the phone.

edgeCases.title: The last update would not start
edgeCases.handling: If expo-updates fell back to the embedded bundle (isEmergencyLaunch), the card says "The last update couldn't start, so AntFabric is running the version it shipped with." and Check for updates fetches a fresh one.

web.base: A role="status" inverse pill, inline styles over `t`, fading in with enter("fade"), with the kit's Button for Reload; the app pins it bottom-left and compares the build id against /version.json on each route change and every 30 min
notes: Reload is the person's choice. The page is never reloaded for them while a composer has focus or holds text — drafts are already saved per conversation, so Reload brings them back.

Only when the server says the running build is too old to talk to it (an API version below the minimum) does the line change to "This version of AntFabric is out of date. Reload to keep going." — still a button, still waiting for an idle moment.

keyboard.action: On Reload: reloads; drafts are restored

desktop.base: A <button> card (role="status", or "alert" when failed) for the foot of the nav rail, inline styles over `t`, rising in with enter("rise"); a non-pressable busy card while downloading or installing; a 40px rail <button> with a dot when collapsed. Hover and focus from useInteraction, `stage` through useControllable; the app drives it from the Tauri updater plugin
notes: Renders nothing unless a release is genuinely waiting: a failed launch check, or a shell with no updater configured, stays idle and silent.
No dismiss, by the owner's design (ADR-0294): a waiting update stays until it is installed or the app restarts.

The card rises in. Pressing Update available (or a failed one) moves it to downloading at once and calls onApply; downloading → installing → ready then follow the updater's events through `stage`. The busy card is not pressable. Restart to update calls onRestart, which relaunches.
The title must fit a 127 px column at the 15 px top of the type ladder — every stage title is one line, nowrap.
Collapsed rail: the same glyph with a dot, never a number — there is only ever one release waiting.
The running app re-checks periodically, not only at launch; an app nobody quits otherwise never learns a release exists.

keyboard.action: Installs, restarts or retries, by stage

mobile.base: A View card with the kit's Button, StyleSheet over useTheme(); the Restart to apply? sheet slides up with <Enter motion="slide-up"> and follows a downward drag (PanResponder + Animated) to put itself away. `stage` and `confirm` through useControllable; the app drives it from expo-updates
notes: OTA updates replace the JavaScript only. A change to native code bumps runtimeVersion, and the phone is then told to update from the store — an OTA cannot deliver it.
Restarting is optional: an update that has downloaded applies on its own the next time the app opens.
In the catalogue Check for updates moves latest or failed to checking, Restart to apply update sets `confirm` so the sheet slides up, and Later puts it away.
In a development build expo-updates rejects every call, so the card says "Updates are not enabled in this build." rather than pretending it checked.

gestures.action: Same as Later

flows.title: A release is waiting: install it, then restart onto it
Check for updates, then restart to apply

web-top-bar.name: Web top bar
web-top-bar.description: The strip across the top of AntFabric in a browser tab. Back, Forward and History drive the browser's own history, search opens the command palette, and on the right sit Help, a way into the desktop app, and the ⋯ app menu. No window controls and no drag region — the browser owns the frame.

canGoBack.description: False at the first in-app entry of this tab, even when the browser could go further back (to a sign-in page, say).

history.description: Draws the Recent history button after Back and Forward.

search.description: Draws the search field in the middle (its magnifier alone while `compact`).

searchPlaceholder.description: The field's text. Empty uses the `searchPlaceholder` string ("Search"); a product says what it searches.

searchKeys.description: The palette shortcut shown in the field. '/' is the fallback where the browser keeps Ctrl+K.

compact.description: Search collapses to its magnifier, a labelled action to its icon and Recent history leaves the bar. The bar does this itself below 768px wide, so it fits a phone-width window; `compact` forces it at any width.

actions.description: WebTopBarAction: IconActionItem and `showLabel`: { key, label, icon, badge?, disabled?, showLabel? }. Buttons before the ⋯ menu: an icon button, or a ghost button with its label while the bar is not `compact` when `showLabel` is on.

workspace.description: Names the banner and the ⋯ menu ("GeekyAnts menu"). Empty names the menu "Menu".

menuOpen.description: The ⋯ app menu is open (see app-menu-bar).

sidebarExpanded.description: The nav rail is open (248px with labels). The sidebar button before Back draws panel-left-close then, panel-left-open otherwise, and its name says which way it goes.

menu.description: What the ⋯ button opens, drawn under it while `menuOpen`. Leave it out when the app draws its own popover.

trailing.description: Transient status at the end of the bar, before the actions.

onSidebarExpandedChange.description: The sidebar button was pressed, with the width it leaves the rail: pass it to NavRail as `expanded`.

onMenuOpenChange.description: ⋯ was pressed, with `menuOpen` as it leaves it.

notes: The ⋯ button is a menu button: aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded follow `menuOpen`, with aria-controls on the menu while it is open. Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the button, and a press outside closes it.

Back and Forward are natively disabled when there is nowhere to go, so they are announced as dimmed and leave the tab order. A 'Skip to conversation' link is the app's to draw before the bar; the bar draws none.
The bar compacts itself below 768px wide (a labelled action becomes its icon, search its magnifier, Recent history leaves), so it does not scroll sideways at 320px.

examples.name: Sidebar open
examples.description: The nav rail is expanded, so the sidebar button offers to collapse it.

edgeCases.title: Browser Back versus in-app Back
edgeCases.handling: One stack: the in-app buttons call history.back() / forward(), so they and the browser's arrows always agree. The in-app Back stops at this tab's first AntFabric entry; the browser's Back can still leave. A deep link opened in a fresh tab starts with Back disabled.

edgeCases.title: Ctrl+K belongs to the browser on Windows and Linux
edgeCases.handling: Chrome, Edge and Firefox use Ctrl+K (and Ctrl+E) for the address-bar search. The page takes Ctrl+K while it has focus, but with focus in the address bar, or in Firefox with the search bar shown, the browser keeps it. '/' always works outside a text field, and the field's hint switches to '/' after Ctrl+K has failed to reach the page once.

edgeCases.title: Narrow window (under 768px)
edgeCases.handling: Search collapses to its magnifier and 'Open in desktop app' to its icon, each keeping its full name as tooltip and accessible label. Back, Forward and History never collapse. At 320 CSS px (400% zoom on a laptop, WCAG 1.4.10) the bar still fits without horizontal scroll.

edgeCases.title: Several AntFabric tabs open
edgeCases.handling: Each tab is the whole app with its own history. A BroadcastChannel elects one leader tab to play sounds, show browser notifications and own the favicon dot, so three tabs never ring three times; read state and drafts sync across tabs through it. Closing the leader hands the role on within a second.

edgeCases.title: Desktop app not installed
edgeCases.handling: The antfabric:// link fails silently in Chrome and Edge, so if the tab still has focus 1.5 s after 'Open in desktop app', the bar swaps to 'Get the desktop app'. Safari shows an error sheet for an unknown scheme, so on Safari the bar shows 'Get the desktop app' until one open has succeeded. A successful open is remembered per browser.

edgeCases.title: Background tab
edgeCases.handling: Nothing in the bar is live. Unread lives in the tab title, '(3) AntFabric', and the favicon dot (tab-badge), which is what a person sees from another tab.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Back and Forward still work for routes already loaded. Search opens the palette with recent places only and says 'You're offline. Showing recent places.' 'Open in desktop app' stays — the desktop app has its own offline cache.

edgeCases.title: Touch laptop and keyboard-only
edgeCases.handling: pointer: coarse raises every icon button to 40px and the bar to 52px. Keyboard users get the skip link first and a visible focus ring on every control; F6 is the browser's (address bar) and is never bound by the page.

web.base: A <header role="banner">: IconButton for the sidebar button, Back / Forward / History, Help and ⋯; the search field is a <button> with a Kbd hint (an IconButton when compact); Button (ghost, sm) or IconButton for the desktop app. Inline styles over `t`, hover / press / focus from useInteraction, `menuOpen` and `sidebarExpanded` through useControllable. The app wires onBack / onForward to TanStack Router (router.history.back / forward, useCanGoBack).
notes: Back and Forward ARE the browser's history — every in-app navigation is a router push, so the buttons, the browser's own arrows, a mouse's side buttons and a trackpad swipe all walk one stack and can never disagree.

The app writes its own index into history.state on each push. Back is disabled at index 0 — the first in-app entry of the tab — so the in-app button never leaves the app, even when the browser's Back could return to the SSO page.

History (the clock) lists the last 20 places visited in this tab and the ones the account visited on other devices, newest first; choosing one is a push, not a jump back. The desktop's ⌘Y for it is not bound on the web: it is Chrome's own History on macOS.
The ⋯ menu is the app menu (app-menu-bar): Preferences, Keyboard shortcuts, Theme, the desktop app, Help, Sign out. Never Reload, Zoom or Quit.
Pressing ⋯ toggles `menuOpen`, so the button holds its pressed look while the app menu is open.

The sidebar button, first in the bar, opens and closes the nav rail: outside the rail, where shadcn's sidebar puts its trigger. onSidebarExpandedChange hands the app the width for NavRail's `expanded`, which it keeps in the same cookie as before.
The search field is a button that opens the command palette, as on desktop. The hint shows Mod+K; on Windows and Linux its tooltip adds 'or /'.

keyboard.action: Opens the command palette while the page has focus
Opens the command palette when no text field has focus — the fallback where Ctrl+K stays with the browser
The browser's own Back / Forward; the app does not intercept them, and they walk the same stack as the buttons
The sidebar button, Back, Forward, History, Search, Open in desktop app, Help, ⋯ — in that order, after the skip link

desktop.alternative: title-bar. The desktop app draws its own window frame: traffic lights or window controls, a drag region, the ☰ menu on Windows and Linux, and the same Back / Forward / History / Search cluster.

mobile.alternative: mobile-header. In the native app each tab has a large-title header with the bell and your photo; pushed screens get a back chevron. A phone-sized browser is offered the mobile app instead of a squeezed web top bar.

flows.title: Back walks the browser's own history
The ⋯ opens the app menu

workspace-switcher.name: Workspace switcher
workspace-switcher.description: Slack's way between organisations: one tile per workspace, each with its own unread count, ⌘1 to ⌘9 to jump, and a + to add another. On desktop the tiles stack in the rail; in a browser each workspace lives at its own address, so it is a menu of links; on a phone it is a sheet from the header photo.

workspaces.description: Every workspace this device has signed into, in the person's own order: { key, name, host, identity?, current?, mentions?, activity?, signedIn?, src? }. Empty draws only the add tile (the web menu: its title and the add row). mentions is coral; activity is new messages that nobody asked you about.

current.description: The key of the workspace this window is in. Empty falls back to each workspace's own `current`; pressing a signed-in workspace sets it (a signed-out one starts sign-in instead and changes nothing here). Given with onCurrentChange it is controlled: the app confirms the switch, then passes the new key.

showShortcuts.description: Holding ⌘ (Ctrl) for 400 ms labels each tile with its ⌘1–⌘9.

addLabel.description: The add tile's (desktop and phone) or add row's (web) name. Empty uses the `add` string on desktop and the phone ("Add a workspace") and `addMenu` on the web ("Sign in to another workspace").

onCurrentChange.description: A workspace was chosen, signed in or not: its key, so the app can look up the workspace (host included) and sign in there. A signed-out workspace fires it too and leaves `current` where it was. In a browser a plain click is the app's to navigate; ⌘-click and middle-click follow the row's link into a new tab without firing it.

notes: Each tile's name says everything a sighted person reads off it: 'Northwind Health, 3 mentions, Command 2'.
The current tile has aria-current; the black ring and the left bar are never the only signal.
Signed-out tiles stay focusable and say 'signed out' — choosing one starts sign-in.

Web: a role=menu named by its 'Workspaces' heading (which sits outside the menu) holding menuitemradio links, the current one checked, and the add row. The menu is one tab stop (the current row); Up, Down, Home, End and typing a letter move between rows. Truncated names and hosts are in each row's tooltip.
Phone: a sheet (accessibilityViewIsModal) of buttons with the current one selected.

edgeCases.title: Only one workspace signed in at a time (today)
edgeCases.handling: Until per-origin stores land, only the current tile is live; every other tile is drawn signed out, without a count, and choosing it runs the confirm-sign-out-reload switch. The design is ready for counts; the data is not.

edgeCases.title: Two workspaces with the same initials
edgeCases.handling: Northwind Health and Nimbus Hub both read 'NH'. Tiles take the workspace's uploaded icon when there is one and otherwise differ by identity colour; the tooltip and the accessible name always carry the full name.

edgeCases.title: More than nine
edgeCases.handling: ⌘1–⌘9 cover the first nine in the person's order; the tenth onward have no chord. The column scrolls inside the rail above the destinations, and tiles reorder by drag or by 'Move up / Move down' in the tile's context menu.

edgeCases.title: Switching mid-task
edgeCases.handling: A switch is refused while a recording is running ('Stop the recording first — it belongs to GeekyAnts') and waits for uploads in flight. Drafts survive, as they survive sign-out today; they hold server ids that simply match nothing in another instance.

edgeCases.title: A mention in another workspace while hidden in the tray
edgeCases.handling: With multi-sign-in, the Dock / taskbar badge counts all workspaces and the notification says 'Northwind Health · #triage'. Clicking it switches and opens the message; with one-at-a-time, it asks to switch first.

edgeCases.title: SSO expired in one workspace
edgeCases.handling: That tile is drawn signed out and its name gains ', sign in again'; the others keep working. Nothing pops up until the person chooses it.

edgeCases.title: Offline
edgeCases.handling: Switching needs the network (sign-in, the new instance's data), so tiles other than the current one are disabled with the tooltip 'You're offline — switch when you're back online'. The current workspace keeps working from its cache.

edgeCases.title: Text at 130% on a phone
edgeCases.handling: Rows grow past 64pt; names and hosts truncate on one line each, and the sheet scrolls once it reaches 90% of the screen.

web.base: A <div role="menu"> that pops in (enter("pop")): each workspace an <a href> (role="menuitemradio") to its own origin with a square Avatar, then a 'Sign in to another workspace' <button role="menuitem">; inline styles over `t`, hover and focus from useInteraction. In the app it opens from the rail's workspace pill inside the menu primitive, which owns opening, Esc and arrow keys.
notes: DECISION: one workspace per tab, switched from a menu — not a tile column. Every workspace is its own instance at its own origin (<org>.antfabric.ai, ADR-5552), with its own session cookie, so a tab can only ever be signed into the workspace in its address bar.
Choosing a workspace navigates this tab there; ⌘-click or middle-click opens it in a new tab, which is how a person keeps two workspaces open in a browser.

No unread counts for other workspaces: the page cannot read another origin's session or counts, and BroadcastChannel is same-origin only. A badge that could only ever say 0 would be a lie, so rows carry names and addresses only.
No ⌘1–⌘9: in every browser those switch tabs. The list comes from this browser's history of sign-ins, kept on the account server once the account is linked, otherwise in localStorage.

keyboard.action: Moves between workspaces
Goes to that workspace in this tab
Opens that workspace in a new tab
Closes the menu

desktop.base: A role="list" column, the rail's 64px width: each tile a <button> (title tooltip, aria-current, aria-keyshortcuts) around a square Avatar with a Badge for mentions, the left bar for current / activity, and a Kbd under it while ⌘ is held; a dashed + <button> to add one. Inline styles over `t`, hover / press / focus from useInteraction, `current` kept by the component unless the app controls it. The app confirms a switch with its ConfirmDialog.
notes: Today (desktop-onboarding, ADR-5553): the rail's workspace pill opens a menu — 'Workspaces', every one this device has used with the current one ticked, then 'Sign in to another workspace'. The profile menu carries 'Switch workspace' for the collapsed rail.
This spec moves it to Slack's tile column, shown once two or more workspaces are signed in. With one, the rail keeps the pill.

⚠️ Only ONE workspace is signed in at a time today: session, shell snapshot, chat history, message cache and avatars are one slot each on the device. A switch is confirmed — 'Switch to Northwind Health?' / 'You'll be signed out of GeekyAnts on this device, then asked to sign in to Northwind Health.' — signs out, awaited, then reloads. Per-tile unread needs those stores keyed per origin (ADR-5553's follow-up); until then, other tiles show signed out with no count.
The Dock / taskbar badge sums every signed-in workspace; an OS notification names its workspace in the title.
Pressing a signed-in tile sets `current`: the ring moves to it and its left bar grows from 8 to 20px. A signed-out tile changes nothing here — it starts sign-in.

keyboard.action: Switches to the workspace in that position
Previous / next workspace
Moves between tiles when the column has focus

mobile.base: The sheet's panel as a View that slides up (<Enter motion="slide-up">, accessibilityViewIsModal): a grabber, the title, and a Pressable row per workspace with a square Avatar, Badge (count or neutral dot) and a tick that pops in; StyleSheet over useTheme(), fonts by file, press from usePress. In the app it sits in the sheet host opened by long-pressing the header photo, which owns the scrim and the drag to dismiss.
notes: The photo in the main header opens Settings on a tap (ADR-9419); a long-press, or 'Switch workspace' at the top of Settings, opens this sheet. With one workspace the sheet is never offered from the long-press.
Rows are 64pt with a 40pt tile; current is ticked, others carry their mention count once multi-sign-in exists.
Push notifications are per workspace: tapping one from a workspace you are not in switches to it first, with a 'Switched to Northwind Health' toast.
The sheet slides up; tapping a signed-in row sets `current` and the tick pops onto it.

gestures.action: Opens the sheet
Switches (with the confirm while one-at-a-time)
Dismisses

flows.title: Switch to Northwind Health
